क्रमवाचक संख्या: क्रम दर्शविणाऱ्या संख्या (जसे: पहिला, दुसरा, तिसरा, चौथा, पाचवा ...)
एकूण रक्कम: नोटे व नाण्यांचे मूल्य जोडून एकूण रक्कम काढतात.
जगजग: एकूण वस्तूची संख्या दर्शविणाऱ्या संख्या (मूल्यबाचक).
क्रमांक: क्रमातील स्थान दर्शविणाऱ्या संख्या (क्रमवाचक).
क्रमवाचक संख्या १ ते १०: पहिला, दुसरा, तिसरा, चौथा, पाचवा, सहावा, सातवा, आठवा, नववा, दहावी.
क्रमवाचक संख्या ११ ते २०: अकरावा, बारा, तेरवा, चौदा, पंधरा, सोलहा, सतरहा, अठरा, एकोनवीस, वीस.
जगजग व क्रमवाचक संख्या एकत्र वापरली जाते जसे: रस्तेवर गाडींचा क्रमांक, शाळेत विद्यार्थ्यांचा क्रमांक.
क्रमवाचक संख्यांची ओळख: पहिला, दुसरा, तिसरा, चौथा, पाचवा, सहावा, सातवा, आठवा, नववा, दहावी, अकरावा, बारा, तेरवा, चौदा, पंधरा, सोलहा, सतरहा, अठरा, एकोनवीस, वीस ...
क्रमवाचक संख्यांची तुलना: पहिला < दुसरा < तिसरा < चौथा < पाचवा ...

quiz.q: जगजग संख्या १५ चा क्रमवाचक रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: १५ चा क्रमवाचक रूप पंधरा आहे.

quiz.q: क्रमवाचक संख्या 'सातवा' चा जगजग रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: सातवा चा जगजग रूप ७ आहे.

quiz.q: एक नोटे ५०० रुपयांची आहे व दोन नाणी १० पैसे च्या आहेत. एकूण रक्कम किती?
जगजग संख्या २० चा क्रमवाचक रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: २० चा क्रमवाचक रूप वीसवा आहे.

quiz.q: क्रमवाचक संख्या 'पहिला' चा जगजग रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: पहिला चा जगजग रूप १ आहे.

quiz.q: तीन नोटे १०० रुपयांची व पाच नाणी ५० पैसे च्या आहेत. एकूण रक्कम किती?
जगजग संख्या १२ चा क्रमवाचक रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: १२ चा क्रमवाचक रूप बारा आहे.

quiz.q: क्रमवाचक संख्या 'दहावी' चा जगजग रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: दहावी चा जगजग रूप १० आहे.

quiz.q: चार नोटे ५० रुपयांची व तीन नाणी २० पैसे च्या आहेत. एकूण रक्कम किती?
जगजग संख्या १ चा क्रमवाचक रूप कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: १ चा क्रमवाचक रूप पहिला आहे.

subject: Maths
notes: वजाबाकी म्हणजे दोन संख्यांचा फरक शोधणे.
वजाबाकी करण्यासाठी मोठ्या संख्येपासून लहान संख्या वजा करतो.
वजाबाकी करणे 'minus' असे लिहितो.
वजाबाकी करण्यापूर्वी एकांक, दशक, शतक जागा पहाणे.
एकांक जागात वजा होत नाही तर दशक मोकळा करतो.
एक दशक मोकळा केल्यास तो १० एकक बनतो.
एक शतक मोकळा केल्यास तो १० दशक बनतो.
वजाबाकी करण्यासाठी प्रत्येक जागा स्वतंत्रपणे वजा करतो.
वजाबाकीचे उत्तर सध्या अंके होते.
वजाबाकी चेक करण्यासाठी वजा केलेली संख्या व उत्तर जोडलील, मोठ्या संख्ये मिळवली पाहिजे.
वजाबाकी शब्द problem लिहा, माहिती ओळखा, सोडवा, उत्तर लिहा.
वजाबाकी करणे दैनंदिन जीवनात वापरतो, जसे पैसे शिल्लक शोधणे.
वजाबाकीमध्ये उधार (borrow) घेणे आवश्यक पडतो.
वजाबाकी करण्यासाठी संख्ये खालीलपैली लिहावी.

quiz.explain: एकांक जागात ७ - ८ होत नाही, म्हणून दशक मोकळा केला. त्यामुळे १७ - ८ = ९, दशक ९ - ६ = ३, शतक ४ - २ = २.

quiz.q: सायलीकडे ५०० रुपये होते. तिने ३७५ रुपयांची पुस्तके घेतली. शिल्लक किती?
एक शाळेत ८३२ विद्यार्थी आहेत, त्यांपैकी ७४९ शैक्षणिक सहलीस गेले. सहलीस न गेलेले किती?
जॉनच्या वीज बिलचे ४६९ रुपये आले. त्याने ५०० रुपयीची नोट दिली. परत किती मिळतील?
आदर्श ग्रंथालयात मराठी, हिंदी, इंग्रजी पुस्तके एकत्र ८२०. हिंदी २५२, इंग्रजी २७९. मराठी किती?
आईजवळ ७०० रुपये होते. तिने साखर २४५ व चहा पावडर १२८ रुपयांची घेतली. शिल्लक किती?
एक दूध संकलन केंद्रात ६२४ लीटर दूध होते. ३४७ लीटर जमा झाले. ५१२ लीटर दिले. शिल्लक किती?
एंजलने १ डझन केळी आणली. अर्धा डझन मैत्रिणीला दिली. शिल्लक किती केळी?
quiz.explain: १ डझन = १२ केळी. अर्धा डझन = ६ केळी. शिल्लक = १२ - ६ = ६.

quiz.q: एक वर्षात १२ महिने. अर्ध्या वर्षात किती महिने?
तिसरीच्या एका वर्गात ३० विद्यार्थी. निम्म्या विद्यार्थ्यांनी धावण्याचा भाग घेतला. किती?

subject: Maths
notes: अपूर्णांक म्हणजे एक पूर्णांक से कम किंवा अधिक संख्या.
अपूर्णांक दोन भागे दर्शवते: अंश (रंगवलेला भाग) व छेद (एक पूर्णचे एकूण समान भाग).
अंश हा रंगवलेला भाग आहे, छेद हा एक पूर्णचे एकूण समान भाग आहे.
पाव म्हणजे १/२, पाऊण म्हणजे ३/४, अर्धा म्हणजे १/२.
पाव संख्यारूपात १/२ लिहितो, पाऊण ३/४ लिहितो.
एक पूर्णचे केलेले एकूण समान भाग छेद म्हणून ओळखले जाते.
रंगवलेले भाग अंश म्हणून ओळखले जाते.
अंश व छेद समान असल्यास एक पूर्ण होतो.
अंश छेदापेक्षा लहान असल्यास तो छेदाधिक अपूर्णांक असतो.
अंश छेदापेक्षा मोठा असल्यास तो अंशाधिक अपूर्णांक असतो.
एक पूर्णचे २ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/२ अंश होतो.
एक पूर्णचे ४ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/४ अंश होतो.
एक पूर्णचे ३ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/३ अंश होतो.
एक पूर्णचे ५ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/५ अंश होतो.
एक पूर्णचे ८ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/८ अंश होतो.

quiz.q: पाव संख्यारूपात कसा लिहावा?
quiz.explain: पाव म्हणजे एक पूर्णचे दोन समान भागात एक भाग, त्यामुळे १/२.

quiz.q: पाऊण संख्यारूपात कसा लिहावा?
quiz.explain: पाऊण म्हणजे एक पूर्णचे चार समान भागात तीन भाग, त्यामुळे ३/४.

quiz.q: अर्धा भाग संख्यारूपात कसा लिहावा?
quiz.explain: अर्धा म्हणजे पाव, जे १/२ आहे.

quiz.q: एक पूर्णचे ४ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग काय आहे?
quiz.explain: एक पूर्णचे ४ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/४ अंश होतो.

quiz.q: एक पूर्णचे ३ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग काय आहे?
quiz.explain: एक पूर्णचे ३ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/३ अंश होतो.

quiz.q: अंश व छेद समान असल्यास संख्या काय होते?
quiz.explain: अंश व छेद समान असल्यास एक पूर्ण होतो, जे १ आहे.

quiz.q: अंश १, छेद ४ असलेला अपूर्णांक काय आहे?
quiz.explain: अंश १, छेद ४ म्हणजे १/४.

quiz.q: अंश ३, छेद ४ असलेला अपूर्णांक काय आहे?
quiz.explain: अंश ३, छेद ४ म्हणजे ३/४.

quiz.q: अंश २, छेद ४ असलेला अपूर्णांक काय आहे?
एक पूर्णचे ८ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग काय आहे?
quiz.explain: एक पूर्णचे ८ समान भाग केल्यास प्रत्येक भाग १/८ अंश होतो.

subject: Maths
notes: लांबी मोजण्यासाठी मीटर, सेमीमीटर, पाव मीटर, अर्धा मीटर इत्यादी एकक वापरतात.
एक मीटर = 100 सेमीमीटर.
पाव मीटर = 50 सेमीमीटर.
अर्धा मीटर = 50 सेमीमीटर.
वस्तूची लांबी मोजताना तिच्या दोन टोके जोडून मोजली जाते.
दोरी जोडून लांबी वाढवली जाऊ शकते, जसे की दोन अर्धा मीटरची दोरी जोडून एक मीटर बनवली जाते.
वजन मोजण्यासाठी किलोग्राम, ग्राम इत्यादी एकक वापरतात.
एक किलोग्राम = 1000 ग्राम.
वजन तुलन्यासाठी तराजू वापरते, जिथे दोन पायरी समान होऊन वजन मोजला जातो.
जड वस्तू त्यांच्या वजनामुळे खालच्या दिशेने जातात, त्यामुळे तराजूतील पायरी खाली जाते.
वस्तूचे वजन अंदाजे लागवून, त्यानंतर प्रत्यक्ष मोजून खातरी केली जाते.
वस्तूचे वजन जास्त असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी खाली जाते.
वस्तूचे वजन कमी असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी वर राहते.
वजन मोजताना समान वजनाची वस्तू (जसे की गोट्या) वापरली जाते, जिथे समान संख्या होऊन वजन समान मोजला जातो.
वस्तूचे वजन मोजताना, तिचे वजन ज्ञात असलेली वस्तू (जसे की 1 किलोग्रामची पुडा) तुलनेसाठी वापरली जाते.

quiz.q: एक मीटर किती सेमीमीटर होते?
quiz.explain: एक मीटर = 100 सेमीमीटर.

quiz.q: पाव मीटर किती सेमीमीटर होते?
quiz.explain: पाव मीटर = अर्धा मीटर = 50 सेमीमीटर.

quiz.q: वस्तूची लांबी मोजताना दोन्ही टोके काय केली जातात?
quiz.explain: वस्तूची लांबी मोजताना दोन्ही टोके जुळवली जातात.

quiz.q: वजन मोजण्यासाठी तराजूतील दोन पायरी कधी समान होतात?
quiz.explain: तराजूतील दोन पायरी तेव्हा समान होत्या जेव्हा त्यामध्ये रखलेली वस्तूंचे वजन समान असते.

quiz.q: जड वस्तू तराजूतील पायरी कधी खाली जाते?
quiz.explain: जड वस्तू त्यांच्या वजनामुळे खालच्या दिशेने जातात, त्यामुळे तराजूतील पायरी खाली जाते.

quiz.q: एक किलोग्राम किती ग्राम होते?
quiz.explain: एक किलोग्राम = 1000 ग्राम.

quiz.q: वस्तूचे वजन अंदाजे लागवून, त्यानंतर काय केला जातो?
quiz.explain: वस्तूचे वजन अंदाजे लागवून, त्यानंतर प्रत्यक्ष मोजून खातरी केली जाते.

quiz.q: वस्तूचे वजन जास्त असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी काय होते?
quiz.explain: वस्तूचे वजन जास्त असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी खाली जाते.

quiz.q: वस्तूचे वजन कमी असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी काय राहते?
quiz.explain: वस्तूचे वजन कमी असल्यास तराजूतील तिच्या पायरी वर राहते.

quiz.q: वजन मोजताने समान वजनाची वस्तू जसे की गोट्या वापरली जातात, त्यामुळे काय होतो?
quiz.explain: समान वजनाची वस्तू (जसे की गोट्या) वापरून त्यांची समान संख्या होऊन वजन समान मोजला जातो.

subject: Maths
notes: माहिती म्हणजे गोळा केलेली तथ्ये आणि आकडे
तक्ते म्हणजे माहितीची व्यवस्थित मांडणी
तक्त्यांमध्ये स्तंभ आणि ओळी असतात
प्रत्येक स्तंभात एकच विषय असतो
प्रत्येक ओळीमध्ये एकच वस्तू किंवा व्यक्तीची माहिती असते
ताळ्याच्या खुणा म्हणजे तक्त्यातील रेषा
रेषा काढताना प्रत्येक ५ ओळींनंतर थोडी जागा सोडावी
सर्वाधिक मुलांनी कोणते फळ आणले हे तक्त्यातून कळते
सर्वात कमी मुलांनी कोणते फळ आणले हे कळते
समान, जास्त आणि कमी हे शब्द रिकाम्या जागेत भरण्यासाठी वापरले जातात
शाळेत येण्यासाठी वापरलेल्या वाहनांची संख्या तक्त्यातून कळते
सर्वाधिक आणि सर्वात कमी विद्यार्थ्यांनी कोणत्या वाहनाने शाळेत आले हे तक्त्यातून कळते
सायकल आणि पायी येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची तुलना तक्त्यातून करता येते
आंतरशालेय क्रीडा स्पर्धेतील खेळांमध्ये सर्वाधिक सहभाग कोणत्या खेळात आहे हे तक्त्यातून कळते
सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमातील विविध कलाप्रकारांची संख्या तक्त्यातून कळते
कपाटातील वस्तूंची स्थिती तक्त्याच्या मदतीने ओळखता येते
वस्तूंची समोरून, बाजूने आणि वरून दृश्ये वेगवेगळी असतात
माहितीचे व्यवस्थापन म्हणजे गोळा केलेली माहिती योग्य पद्धतीने सादर करणे
तक्ते व ताळ्याच्या खुणांचा वापर करून माहिती स्पष्टपणे दाखवता येते

quiz.q: तक्त्यातील रेषा काढताना प्रत्येक किती ओळींनंतर थोडी जागा सोडावी?
quiz.explain: ताळ्याच्या खुणा वापरताना प्रत्येक 5 ओळींनंतर थोडी जागा सोडावी.

quiz.q: सर्वाधिक मुलांनी कोणते फळ आणले?
quiz.explain: तक्त्यातून दिसते की चिकू सर्वाधिक मुलांनी आणले.

quiz.q: सर्वात कमी मुलांनी कोणते फळ आणले?
quiz.explain: तक्त्यातून दिसते की पेरू सर्वात कमी मुलांनी आणले.

quiz.q: सायकलने येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या पायी येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांपेक्षा किती जास्त/कमी आहे?
quiz.explain: सायकलने येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांची संख्या पायी येणाऱ्या विद्यार्थ्यांपेक्षा कमी आहे.

quiz.q: आंतरशालेय क्रीडा स्पर्धेत सर्वाधिक सहभाग कोणत्या खेळात होता?
quiz.explain: तक्त्यातून कळते की लांब उडीमध्ये सर्वाधिक मुलांनी सहभाग घेतला.

quiz.q: सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रमात किती कलाप्रकारांचे आयोजन करण्यात आले होते?
quiz.explain: सारणीतील कलाप्रकारांची संख्या 5 आहे.

quiz.q: कपाटाच्या वरच्या कप्प्यात कोणती वस्तू आहे?
quiz.explain: कपाटाच्या वरच्या कप्प्यात घड्याळ आहे.

quiz.q: वस्तूंची समोरून, बाजूने आणि वरून दृश्ये काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: ती दृश्ये वस्तूंची विविध दृष्टीकोन आहेत.

quiz.q: ताळ्याच्या खुणा वापरताना प्रत्येक 5 ओळींनंतर थोडी जागा सोडणे का महत्त्वाचे आहे?
quiz.explain: जागा सोडल्याने तक्ता वाचायला सोपा होतो.

quiz.q: माहितीचे व्यवस्थापन म्हणजे काय?
options: तक्ते व ताळ्याच्या खुणांचा वापर करून माहिती सादर करणे
quiz.explain: माहितीचे व्यवस्थापन म्हणजे गोळा केलेली माहिती व्यवस्थित सादर करणे.

subject: Maths
notes: नजरी नकाशा म्हणजे वस्तूंचा वाढून लहान आकारात चित्र.
नकाशेतील चिन्हे विशिष्ट वस्तू दर्शवतात (उदा. पेडे, घर, मार्ग).
नकाशेतील दिशा: समोर, डाव, उजवी, वर, खाली.
नकाशेतील मार्गे रंगून दर्शवता येतात.
जाळी (ग्रीड) स्तंभ व ओळीने बनेली होती.
स्तंभे अ, ब, क, ड; ओळी १, २, ३, ४ असे क्रमांकित.
वस्तूचे स्थान स्तंभ व ओळींच्या संयोजनाने दर्शविते (उदा. क-४).
नकाशेतील चिन्हे समजून घ्यावे.
नकाशेतील एक वस्तूच्या इतर वस्तूशी स्थिती सांगता येते.
नकाशा वाचून मार्ग, दूरी, दिशा शोधता येते.
नकाशेतील चिन्हे सांकेतिक हवे.
नकाशा बनवताना समानुपात लक्षात घ्यावे.
नकाशेतील चिन्हे खालीलपैकी असू शकतात: पेडे, घर, झोपे, टाकी, मार्ग.
नकाशा वाचून प्रश्नांची उत्तरे देथे शोधता येतात.

quiz.q: नजरी नकाशा म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: नजरी नकाशा म्हणजे वस्तूंचा वाढून लहान आकारात बनवला गेला चित्र.

quiz.q: नकाशेतील चिन्हे काय दर्शवतात?
quiz.explain: नकाशेतील प्रत्येक चिन्ह काही विशिष्ट वस्तू दर्शवतो जसे की पेडे, घर, मार्ग इ.

quiz.q: जाळी (ग्रीड)तील स्तंभांचे क्रमांक कसे होते?
quiz.explain: जाळीतील स्तंभे अ, ब, क, ड अक्षरांने क्रमांकित होती.

quiz.q: जाळीतील ओळींचे क्रमांक कसे होते?
quiz.explain: जाळीतील ओळी १, २, ३, ४ असे क्रमांकित होती.

quiz.q: क-४ म्हणजे काय दर्शवते?
quiz.explain: क-४ म्हणजे क स्तंभ व ४ ओळींचा संयोग, जिथे वस्तूचे स्थान दर्शविते.

quiz.q: नकाशेतील मार्ग कशी दर्शवता येते?
quiz.explain: नकाशेतील मार्गे रंगून दर्शवता येतात जेणेकरता स्पष्ट होईल.

quiz.q: नकाशेतील 'घसरगुंडी' काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: घसरगुंडी म्हणजे वाहनांचे तळ, जिथे वाहने चालवली जातात.

quiz.q: नकाशा वाचून आपण काय शोधू शकतो?
quiz.explain: नकाशा वाचून आपण मार्ग, दिशा, वस्तूंची एकमेकाशी स्थिती शोधू शकतो.

quiz.q: नकाशेतील चिन्हे कसे हवे?
quiz.explain: नकाशेतील चिन्हे सांकेतिक हवे, ज्यामुळे त्यांचे अर्थ स्पष्ट होईल.

quiz.q: जाळीतील ड-३ म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: ड-३ म्हणजे ड स्तंभ व ३ ओळींचा संयोग, जिथे वस्तूचे स्थान दर्शविते.

subject: Maths
notes: गुणाकार म्हणजे एक संख्येला इतर संख्येने बरोबर वेळा जोडणे.
गुणाकारात गुणले जाणारी संख्या 'गुणक' असे म्हणतात.
गुणले जाणारी संख्या 'गुण्य' असे म्हणतात.
गुणाकाराचा परिणाम 'गुणाकार' असे म्हणतात.
गुण्य × गुणक = गुणाकार.
कोणत्याही संख्येला १ गुणली तर त्याच गुणाकार तीच संख्या होते.
कोणत्याही संख्येला ० गुणली तर त्याच गुणाकार शून्य होते.
गुणाकार सारणी १ ते १० पर्यंतची याद करावी.
गुणाकारात क्रम बदलण्याने परिणाम बदलत नाही (समांतर गुणधर्म).
गुणाकार वितरणीय गुणधर्म दर्शवतो: a × (b + c) = (a × b) + (a × c).
दहा गुणली संख्या दशकस्थानातील अंक होते.
शेकडो गुणाकारचे परिणाम ओळखण्यासाठी पाढे वापरता येईल.
गुणाकारचे परिणाम अंदाज लगवून पुढे ठीक गणना केली जाऊ शकते.
गुणाकारचे परिणाम लिहिताना एकक व दशक स्थान योग्यपणे लिहावे.
गुणाकारचे परिणाम शोधण्यासाठी लॅटिस पद्धत वापरता येईल.

quiz.q: कोणती संख्या १ गुणली तिचा गुणाकार तीच संख्या होते?
quiz.explain: कोणतीही संख्या १ गुणली तिचा गुणाकार तीच संख्या होते.

quiz.q: कोणती संख्या ० गुणली तिचा गुणाकार शून्य होते?
quiz.explain: कोणतीही संख्या ० गुणली तिचा गुणाकार शून्य होते.

quiz.q: एक डब्यात ६ लाडू मावतात. ५ डब्यांमधील लाडूची संख्या किती?
एक पेनची किंमत ७ रुपये आहे. ९ पेनांची किंमत किती?
एक बॉक्समध्ये १० पेन्सिली आहेत. ७ बॉक्समधील पेन्सिलींची संख्या किती?
एक रांगेत २१ विद्यार्थी उभे आहेत. ३ रांगांतील एकूण विद्यार्थी किती?

subject: Maths
notes: भागाकार म्हणजे समान वाटणी किंवा समान गट करणे.
भागाकार म्हणजे एकाच संख्येला पुन्हा पुन्हा वजा करणे.
भाज्य: वाटण्यासाठी उपलब्ध एकूण वस्तूंची संख्या.
भाजक: प्रत्येक गटातील वस्तूंची संख्या किंवा वाटण्याची जणांची संख्या.
भागाकार: एकूण गटांची किंवा प्रत्येकाला मिळणारी वस्तूंची संख्या.
बाकी: भागाकार केल्यानंतर शिल्लक राहिल्या वस्तूंची संख्या.
भाज्य = भाजक × भागाकार + बाकी.
बाकी हमेशा भाजकापेक्षा लहान असते.
कोणतीही संख्या स्वतःला भागली तर भागाकार १ येतो.
शून्य ला कोणतीही संख्या भागली तर भागाकार ० येतो.
भागाकाराची उभी मांडणी सारणीद्वारे केली जाते.
समान वाटणीमध्ये प्रत्येकाला समान प्रमाण मिळतो.
समान गट करणे म्हणजे वस्तूंचे समान संख्येने गट बनवणे.
भागाकार करताना ५ चिन्ह (÷) वापरतो.
भागाकाराचे परिणाम अंतीच संख्या असते.

quiz.q: भागाकार २० ÷ ५ चा उत्तर काय आहे?
भाज्य १८, भाजक ३ असल्यास भागाकार काय होईल?
कोणतीही संख्या स्वतःला भागली तर भागाकार काय येतो?
quiz.explain: कोणतीही संख्या स्वतःला भागली तर भागाकार १ येतो, उदा. 7 ÷ 7 = 1.

quiz.q: शून्य ला ५ भागली तर भागाकार काय येतो?
quiz.explain: शून्य ला कोणतीही शून्येतर संख्या भागली तर भागाकार ० येतो.

quiz.q: भाज्य २५, भाजक ५, बाकी ० असल्यास भागाकार काय?
भागाकार ७, भाजक ४, बाकी २ असल्यास भाज्य काय?
१२ वस्तूंची ३ जणांमध्ये समान वाटणी केली तर प्रत्येकाला किती मिळतील?
quiz.explain: 12 ला 3 भागली तर 4 येतो, प्रत्येकाला ४ वस्तू मिळतात.

quiz.q: भाजक ६, भागाकार ९, बाकी ० असल्यास भाज्य काय?
२० फळे ५ मुलेसाठी समान वाटले तर प्रत्येक मULEला किती फळे मिळतात?
quiz.explain: 20 ला 5 भागली तर 4 येतो, प्रत्येक मULEला 4 फळे मिळतात.

quiz.q: भागाकार ०, भाजक ७, बाकी १५ असल्यास भाज्य काय?
quiz.explain: भागाकार ० असल्यास बाकी हमेशा ० हवी, त्यामुळे हा प्रश्न शक्य नाही.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Bunds are structures made of stones or soil to stop flowing water in rivers or streams.
Bunds are also built to store water in fields for farming.
Ponds and tanks onds and tanks on forts were built in old times to store water for people living there.
Old tanks (haud) were used to store water for drinking, farming, and construction.
Some old tanks (haud) are still in use today in certain places.
Baramotichi Vihir in Limb, Satara district is a historical well with stone construction and many steps.
It is an example of Shivkal architecture and attracts many tourists.
About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water, mostly in oceans and seas.
Very little of Earth's water is fresh and even less is potable (safe to drink).
If all Earth's water were in a barrel, fresh water would fill only a cup, and potable water just a drop.
Water is precious and essential for life; no living being can survive without it.
We must use water appropriately and avoid wasting even a single drop.
Activities like leaving taps open, overusing water in washing, etc., lead to water wastage.
We should use water sparingly, conserve it, and recycle it whenever possible.
Water stored for drinking or home use does not become stale if kept properly.

quiz.q: What are bunds made of?
quiz.explain: Bunds are built up of stones or soil to stop flowing water.

quiz.q: Where were ponds and tanks built in earlier times?
quiz.explain: Ponds and tanks were dug on forts for people living there.

quiz.q: What is an old tank (haud) used for?
quiz.explain: Old tanks (haud) store water used for drinking, farming, and construction.

quiz.q: What percentage of Earth's surface is covered by water?
quiz.explain: Approximately 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water.

quiz.q: If all Earth's water were in a barrel, how much would be fresh water?
quiz.explain: Fresh water would fill only a cup from the barrel of total water.

quiz.q: How much potable water is available from sources like rivers and wells in the barrel analogy?
quiz.explain: Available potable water would be just a single drop in the barrel analogy.

quiz.q: Why is water called 'Life'?
options: Because no living being can survive without it
quiz.explain: Water is called 'Life' because no living being can survive without it.

quiz.q: Which of the following helps in water conservation?
quiz.explain: Using water sparingly is a way to conserve water.

quiz.q: What should we do to prevent water wastage at home?
quiz.explain: Recycling water whenever possible helps prevent wastage.

quiz.q: Is it true that stored water for drinking becomes stale quickly?
options: Yes, it becomes stale in a day
No, it does not go stale if stored properly
quiz.explain: Water stored for drinking or home use does not go 'stale' if kept properly.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: A map is a proportional drawing of the earth or a part of it.
Maps use directions, conventional signs, symbols, projections, and scale.
Scale shows the ratio between distance on map and actual distance on ground.
Example of scale: 1 cm on map = 1 meter on ground (1 cm : 1 m).
Symbols represent features like post office (PO), spring (+), temple, mosque.
Index or legend explains the meaning of signs and symbols used on a map.
Direction arrows (North, South, East, West) help orient the map correctly.
Natural items on maps include rivers, mountains, coasts; man-made include roads, buildings.
Maharashtra has a coastline of 720 km along the Arabian Sea.
Maharashtra is divided into 6 administrative divisions: Nashik, Pune, Aurangabad, Amravati, Nagpur, Konkan.
Mumbai is the capital and Nagpur is the second capital of Maharashtra.
The Godavari is the longest river in Maharashtra, about 1465 km long.
The Sahyadri Mountains (Western Ghats) run north-south; Kalsubai is the highest peak.
The Konkan region is the coastal strip of Maharashtra.
Maps need a title, scale, direction, and index to be complete and useful.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of using a scale in map making?
options: To show actual distances in reduced form
quiz.explain: Scale helps represent real distances on ground in a smaller, proportional way on paper.

quiz.q: Which of the following is used to show a spring on a map?
quiz.explain: The symbol '+' is used to represent a spring on maps.

quiz.q: What does the index or legend on a map help us understand?
options: The meaning of signs and symbols
quiz.explain: The index explains what each sign or symbol on the map stands for.

quiz.q: Which direction is the Arabian Sea located relative to Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: The Arabian Sea lies to the west of Maharashtra state.

quiz.q: What is the longest river in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: The Godavari is the longest river in Maharashtra, with about 740 km flowing through the state.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a man-made feature commonly shown on maps?
quiz.explain: Roads are man-made structures, while mountains, rivers, and coasts are natural.

quiz.q: What is the capital of Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra; Nagpur is the second capital.

quiz.q: Which symbol is used to represent a post office on a map?
quiz.explain: PO is the conventional symbol used for Post Office on maps.

quiz.q: Why do maps need to be scaled?
options: To fit large areas on paper while keeping proportions
quiz.explain: Scaling allows large geographical areas to be represented accurately on a small sheet of paper.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a basic element of a map?
quiz.explain: Direction, scale, and symbols are essential; music is not related to map elements.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Maharashtra has five main forest types: Tropical Evergreen, Semi-evergreen, Deciduous, Thorny and Shrub, and Mangrove forests.
Tropical Evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri) and receive more than 3000 mm annual rainfall.
Semi-evergreen forests are found on the eastern and western slopes of the Sahyadri with rainfall between 1000 to 3000 mm.
Deciduous forests are found in Konkan, eastern low rainfall regions, Sahyadris, Satpura, plateau regions, and eastern part of the state with 600 to 1000 mm rainfall.
Thorny and Shrub forests are found in rain shadow regions with less than 600 mm rainfall; plants have small leaves and thorns to reduce water loss.
Mangrove forests are located in coastal intertidal and estuarine saline zones; examples include red and black mangroves.
Forest distribution depends on rainfall distribution, leading to diversity in forest types across the state.
National Parks and Sanctuaries are marked on the map; examples include Melghat and Tadoba-Andhari (implied from context).
Evergreen forests are found in districts like Thane, Raigad, Ratnagiri, Sindhudurg, and parts of Pune and Nashik (Western Ghats).
Major minerals in Maharashtra include manganese, iron ore, bauxite, limestone, chromite, dolomite, silica, and coal.
Manganese is found in Nagpur, Gondia, Bhandara, Sindhudurg and used in iron and steel industry.
Iron ore is found in Chandrapur, Bhandara, Gadchiroli, Nagpur, Gondia, Sindhudurg and used to produce pure iron and steel.
Bauxite is found in Sindhudurg, Ratnagiri, Kolhapur, Raigad and used for aluminum production.
Limestone is found in Gadchiroli, Yavatmal, Chandrapur, Nagpur, Pune, Ahilyanagar and used in chemical and cement industries.
Major food crops: rice (paddy) in high rainfall areas, jowar, bajra, maize, and pulses in low rainfall areas.
Kharif season is the monsoon farming season; Rabi season is the winter farming season.
State bird: Hariyal (green pigeon); State animal: Shekru (Indian giant squirrel).
Major festivals: August 15 (Independence Day) and January 26 (Republic Day) are national festivals celebrated with enthusiasm.
Musical instruments used in festivals: dhol, tasha, peti (harmonium), tabla, sambal, sanai (clarinet), taal, mrudung, halgi, tarpa.

quiz.q: Which type of forest is found in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra and receives more than 3000 mm of annual rainfall?
quiz.explain: Tropical Evergreen forests are found in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri) and receive more than 3000 mm annual rainfall, as stated in the textbook.

quiz.q: On which date is 'Maharashtra Day' celebrated?
quiz.explain: Maharashtra Day is celebrated on 1 May every year to commemorate the formation of the state.

quiz.q: Which is the longest river in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: The Godavari river is the longest river in Maharashtra, as indicated in the textbook exercise.

quiz.q: Sugarcane and cotton are classified as which type of crops in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Sugarcane and cotton are major commercial crops grown for sale and industry, not just for food.

quiz.q: Which plateau is Maharashtra a part of?
quiz.explain: Maharashtra is part of the Deccan Plateau, which covers large parts of southern and central India.

quiz.q: Which mountain range is located to the west of Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: The Sahyadri range, also known as the Western Ghats, runs along the western border of Maharashtra.

quiz.q: What is the major food grain crop grown in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Rice (paddy) is the major food grain crop in Maharashtra, especially in high rainfall areas like Konkan and eastern Vidarbha.

quiz.q: How many administrative divisions are there in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Maharashtra has 6 administrative divisions: Amravati, Aurangabad, Konkan, Nagpur, Nashik, and Pune.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a reason for diversity in forests of Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Forests vary due to rainfall, soil, and altitude; temperature is not uniform and does not cause uniformity in forests.

quiz.q: What is the main difference between evergreen and thorny forests in Maharashtra?
options: Evergreen forests have trees that shed leaves annually; thorny forests remain green all year.
Evergreen forests are found in low rainfall areas; thorny forests in high rainfall areas.
Evergreen forests have dense trees that remain green throughout the year; thorny forests have small leaves and thorns to reduce water loss.
Evergreen forests are found only in coastal areas; thorny forests in mountainous regions.
quiz.explain: Evergreen forests retain leaves year-round and are found in high rainfall areas; thorny forests have adaptations like small leaves and thorns for dry, low rainfall regions.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Public life includes facilities like roads, electricity, water, transport, communication, education, health, and jobs.
Urban areas have better facilities such as roads, electricity, water supply, transport, and communication compared to rural areas.
Rural areas have limited facilities but offer a natural and pollution-free environment.
Transport is the movement of people and goods from one place to another.
Geographical factors like mountains, plateaus, plains, coasts, deserts, and snowy regions affect the choice of transport.
In mountainous regions, only road transport is used due to steep slopes.
In plateaus and plains, road and rail transport are common due to flat terrain.
In coastal areas, water transport is used via sea and large river channels.
Air transport connects large cities and requires airports and runways.
In deserts and snowy regions, animals are used for transport.
Modern highways like Mumbai-Pune Expressway, Atal Setu Sea Link, and Solapur-Vijayapura Highway have improved travel.
Modern transport reduces travel time due to better infrastructure and faster vehicles.
Fuels used in transport include petrol, diesel, CNG, electricity, and solar energy.
Communication is obtaining and sharing information with others.
Traditional means of communication: post, newspaper, telephone, television, radio.
Modern means of communication: mobile phones, Internet, e-mail, computers, artificial satellites.
Mobile phones are widely used today for communication in agriculture, industry, trade, transport, education, and IT.
A traffic garden is a place with models of signals, roads, and signs to teach children traffic rules through play.
Following traffic rules reduces accidents and increases safety for everyone.
Safety rules: wear helmet on two-wheelers, avoid mobile phone use while driving, use internet for work, promote harmony through messaging.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a facility commonly found in urban areas?
quiz.explain: Urban areas have better electricity supply, not limited.

quiz.q: In which geographical region is animal transport commonly used?
quiz.explain: Animals are used for transport in deserts and snowy regions due to lack of vehicle access.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a traffic garden?
options: To teach traffic rules through play
quiz.explain: A traffic garden uses models of roads and signs to teach children traffic safety while playing.

quiz.q: Which of these is a modern means of communication?
quiz.explain: E-mail is a modern electronic means of communication, unlike traditional tools.

quiz.q: Which transport is most common in plains and plateaus?
quiz.explain: Flat terrain in plains and plateaus supports road and rail transport.

quiz.q: What has reduced travel time in recent years?
quiz.explain: Highways like Mumbai-Pune Expressway and Atal Setu Sea Link have made travel faster.

quiz.q: Which fuel is NOT typically used in transport?
quiz.explain: Coal is used in homes for cooking, not commonly in vehicles.

quiz.q: What is messaging mainly used for in society?
quiz.explain: Messaging helps people stay connected and promotes harmony in society.

quiz.q: Which statement is true about rural areas?
options: They have more hospitals than cities
They have better malls than urban areas
People depend on agriculture and small industries
quiz.explain: Rural areas rely on agriculture and small-scale industries for employment.

quiz.q: Which of these is a traditional means of communication?
quiz.explain: Television is a traditional electronic medium, though now also modern in form.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Energy is the capacity to do any work.
We get energy from food to do activities like playing, running, and speaking.
Solar energy comes from the sun and is used in solar cookers, solar water heaters, and solar lamps.
Wind energy is obtained from wind and used to generate electricity via windmills.
Light energy travels in a straight line.
Light cannot pass through opaque objects, which results in the formation of a shadow.
Shadows are formed when an opaque object blocks the path of light.
On Zero Shadow Day, the sun is exactly overhead and shadows disappear at noon.
Magnetism is the property of a magnet to attract iron objects.
Substances attracted to a magnet are magnetic; those not attracted are non-magnetic.
Uses of magnetism include loudspeakers, electric motors, door latches, handbag locks, toy compasses, geometry boxes, and fridge stickers.
National Energy Conservation Day is observed on December 14th to promote efficient energy use.
To save energy, switch off lights and fans when not needed.
Energy sources include the sun, wind, water, and fuel.
Appliances that run on solar energy help conserve non-renewable resources.

quiz.q: What is energy defined as in the chapter?
options: The capacity to do any work
quiz.explain: Energy is defined as the capacity to do any work.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a form of energy mentioned in the chapter?
quiz.explain: Gravitational energy is not discussed in the chapter; solar, wind, and sound energy are.

quiz.q: What happens when an opaque object blocks light?
quiz.explain: When light is blocked by an opaque object, a shadow is formed.

quiz.q: From where is solar energy obtained?
quiz.explain: Solar energy is obtained from the sun.

quiz.q: Which appliance uses wind energy to generate electricity?
quiz.explain: Windmills use wind energy to generate electricity.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a magnetic substance?
quiz.explain: Iron is attracted to a magnet and is a magnetic substance.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of National Energy Conservation Day?
options: To celebrate the invention of electricity
To promote the use of fossil fuels
To create awareness about energy conservation
To encourage more use of lights
quiz.explain: The day aims to create public awareness about efficient use of energy.

quiz.q: In which month does Zero Shadow Day usually occur in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: In Maharashtra, Zero Shadow Day usually occurs in the month of May.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a use of magnetism?
quiz.explain: Magnets are used in door latches to keep them closed.

quiz.q: What should be done to save energy at home?
options: Switch off lights and fans when not needed
quiz.explain: Switching off lights and fans when not needed helps save energy.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Our body has external organs (outside) like hands, legs, eyes, ears, nose, skin, tongue.
Our body has internal organs (inside) like brain, heart, lungs, liver, stomach, intestines.
External organs help us interact with the surroundings; internal organs work inside the body.
Hands and legs are motor organs (Karmendriya) used for movement and work.
Eyes, ears, nose, skin, and tongue are sensory organs that help us sense the world.
The brain is inside the skull, processes information, and controls emotions and actions.
The heart pumps blood throughout the body and is slightly left of the chest centre.
Lungs supply oxygen to the body and work with the heart to purify blood.
The stomach churns food with help from the liver; digestion starts here.
The small intestine absorbs nutrients and water from food into the blood.
The large intestine absorbs water from waste and stores feces before expulsion.
The rectum stores feces temporarily; the anus expels waste from the body.
Oesophagus is the food pipe connecting mouth to stomach.
Internal organs perform specific functions like digestion, circulation, respiration, and excretion.
We must take care of our body by eating well, exercising, and keeping clean.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an external organ?
quiz.explain: Skin is an external organ as it covers the outside of the body.

quiz.q: What is the main function of the heart?
quiz.explain: The heart works like a pump to circulate blood throughout the body.

quiz.q: Which organs help us sense our surroundings?
quiz.explain: Eyes, ears, nose, skin, and tongue are sensory organs that detect surroundings.

quiz.q: Where is the brain located in the body?
quiz.explain: The brain is located inside the skull, which protects it.

quiz.q: What happens in the small intestine?
quiz.explain: In the small intestine, nutrients and water from food are absorbed into the blood.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT an internal organ?
quiz.explain: Tongue is an external organ as it is visible outside the body.

quiz.q: What is the function of the lungs?
quiz.explain: Lungs supply oxygen to the entire body, which is needed to purify blood.

quiz.q: Which organ stores feces temporarily before expulsion?
quiz.explain: The rectum is the last part of the large intestine where feces are stored for a while.

quiz.q: Hands and legs are called motor organs because they help in:
quiz.explain: Hands and legs are motor organs (Karmendriya) used to perform daily tasks like walking and picking up objects.

quiz.q: Which statement is true about internal organs?
options: They perform functions like digestion and circulation
quiz.explain: Internal organs are inside the body and perform functions like digestion, circulation, respiration, and excretion.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Stars are self-luminous objects that sparkle in the sky.
Planets do not have their own light and reflect sunlight.
The Sun is a star and the center of the solar system.
Earth is a planet that revolves around the Sun and rotates on its axis.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.
There are eight planets in the solar system: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.
Venus is the second planet from the Sun.
Earth is the third planet and has life.
Mars is the fourth planet, known as the red planet.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
Saturn has prominent rings around it.
Uranus rotates on its side with an axial tilt of about 98°.
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.
Asteroids are small rocky bodies found mainly between Mars and Jupiter.
Dwarf planets, like Pluto, orbit the Sun but are not full planets.
Comets are icy bodies that develop tails when near the Sun.
One Astronomical Unit (AU) is the average Earth-Sun distance: ~149 million km.
Inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars) are rocky and lie inside the asteroid belt.
Outer planets (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) are large and gaseous.
Earth's rotation causes day and night; one rotation takes about 24 hours (a day).
Earth's revolution around the Sun causes a year; one revolution takes about 365 days.
The Moon's phases change due to its changing position relative to Earth and Sun.
Phases include new moon, crescent, quarter, gibbous, and full moon.
Waxing moon: illuminated part increases (Shukla Paksha).

quiz.q: Which of the following is a star?
quiz.explain: The Sun is a star because it produces its own light and heat through nuclear fusion.

quiz.q: What is the correct sequence of planets from the Sun?
options: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Earth, Venus, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Uranus, Saturn, Neptune
quiz.explain: The correct order of planets from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

quiz.q: What causes day and night on Earth?
quiz.explain: Day and night occur due to Earth's rotation on its axis; one full rotation takes about 24 hours.

quiz.q: Which planet is known for having rings?
quiz.explain: Saturn is known for its prominent ring system made of ice and rock particles.

quiz.q: What is a satellite?
options: A star that orbits a planet
A planet that orbits the Sun
A heavenly body that orbits a planet
A comet that orbits the Sun
quiz.explain: A satellite is a heavenly body that revolves around a planet; the Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

quiz.q: Which are the inner planets of the solar system?
quiz.explain: Inner planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars; they are rocky and lie inside the asteroid belt.

quiz.q: What causes the phases of the Moon?
options: Moon's changing position relative to Earth and Sun
quiz.explain: The phases of the Moon occur because we see different amounts of its sunlit side as it orbits Earth.

quiz.q: How long does Earth take to complete one revolution around the Sun?
quiz.explain: Earth takes approximately 365 days to complete one orbit around the Sun, which defines a year.

quiz.q: What is the average distance of Earth from the Sun in kilometers?
quiz.explain: The average Earth-Sun distance is 149 million kilometers, also known as one Astronomical Unit (AU).

quiz.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
quiz.explain: Neptune is the eighth and farthest planet from the Sun in our solar system.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Plants are classified as trees, shrubs, herbs, or climbers based on height and stem type.
Trees grow tall with hard stems; shrubs are shorter with hard stems; herbs are short with soft stems; climbers need support.
A flower bud develops into a flower, which after fertilization becomes a fruit containing seeds.
Seeds germinate in soil, producing a sprout and root, then grow into a seedling and eventually a mature plant.
Autotrophic plants make their own food via photosynthesis; heterotrophic plants depend on others for food.
Insectivorous plants trap and digest insects to obtain nutrients.
Simple leaves have a single blade attached to the stem; compound leaves have multiple leaflets.
Taproot is a thick main root with smaller branches; fibrous roots are many thin roots from the stem base.
Roots absorb water and nutrients from soil and anchor the plant.
Leaves are the main site of photosynthesis, where food is made using sunlight, air, water, and nutrients.
Plants provide food, clothing, shelter, shade, and medicine to humans and animals.
Medicinal plants like Neem, Tulsi, Aloe Vera, and Basil are used in traditional healing.
Plants have varying lifespans: some live months (e.g., wheat), others years (e.g., mango), and some like banyan live for centuries.
Seed balls are a method to grow plants by mixing seeds with soil and dung, then scattering after rain.
We should protect plants by planting trees, avoiding harm, and conserving green spaces.

quiz.q: What are plants that grow tall and have a hard stem called?
quiz.explain: Trees are tall plants with hard, woody stems.

quiz.q: What are plants called that grow on other plants and absorb some food from them?
quiz.explain: Such plants are heterotrophic as they depend on host plants for food.

quiz.q: What is the use of the colour and fragrance of flowers to the plant?
quiz.explain: Colour and fragrance attract insects for pollination.

quiz.q: What does a floral bud transform into?
quiz.explain: A floral bud develops into a flower.

quiz.q: By which process do plants prepare food?
quiz.explain: Plants make food through photosynthesis in leaves using sunlight.

quiz.q: What is the main function of roots?
quiz.explain: Roots absorb water and minerals from soil and anchor the plant.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of a simple leaf?
quiz.explain: Mango leaf is simple; tamarind, gulmohar, and neem have compound leaves.

quiz.q: Which plants have fibrous roots?
quiz.explain: Wheat has fibrous roots; mango and peepal have taproots; banyan has both.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an insectivorous plant?
quiz.explain: Pitcher plant traps and digests insects for nutrition.

quiz.q: What is the product of photosynthesis in plants?
quiz.explain: Photosynthesis produces glucose (stored as starch) and releases oxygen.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Seasons change due to Earth's revolution around the Sun and the tilt of its axis (23°30').
When the North Pole tilts toward the Sun, the Northern Hemisphere experiences summer; the Southern Hemisphere experiences winter.
The three major seasons in India are summer, monsoon, and winter.
Summer is hot; we wear cotton clothes, drink more water and cold drinks, and eat fruits like mango and watermelon.
Monsoon (June–September) brings rain; farmers sow crops, and we use umbrellas and raincoats.
Winter is cold; we wear warm clothes, eat dry fruits and fruits like guava, and enjoy Diwali holidays.
Seasonal changes affect human health: fatigue, body aches, and changes in appetite.
Our diet and clothing change with the seasons to stay healthy and comfortable.
Birds migrate seasonally; many come to India in winter for food and breeding.
Tree plantation week is celebrated from July 1 to 7 after monsoon onset.
Farmers plough, sow, harvest, thresh, and winnow grains; then grains are stored, sold, and made into flour for bread.
Food should not be wasted because it is the result of farmers' hard work.
Food grains like rice, wheat, jowar, and pulses are used differently across regions (Konkan, Vidarbha, etc.).
Seasonal winds cause rain in India; moisture-laden winds from oceans lead to rainfall.
High and low pressure areas due to temperature differences generate winds that bring rain.

quiz.q: What causes the change of seasons on Earth?
options: Earth's revolution around the Sun and tilt of its axis
quiz.explain: Seasons change due to Earth's revolution around the Sun and the tilt of its axis (23°30'), which causes different parts of Earth to receive varying sunlight throughout the year.

quiz.q: In which season do farmers in India usually start sowing crops?
quiz.explain: Farmers start sowing crops during the monsoon season (June–September) when rains begin and the soil is moist.

quiz.q: Which of the following fruits is commonly eaten in summer?
quiz.explain: Mango is a summer fruit abundantly available in markets during hot weather.

quiz.q: What do we wear in winter to protect ourselves from cold?
quiz.explain: In winter, we wear warm clothes to protect ourselves from the cold air.

quiz.q: By how many degrees is the Earth's axis tilted?
quiz.explain: The Earth's axis is tilted at 23°30', which is responsible for the changing seasons.

quiz.q: Which season is experienced in the Southern Hemisphere when it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere?
quiz.explain: When the North Pole faces the Sun (summer in Northern Hemisphere), the South Pole is tilted away, causing winter in the Southern Hemisphere.

quiz.q: What is the main reason for rain in India during monsoon?
options: Seasonal winds carrying moisture from the ocean
quiz.explain: Monsoon rains in India are caused by seasonal winds that blow from the ocean, carrying moisture which leads to rainfall.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a seasonal change in human lifestyle?
quiz.explain: While clothing, diet, and daily routines change with seasons, the language spoken does not change seasonally.

quiz.q: Why should we not waste food?
options: It is the result of farmers' hard work
quiz.explain: Food should not be wasted because it is produced with the hard work of farmers, and wasting it disrespects their effort.

quiz.q: During which festival do we often eat sweets made from grains and enjoy holidays in winter?
quiz.explain: Diwali is celebrated in winter, and we enjoy holidays and eat sweets made from grains and other ingredients during this time.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Agriculture depends on rainwater and varies with rainfall levels.
High rainfall areas grow rice, nachani, varai, coconut.
Moderate rainfall areas grow wheat, tur, soybean.
Low rainfall areas grow jowar, bajra, moong, matki.
Good crops need improved seeds, fertile land, sunlight, and water.
Food grains and vegetables vary with seasons in India.
Farmers prepare land, sow, harvest, thresh, winnow, pack, and transport grains.
Organic farming uses natural fertilizers like dung, compost, and avoids chemicals.
Food preparation methods include roasting, boiling, steaming, frying, etc.
Cooking makes food soft, tasty, and easy to digest; some foods are eaten raw.
Food preservation includes sun drying, storing in ventilated areas, using neem leaves.
Proper storage prevents insect and fungus damage.
Contaminated food is spoiled by microbes, chemicals, or unclean handling.
Effects of contaminated food: stomach ache, diarrhea, vomiting, exhaustion.
Prevent contamination by covering food, using clean water, eating fresh food.
Shelter protects from heat, wind, rain, and danger; animals and humans need it.
Rural houses use mud, bamboo, grass; urban houses use cement, steel, bricks.
Eco-friendly homes use natural materials, renewable energy, recycle water and waste.
Birds build nests to protect eggs and chicks from predators and weather.
Grains like wheat, rice, jowar are preserved year-round for food security.

quiz.q: Which crop is mainly grown in high rainfall areas?
quiz.explain: Rice requires high rainfall and is grown in regions like Konkan.

quiz.q: What is the first work a farmer does in the field?
quiz.explain: Farm preparation (like ploughing) is the first step before sowing.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a method of food preparation?
quiz.explain: Painting is not a food preparation method; others are common cooking techniques.

quiz.q: What is organic farming?
options: Using natural fertilizers and avoiding chemicals
quiz.explain: Organic farming uses natural inputs like dung and compost and avoids synthetic chemicals.

quiz.q: Which of these foods is often eaten raw?
quiz.explain: Cucumber is commonly eaten raw in salads; others are usually cooked.

quiz.q: Why are grains dried in the sun before storage?
options: To remove moisture and prevent spoilage
quiz.explain: Drying reduces moisture, preventing mold and insect growth during storage.

quiz.q: Which material is commonly used in rural house construction in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Rural houses use locally available natural materials like mud, bamboo, and grass.

quiz.q: What is a key feature of eco-friendly homes?
options: Extensive use of non-conventional energy like solar
quiz.explain: Eco-friendly homes use renewable energy sources such as solar and wind energy.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an effect of eating contaminated food?
quiz.explain: Contaminated food can cause gastrointestinal issues like diarrhea and vomiting.

quiz.q: Which season sees the fastest spoilage of food?
quiz.explain: High temperatures in summer promote microbial growth, causing food to spoil quickly.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: A disaster is a sudden calamity causing immense damage and loss.
Natural disasters include floods, earthquakes, droughts, storms, hailstorms, heavy rainfall, and landslides.
Man-made disasters result from human errors and greed, such as fire, accidents, war, and pollution.
Drought is a water shortage due to insufficient rainfall, leading to problems for people, animals, and agriculture.
Causes of drought: lack of rain, deforestation, concretization preventing water percolation, and wastage of water.
Effects of drought: water scarcity affecting humans, animals, and crops.
Solutions to overcome drought: building lakes, bunds, dams; using drip and sprinkler irrigation; rainwater harvesting; planting trees; growing low-water crops.
During a cyclone at sea, winds blow at very high speed, causing heavy rainfall and high waves.
To stay safe during a cyclone: listen to weather department messages, stay in a safe place, avoid unnecessary travel.
Excessive rain causes rivers and streams to overflow, leading to floods and damage to houses, crops, trees, and animals.
To reduce damage from excessive rain: move to safe or high ground with animals.
Safety symbols help identify dangers; draw and understand symbols seen in daily life.
A life-saving bag should contain essentials like water bottle, dry snacks, torch, and regular medicines for emergencies.
National Disaster Management Day is observed on October 13th every year since 1989 to guide on emergency protection.
Home disasters can occur due to mistakes: short circuit, gas leakage, mobile explosion, improper use of electric heater.
Precautions in kitchen: never play near gas stove when in use; turn off stove and regulator when not in use.
Do not play with fire hazards like candles, lighters, or matchsticks.
Handle electrical appliances safely: do not touch broken wires or damaged switches; never touch appliances with wet hands; adults should use rubber gloves and slippers while repairing.
Stay away from dangerous chemicals like medicines, pesticides, or cleaning agents; wash hands thoroughly if touched accidentally.
Care at heights: walk slowly on stairs, hold railing for support, avoid leaning out of windows or off balconies, and do not go to terrace alone.
Use elevator only with an adult.
Self-safety is the first responsibility; shout for help or use hand signals or write 'SOS!' if approached by strangers.
Emergency numbers: Police - 100, Fire Brigade - 101, Ambulance - 108/102, Women & Child Care - 181, Child Helpline - 1098, Disaster Management Cell - 1077.
Protect environment by planting trees, saving water, reducing waste; treat environment as part of family.
Help visually impaired by acting as a 'Vision-Friend': guide with instructions, avoid obstacles, ensure safe movement.

quiz.q: What is the most important identity of a disaster?
options: It happens in a limited space.
It occurs suddenly and causes immense damage.
quiz.explain: A disaster is defined as a sudden calamity causing immense damage, which matches option 4.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a natural disaster?
quiz.explain: Earthquake occurs naturally without human intervention, making it a natural disaster.

quiz.q: What should you do if an unknown person offers you snacks?
options: Say 'No' immediately and leave the place.
quiz.explain: For self-safety, one must refuse and leave immediately when approached by strangers offering objects.

quiz.q: Which activity is safe during lightning?
quiz.explain: Staying inside a concrete building protects from lightning strikes; the other options are dangerous.

quiz.q: Why should we avoid using plastic?
options: It pollutes the environment and can spread diseases.
It is not available in markets.
quiz.explain: Plastic pollution harms the environment and can lead to diseases, making option 3 correct.

quiz.q: What is a man-made disaster?
options: A disaster caused by heavy rainfall.
A disaster caused by human errors and greed damaging nature.
A disaster that occurs without any cause.
quiz.explain: Man-made disasters result from human actions like negligence or greed, such as fire, accidents, war, and pollution.

quiz.q: Which of the following helps overcome drought?
quiz.explain: Building lakes, bunds, and dams stores water, which helps overcome drought.

quiz.q: What should you do if someone tries to pull you by force?
options: Shout loudly, struggle, and run to a crowded place.
quiz.explain: One should shout for help, resist, and escape to a safe place like a crowded area or police station.

quiz.q: Which precaution is correct for using electrical appliances?
options: Touch switches with wet hands for better grip.
Never touch broken wires or damaged switches.
Use metal ladders while fixing electrical points.
quiz.explain: For safety, one must avoid touching broken electrical wires or damaged switches to prevent electric shock.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a life-saving bag?
options: To store extra clothes for travel.
To keep essential items for emergencies like water, snacks, torch, and medicines.
To use as a pillow during travel.
quiz.explain: A life-saving bag contains essentials such as water

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: Wet waste includes vegetable stalks, fruit peels, dry leaves, eggshells, and spoiled food that rot and decompose.
Dry waste includes plastic, metal, glass, nails, and other materials that do not rot and remain unchanged for years.
A green dustbin is used for wet waste; a blue dustbin is used for dry waste.
Compost fertilizer is made by decomposing wet waste in a pit or container with soil and water over 4–6 weeks.
The 3R principle stands for Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle to minimize waste and protect the environment.
Reduce means using fewer resources, like steel cups instead of plastic or cloth bags instead of tissue paper.
Reuse means using old items again, such as blank paper for rough work or toys in ice cream boxes.
Recycle means making new products from dry waste, like new paper from old newspapers or plastic from bottles.
Improper garbage disposal leads to foul smell, disease spread by houseflies, and health hazards.
Keeping surroundings clean is everyone’s responsibility; garbage must be segregated before disposal.
Farmers use cow dung manure from animal waste to enrich soil for healthy crop growth.
Drawing on walls, wasting water, and littering are bad habits; using dustbins properly is a good habit.
Wet waste from homes and schools can be turned into compost for school gardens.
Dry waste like plastic and paper is sent to factories to be recycled into new products.
Always throw garbage in the correct dustbin to maintain cleanliness and beauty of surroundings.

quiz.q: Which color dustbin is used for wet waste?
quiz.explain: A green dustbin is used to store wet waste as mentioned in the textbook.

quiz.q: What is compost fertilizer made from?
quiz.explain: Compost fertilizer is formed by decomposing wet waste such as food scraps and plant material.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of dry waste?
quiz.explain: Plastic bags do not rot and remain unchanged for years, making them dry waste.

quiz.q: What does the 'R' in 'Reduce' of the 3R principle mean?
quiz.explain: Reduce means using products that generate less waste, like steel cups instead of disposable ones.

quiz.q: Which activity is part of 'Reuse'?
options: Using blank notebook pages for rough work
quiz.explain: Using blank paper from notebooks for rough work is reusing old material.

quiz.q: What happens if garbage is left lying around?
options: It smells bad and spreads disease
quiz.explain: Garbage causes foul smell and houseflies spread germs, leading to diseases.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a good habit for cleanliness?
quiz.explain: Scribbling or drawing on walls, tables, or chairs is a bad habit as per the textbook.

quiz.q: What is made from decomposing wet waste in a pit over 4–6 weeks?
quiz.explain: Wet waste rots in a pit with soil and water to form compost fertilizer after 4–6 weeks.

quiz.q: Which statement about 3R is correct?
options: Recycle means using old things again
Reuse means making new things from waste
Following 3R keeps surroundings clean and safe
quiz.explain: By following Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, waste is reduced and surroundings remain clean and safe for plants and animals.

quiz.q: What should you do with leftover food from your tiffin?
quiz.explain: Leftover food should be thrown into the green dustbin only, as it is wet waste.

subject: EVS Part 1
chapter: In the Wonderful World of Animals
notes: Birds have beaks, legs, wings, and feathers, but their food, habitats, and flying styles differ.
Kingfisher is larger than a sparrow and smaller than a crow, with a long thick reddish-pink beak, brown head, white neck, blue back, reddish-pink feet, and short legs.
Insects help in decomposition, pollination, and serve as food for birds and animals.
Oviparous animals hatch from eggs (e.g., birds, insects, reptiles); viviparous animals give birth to young ones (e.g., humans, cows).
Many insects undergo a life cycle: egg → larva → pupa → adult (e.g., butterfly, firefly).
Food chain shows how living things depend on each other for food (e.g., plants → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle).
Some animals blend with surroundings using colour and shape for protection (camouflage).
Lifespan varies: butterfly (1–2 weeks), housefly (15–25 days), sparrow (3–5 years), elephant (60–70 years), human (80–100 years).
Diurnal animals are active during the day (e.g., cows, deer); nocturnal animals are active at night (e.g., owls, bats, foxes).
Animals live in groups (herds, flocks, hives) for food, protection, and caring young; some live alone.
Never touch birds, eggs, nests, or insects; use only fallen specimens for collection.
Lac insect produces lac used in bangles, jewelry, and sealing documents.
Silkworms give silk, honeybees give honey and wax, beetles help in decomposition.
State Bird of Maharashtra: Hariyal; State Butterfly: Blue Mormon; State Animal: Shekru; State Fish: Silver Pomfret.
Plants prepare food using sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients; herbivores eat plants; carnivores eat animals.

quiz.q: What is the beak colour of a Kingfisher as observed in the text?
quiz.explain: The text states the Kingfisher's beak colour is reddish-pink.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of a viviparous animal?
quiz.explain: Humans give birth to young ones, making them viviparous.

quiz.q: What do grasshoppers, honeybees, and termites have in common based on the text?
quiz.explain: The text classifies them as herbivores in the fill-in-the-blank exercise.

quiz.q: Which insect is known for producing lac used in bangles and sealing documents?
quiz.explain: The lac insect produces lac, used for bangles, jewelry, and sealing documents.

quiz.q: What is the correct sequence in a food chain involving a caterpillar, frog, snake, and eagle?
quiz.explain: The text states: caterpillar eats leaves, frog eats caterpillar, snake eats frog, eagle eats snake.

quiz.q: Which of these animals is nocturnal?
quiz.explain: Owls are active at night, making them nocturnal, as mentioned in the text.

quiz.q: What is the lifespan of a housefly according to the table in the text?
quiz.explain: The table lists housefly lifespan as 15 to 25 days.

quiz.q: Which bird is described as larger than a sparrow and smaller than a crow with a long thick beak?
quiz.explain: The Kingfisher observation point describes it as larger than a sparrow and smaller than a crow with a long thick beak.

quiz.q: What do insects like termites help in, according to the text?
options: Making soil from dried plant parts
quiz.explain: Termites help make soil by decomposing dried parts of plants.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of insects as per the text?
options: They have a life cycle of egg—larva—pupa—adult
They help keep the environment clean
They are food for many birds
quiz.explain: Insects are oviparous (lay eggs), not viviparous.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: पाणी हे जीवनाचे आधार आहे.
पृथ्वीच्या ७१% भागावर पाणी आहे.
बहुतांश पाणी महासागरात आणि समुद्रात आहे.
फक्त १% पाणी गोडे आणि पिण्यायोग्य आहे.
गोडे पाणी जमिनीच्या वर आणि खाली दोन्ही ठिकाणी असते.
पाण्याचे स्रोत: नद्या, नाले, विहिरी, धरणे, तलाव.
पाणी गोठलेल्या अवस्थेत बर्फ आणि हिम म्हणून असते.
पाण्याचे योग्य वापर करणे आवश्यक आहे.
पाणी वाया जाऊ नये म्हणून स्वच्छता आणि बचत आवश्यक आहे.
पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर करणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
पाणी साठवण्यासाठी बंधारे आणि हौद बांधले जातात.
किल्ल्यांवरील दगडी तलाव पाणी साठवण्यासाठी वापरले जातात.
हौद हे पाणी साठवण्यासाठी पारंपरिक पद्धत आहे.
पाणी साठवण्यासाठी विविध भांडी वापरली जातात.
पाण्याच्या अपव्ययाची कारणे: नळ गळती, स्वच्छतेसाठी जास्त पाणी वापरणे.
पाण्याचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी पाणी बंद करणे, गळती दुरुस्त करणे आवश्यक आहे.
पाणी वाया जाऊ नये म्हणून स्वच्छ पाण्याचे महत्त्व समजून घ्या.
पाणी साठवण्यासाठी पाण्याचे टाकी, पिट, हौद इत्यादी वापरले जातात.
पाण्याचे योग्य व्यवस्थापन केल्यास सर्वांना फायदा होतो.
पाण्याचे संरक्षण हे सर्वांचे कर्तव्य आहे.
पाणी वाया जाऊ नये म्हणून घरात आणि बाहेर पाणी वापराचे नियम पाळा.
पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर केल्याने पाण्याची कमतरता कमी होते.
पाण्याचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी जागरूकता वाढवा.
पाणी वाया जाऊ नये म्हणून पाणी बंद ठेवणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.

quiz.q: पृथ्वीच्या सुमारे किती टक्के भाग पाण्याने व्यापलेला आहे?
quiz.explain: पृथ्वीच्या 71% भागावर पाणी आहे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे गोडे पाणी किती टक्के आहे?
quiz.explain: फक्त 1% पाणी गोडे आणि पिण्यायोग्य आहे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे मुख्य स्रोत कोणते?
quiz.explain: नद्या, नाले, विहिरी, धरणे, तलाव हे मुख्य स्रोत आहेत.

quiz.q: पाणी वाया जाऊ नये म्हणून काय करावे?
quiz.explain: पाणी बंद ठेवणे आणि साठवणे हे महत्त्वाचे आहे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे पुनर्वापर करण्याचे उदाहरण काय?
quiz.explain: कचरा पाणी स्वच्छ करून पुनर्वापर करणे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी कोणती पद्धत सर्वात प्रभावी आहे?
quiz.explain: सर्व पद्धती एकत्र वापराव्यात.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे गोडे पाणी मुख्यतः कुठे आढळते?
quiz.explain: जमिनीच्या वर आणि खाली दोन्ही ठिकाणी गोडे पाणी आहे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी घरात काय करावे?
quiz.explain: सर्व उपाय एकत्र करणे आवश्यक.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी कोणती पद्धत वापरावी?
quiz.explain: पाणी बंद ठेवणे आणि गळती दुरुस्त करणे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे संरक्षण करण्याचे महत्त्व काय?
options: पाणी वापरात कमी करणे आवश्यक नाही
quiz.explain: पाणी वाया जाऊ नये हे महत्त्वाचे आहे.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: नकाशा म्हणजे पृथ्वी व त्याच्या भागांचे प्रमाणबद्ध रेखाटन.
नकाशा तयार करताना दिशा, सांकेतिक चिन्हे, खुणे, प्रमाण व प्रक्षेपण वापरले जातात.

प्रमाण म्हणजे नकाशावरची एकक दूरी आणि वास्तविक जमिनीवरील अंतर यांचा नैतिक.
नकाशाच्या मूलभूत अंगे: शीर्षक, दिशा, सूची, प्रमाण.
दिशादर्शकाने नकाशा योग्य दिशेने मांडता येते.
सूचीमध्ये सांकेतिक चिन्हे व त्यांचे अर्थ दिले जातात.
नकाशात निसर्गनिर्मित घटक (जसे पर्वत, नदी) व मानवनिर्मित घटक (जसे घर, रस्ता) दाखवले जातात.

महाराष्ट्राची आकृती साधारणपणे त्रिकोणी आहे.
महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात लांबी नदी गोदावरी आहे, जी महाराष्ट्रात ७४० किमी लांबी आहे.
महाराष्ट्राच्या प्राकृतिक विभाग: कोकण किनारपट्टी, सह्याद्री पर्वतरांग, महाराष्ट्र पठार, विदर्भाचा मैदानी प्रदेश.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: महाराष्ट्रातील वनांचे पांच प्रकार: सदाहरित, निम सदाहरित, पानझडी, काटेरी, खारफुटी.
सदाहरित वन वर्षभर हिरवी राहतात, उदा. नागचंपा, जांभूळ, फणस.
पानझडी वने पावसाच्या प्रदेशात आढळतात, त्यात पाने गळून पडतात.
काटेरी वने कमी पावसाच्या भागात आढळतात, त्यात पाने लहान असतात.
खारफुटी वने समुद्रकिनार्यावर आढळतात, त्यात क्षारयुक्त मचूळ पाण्यात वाढतात.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय उद्यान: ताडोबा, संजय गांधी (बोरिवली).
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख अभयारण्य: रामलिंगघाट, भिमशंकर.
महाराष्ट्राची राजधानी मुंबई, उपराजधानी नागपूर.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख नद्या: गोदावरी, कृष्णा, भिमा, तापी.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख पिके: तांदूळ, ज्वारी, बाजरी, मका, तूर, सोयाबीन.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख फळे: आंबा, केळी, संत्रा, द्राक्षे, काजू.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख व्यापारी पिके: कपास, गन्ना, तूर, सोयाबीन.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख खनिजे: मँगनीज, लोहखनिज, बॉक्साइट, चुनखडक, क्रोमाईट.
महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख ऊर्जा साधने: तापविद्युत, जलविद्युत, सौरऊर्जा, जैवऊर्जा.
महाराष्ट्रातील राज्यपक्षी: हरियाल (हिरवे कबुतर), राज्यप्राणी: शेकरू.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात जास्त लांबी असलेली नदी कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: गोदावरी नदी महाराष्ट्रातील सर्वात लांबी नदी आहे.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्र राज्याची उपराजधानी कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: महाराष्ट्राची उपराजधानी नागपूर आहे.

quiz.explain: सदाहरित वनात जांभूळ यासारखे वृक्ष शिजात राहतात.

quiz.q: खारफुटी वने कोठे आढळतात?
quiz.explain: खारफुटी वने समुद्रकिनार्यावर क्षारयुक्त मचूळ पाण्यात आढळतात.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख खनिज मँगनीज मुख्यतः कोणत्या जिल्ह्यांमध्ये सापडतो?
quiz.explain: मँगनीज नागपूर, गोंदिया, भंडारा जिल्ह्यांमध्ये अधिक प्रमाणात सापडतो.

quiz.q: जिरायती शेती म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: जिरायती शेती पावसाच्या पाण्यावर अवलंबून केली जाऊ शकते.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्र राज्यातील राज्यपक्षी कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: हरियाल (हिरवे कबुतर) महाराष्ट्राचा राज्यपक्षी आहे.
