quiz.q: महाराष्ट्र दिन कधी साजरा केला जातो?
quiz.explain: महाराष्ट्र दिवस 9 नोव्हेंबर रोजी साजरा केला जातो.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख अन्नधान्य पिक कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: तांदूळ महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख अन्नधान्य पिक आहे.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: वाहतूक म्हणजे एका ठिकाण्यापासून दुसऱ्या ठिकाणी लोक व माल वाहणे.
संदेशवहन म्हणजे माहिती व संदेश एका ठिकाण्यापासून दुसऱ्या ठिकाणी पोहचवणे.
शहरी भागात रस्ते, वीज, पाणी, वाहतूक, वैद्यकीय व शैक्षणिक सुविधा उत्तम असतात.
ग्रामीण भागात सुविधा मर्यादित असतात, प्राथमिक आरोग्य केंद्र व प्राथमिक- माध्यमिक शाळा उपलब्ध असतात.
शहरी भागात रोजगाराची विविध संधी असतात, ग्रामीण भागात शेती व लहान उद्योगांवर अवलंबून राहावे लागते.
भौगोलिक परिस्थिती वाहतूक साधनांची निवड प्रभावित करते, जसे डोंगराळात रस्ते, पठारी व मैदानी भागात लोहमार्ग, किनारी भागात जलवाहतूक.
हवाई वाहतूक मोठ्या शहरांमध्ये उपलब्ध असते, हवाई वाहतूकासाठी विमानतळ व धावपट्टी आवश्यक असतात.
वाळवंटी व बर्फाळ प्रदेशात वाहतूकासाठी प्राण्यांचा वापर केला जातो.
आधुनिक वाहतूक साधने: समृद्धी महामार्ग, मुंबई-पुणे द्रुतगती महामार्ग, अटल सेतू, सी लिंक, पुणे-बंगळूरू महामार्ग इत्यादी.
पारंपरिक संदेशवहन साधने: टपाल, वृत्तपत्र, दूरध्वनी, दूरदर्शन, रेडिओ.
आधुनिक संदेशवहन साधने: भ्रमणध्वनी, इंटरनेट, ई-मेल, संगणक, कृत्रिम उपग्रह.
आधुनिक साधनेमुळे माहिती त्वरित मिळते व जगभर पसरली असते.
मोबाईलचा वापर आज मोठ्या प्रमाणात संदेशवहनासाठी केला जातो.
संदेशवहनाचा वापर शेती, उद्योग, व्यापार, वाहतूक, शिक्षण व माहिती तंत्रज्ञान क्षेत्रात केला जातो.
रहदारीचे नियम पालन करण्याने अपघात कमी होतात व सुरक्षितता वाढते.
ट्रॅफिक गार्डन हे बाग किंवा मोकळ्या जागेत तयार केलेले असते, जिथे मुलांना खेळत-खेळत रहदारीचे नियम समजवले जातात.

quiz.q: शहरी भागातील सुविधा कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: शहरी भागात वीज व पाणीपुरवठा उत्तम असतात, यामुळे पर्याय 2 योग्य.

quiz.q: पारंपरिक संदेशवहन साधने कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: दूरध्वनी पारंपरिक संदेशवहन साधने आहे, शेष आधुनिक.

quiz.q: वाळवंटी व बर्फाळ प्रदेशात वाहतूकासाठी कोणता वापर केला जातो?
quiz.explain: वाळवंटी व बर्फाळ प्रदेशात वाहतूकासाठी प्राण्यांचा वापर केला जातो.

quiz.q: जलद संदेशवहनाचे साधन कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: मोबाईल जलद संदेशवहनाचे साधन आहे.

quiz.q: शहरी व ग्रामीण भागातील उच्च शिक्षणाची सुविधा कोणत्या भागात सहज उपलब्ध होतात?
quiz.explain: उच्च शिक्षणाची सुविधा शहरी भागात सहज उपलब्ध होतात.

quiz.q: मुलांना वाहतुकीचे आणि रहदारीचे नियम समजवण्यासाठी योजना केलेली असते?
quiz.explain: ट्रॅफिक गार्डन हे योजना केलेले असते जिथे मुलांना खेळत-खेळत नियम समजवले जातात.

quiz.q: भौगोलिक परिस्थितीनुसार पठारी व मैदानी प्रदेशात कोणता वाहतूक साधन अधिक प्रमाणात आढळतो?
quiz.explain: पठारी व मैदानी प्रदेशात सपाट भू-भागामुळे लोहमार्ग वाहतूक अधिक प्रमाणात आढळते.

quiz.q: आधुनिक संदेशवहन साधने कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: इंटरनेट आधुनिक संदेशवहन साधने आहे, शेष पारंपरिक.

quiz.q: वाहतूक म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: वाहतूक म्हणजे एका ठिकाण्यापासून दुसऱ्या ठिकाणी लोक व माल वाहणे.

quiz.q: संदेशवहन म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: संदेशवहन म्हणजे माहिती व संदेश एका ठिकाण्यापासून दुसऱ्या ठिकाणी पोहचवणे.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: ऊर्जा म्हणजे कोणतेही काम करण्याची शक्ती.
खेळणे, धावणे, लिहिणे, बोलणे यांसाठी ऊर्जाची गरज असते.
ऊर्जा अन्नातून मिळते.
ऊर्जेचे मुख्य रूपे: प्रकाश ऊर्जा, विद्युत ऊर्जा, उष्णता ऊर्जा, ध्वनी ऊर्जा, सौर ऊर्जा, पवन ऊर्जा.
ऊर्जा स्रोत म्हणजे ज्यापासून ऊर्जा मिळते, उदा. सूर्य, वारा.
सौर ऊर्जा सूर्यापासून मिळणारी ऊर्जा.
पवन ऊर्जा वाऱ्याचा उपयोग करून पवनचक्कीद्वारे तयार होणारी ऊर्जा.
प्रकाश नेहमी सरळ रेषेत प्रवास करतो.
अपारदर्शक वस्तू प्रकाश अडवळते आणि त्यामुळे छाया तयार होते.
छाया प्रकाशाच्या मार्गात अपारदर्शक वस्तू येताने तयार होते.
शून्य छाया दिन म्हणजे सूर्य बरोबर माथ्यावर येतो त्या दिवस सावली नाहिशी होते.
चुंबक लोखंडी वस्तूंना स्वत:कडे ओढून घेतो, हे गुणधर्म चुंबकत्व.
चुंबकाकडे ओढले जाणारे पदार्थ चुंबकीय पदार्थ, ओढले न जाणारे अचुंबकीय पदार्थ.
राष्ट्रीय ऊर्जा संवर्धन दिवस १४ डिसेंबर रोजी साजरा केला जातो.

quiz.q: खेळण्यासाठी, धावण्यासाठी आणि बोलण्यासाठी आपल्याला काय गरज असते?
quiz.explain: खेळणे, धावणे, बोलणे यांसाठी शरीराला ऊर्जाची गरज असते.

quiz.q: सौर ऊर्जा काय आहे?
options: वाऱ्याचा उपयोग करून तयार होणारी ऊर्जा
quiz.explain: सौर ऊर्जा म्हणजे सूर्यापासून मिळणारी ऊर्जा.

quiz.q: प्रकाश कशी प्रवास करतो?
quiz.explain: प्रकाश नेहमी सरळ रेषेत प्रवास करतो.

quiz.q: जेव्हा प्रकाशाच्या मार्गात अपारदर्शक वस्तू येते, तेव्हा काय तयार होते?
quiz.explain: अपारदर्शक वस्तू प्रकाश अडवळते आणि त्यामुळे तिची छाया तयार होते.

quiz.q: वाऱ्याचा उपयोग करून पवनचक्कीद्वारे तयार होणारी ऊर्जा काय आहे?
quiz.explain: वाऱ्याचा उपयोग करून पवनचक्कीद्वारे तयार होणारी ऊर्जा पवन ऊर्जा आहे.

quiz.q: लोखंड हा किस प्रकार का पदार्थ है?
quiz.explain: लोखंड चुंबकाकडे ओढला जातो, त्यामुळे तो चुंबकीय पदार्थ आहे.

quiz.q: राष्ट्रीय ऊर्जा संवर्धन दिवस कधी साजरा केला जातो?
quiz.explain: राष्ट्रीय ऊर्जा संवर्धन दिवस प्रति वर्ष १४ डिसेंबर रोजी साजरा केला जातो.

quiz.q: छाया निर्मिती कशी होते?
quiz.explain: छाया प्रकाशाच्या मार्गात अपारदर्शक वस्तू येताने तयार होते.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणती ऊर्जा स्रोत नाही?
quiz.explain: चुंबक ऊर्जा स्रोत नाही, ती चुंबकत्व दर्शवते.

quiz.q: प्रकाश ऊर्जा का वापरली जाते?
quiz.explain: प्रकाश ऊर्जा म्हणजे सूर्यप्रकाश, ज्याचा वापर प्रकाशासाठी केला जातो.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: पाणी निर्धोक करणे म्हणजे पाण्यापासून गंदगी व जंतू काढून स्वच्छ करणे.
पाणी निर्धोक करण्याची पद्धती: गाळणे, निवळणे, उकळणे, निर्जंतुकीकरण.
गाळणे म्हणजे पाण्याने कपडा किंवा गाळणीने गाळून घेणे, ज्यामुळे मातीचे कण वेगळा होतो.
निवळणे म्हणजे पाण्यात तुरटी फिरवून मातीचे कण तळाशी जाणे.
उकळणे म्हणजे पाण्याला १० ते १५ मिनिटे उकळून जंतू नष्ट करणे.
निर्जंतुकीकरण म्हणजे पाण्यात ब्लिचिंग पावडर किंवा क्लोरीन टाकून जंतू नष्ट करणे.
निर्धोक पाणी म्हणजे कोणत्याही प्रकारे धोका न देणारा पाणी.
निर्धोक पाणी पिण्यासाठी स्वच्छ व सुरक्षित असतो, ज्यामुळे पोटदुखी, जुलाब टाळता येतात.
पाण्याचा पुनर्वापर म्हणजे वापरलेले पाणी पुन्हा वापरणे, जसे धुतले पाणी झाडांना देणे.
पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन म्हणजे पावसाचे पाणी साठवून जमिनीतील पाण्याची पातळी वाढवणे.
पावसाचे पाणी संवर्धन करण्यासाठी शेततळी खोदली जातात व डोंगर उतारावर चर खणले जातात.
माती तयार होण्यासाठी खूप वर्षे लागतात, म्हणून तिचे संरक्षण करणे आवश्यक आहे.
वालुकामय मातीत वाळू जास्त असतो, पाणी लगेच झिरपून जाते, माती लवकर कोरडी होते.
चिकणमाती खूप चिकट व मऊ असते, पाणी सहज धरून ठेवते, पिकांच्या वाढीसाठी वापरली जाते.
पोयटा माती वालुकामय, चिकणमाती व गाळ यांचे मिश्रण आहे, पाणी धरून ठेवते, ओलावा राहतो.

quiz.q: पाणी निर्धोक करण्याची कोणती पद्धत पाण्यातील जंतू नष्ट करते?
quiz.explain: उकळणे म्हणजे पाण्याला १०-१५ मिनिटे उकळणे, ज्यामुळे पाण्यातील जंतू नष्ट होतात.

quiz.q: निर्धोक पाणी म्हणजे काय?
options: कोणत्याही प्रकारे धोका न देणारा पाणी
quiz.explain: निर्धोक पाणी म्हणजे कोणत्याही प्रकारे धोका होत नाही असलेला पाणी.

quiz.q: पाण्याचा पुनर्वापर म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: पाण्याचा पुनर्वापर म्हणजे वापरलेले पाणी पुन्हा वापरणे, जसे धुतले पाणी झाडांना देणे.

quiz.q: पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन म्हणजे काय?
options: पावसाचे पाणी साठवून जमिनीतील पाण्याची पातळी वाढवणे
quiz.explain: पावसाच्या पाण्याचे संवर्धन म्हणजे पावसाचे पाणी साठवून जमिनीतील पाण्याची पातळी वाढवणे.

quiz.q: कोणती माती पाणी धरून ठेवते?
quiz.explain: चिकणमाती व पोयटा माती पाणी धरून ठेवते, वालुकामय मातीत पाणी लगेच झिरपून जाते.

quiz.q: मातीचा संरक्षण करणे आवश्यक असते का?
quiz.explain: माती तयार होण्यासाठी खूप वर्षे लागतात, म्हणून तिचे संरक्षण करणे आवश्यक आहे.

quiz.q: पाण्याचे प्रदूषण कोणती कारणे होऊ शकतात?
quiz.explain: पाण्याचे प्रदूषण कचरा, प्लॅस्टिक, रसायने इत्यादी अनेक घटकांमुळे होतो.

quiz.q: हृदयाचे कार्य कोणते?
quiz.explain: हृदय पंपाप्रमाणे काम करतो व शरीरभर रक्तवाहिन्यांतून रक्त खेळते ठेवतो.

quiz.q: कोणती पद्धत पाण्याने कपडा किंवा गाळणीने गाळून घेणे आहे?
quiz.explain: गाळणे म्हणजे पाण्याने कपडा किंवा गाळणीने गाळून घेणे, ज्यामुळे मातीचे कण वेगळा होतो.

quiz.q: मातीचा उपयोग कोणता?
options: पिकांच्या वाढीसाठी व विविध वस्तू तयार करण्यासाठी
quiz.explain: मातीचा उपयोग पिकांच्या वाढीसाठी व विविध वस्तू तयार करण्यासाठी होतो.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: आकाशात चमचमणाऱ्या चांदण्यांना 'तारे' म्हणतात.
ज्या चांदण्या चमचमत नाहीत त्यांना 'ग्रह' म्हणतात.
सूर्य हा एक तारा आहे, पृथ्वी हा एक ग्रह आहे.
पृथ्वीभोवती फिरणारा चंद्र हा पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह आहे.
सूर्यमालेत एकूण आठ ग्रह आहेत.
ग्रहांचा क्रम: बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी, मंगळ, गुरू, शनी, युरेनस, नेपच्यून.
सूर्यापासूनचे अंतर खगोलीय एकक (AU) मापतात.
1 खगोलीय एकक = पृथ्वी व सूर्याचं सरासरी अंतर = १४९ दशलक्ष किमी.
अंतर्गृह: बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी, मंगळ (सूर्यापासून लघुग्रह पट्ट्यापर्यंत).
बहिर्ग्रह: गुरू, शनि, युरेनस, नेपच्यून (लघुग्रह पट्ट्यापलीकडे).
उपग्रह: ग्रहांभोवती फिरणारे, e.g. चंद्र.
लघुग्रह: मंगळ व गुरू दरम्यान पट्ट्यातील खगोल.
बट॒ग्रह: सूर्याभोवती स्वतंत्रपणे फिरणारे लहान वस्तू, e.g. प्लुटो.
धूमकेतू: बर्फ, धूल, खडक बने खगोलीय वस्तू, लांब कालानंतर दिसते.
पृथ्वीची स्वत:भोवती गती = दैनिक गती = परिभ्रमण = 24 तास = 1 दिवस.
पृथ्वीची सूर्याभोवती गती = वार्षिक गती = परिक्रमा = ३६५ दिवस = 1 वर्ष.
पृथ्वी गोलाकार असल्याने दिवस व रात्र होतात.
चंद्राच्या प्रकाशित भागातील बदल चंद्रकला म्हणतात.
शुक्ल पक्ष: अमावस्या ते पौर्णिमा (प्रकाशित भाग वाढतो).
कृष्ण पक्ष: पौर्णिमे ते अमावस्या (प्रकाशित भाग कमी होतो).
चंद्र हा पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह आहे, त्याची फिरण्याची गती महिना मापण्यासाठी वापरते.

quiz.q: सूर्यमालेत सर्वात जवळचा ग्रह कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: बुध सूर्यापासून सर्वात जवळचा ग्रह आहे.

quiz.q: पृथ्वीचा उपग्रह कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: चंद्र पृथ्वीचा एकमेव नैसर्गिक उपग्रह आहे.

quiz.q: चंद्राच्या रोज बदलत्या आकारास काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: चंद्राच्या आकारात होणाऱ्या बदलांना चंद्रकला म्हणतात.

quiz.q: सूर्यमालेत एकूण किती ग्रह आहेत?
quiz.explain: सूर्यमालेत बुध, शुक्र, पृथ्वी, मंगळ, गुरू, शनी, युरेनस, नेपच्यून यांचा एकूण आठ ग्रह आहेत.

quiz.q: पृथ्वी एका दिवसात स्वत:भोवती एक फेरी पूर्ण करते यास काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: पृथ्वींची स्वत:भोवती गती दैनिक गती किंवा परिभ्रमण असे म्हणतात.

quiz.q: सूर्यापासूनचे अंतर मापण्यासाठी कोणता एकक वापरला जातो?
quiz.explain: सूर्यापासूनचे अंतर खगोलीय एकक (AU) मापतात.

quiz.q: धूमकेतू कधी आकाशात दिसते?
quiz.explain: धूमकेतू फार अंतरावर असतात आणि लांब कालानंतर दिसतात.

quiz.q: लघुग्रह कोणत्या दोन ग्रहांचे दरम्यान असतात?
quiz.explain: लघुग्रह सूर्यमालेमध्ये मंगळ व गुरू ग्रहांच्या दरम्यान असतात.

quiz.q: बट॒ग्रहाचा उदाहरण कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: प्लुटो बट॒ग्रहाचा एक उदाहरण आहे.

quiz.q: अंतर्गृहांचे गुणधर्म कोणते?
quiz.explain: अंतर्गृह खडकाळ असतात, त्यामुळे कठोर पातळी असते.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: वनस्पतींमध्ये पाने, खोड, मुळे यांचे तीन मुख्य अवयव असतात.
पाने हिरव्या वनस्पतींमध्ये प्रकाशसंश्लेषण करण्यामुळे अन्न तयार करतात.
मुळे मातीतून पाणी व पोषक घटक शोषतात आणि वनस्पतीला आधार देते.
खोड टणक असल्यास तो झाड, टणक नसल्यास तो रोपटे असतो.
फुलातील रंग व वासा कीटकांना आकर्षित करतो जेणेकरून परागण होतो.
फुलापासून फळ तयार होतात व फळातील बिया नवीन वनस्पतीच्या बीज असतात.
स्वयंपोषी वनस्पती स्वतःचे अन्न तयार करतात (उदा. आंबा), परपोषी दुसऱ्यावर वाढतात (उदा. अमरवेल).
कीटकभक्षी वनस्पती कीटकांचा सेवन करतात (उदा. टिंडोळा).
सोटमूळ मुख्य मुळापासून लहान उपमुळे फुटतो (उदा. आंबा), तंतुमूळ खोडापासून फुटणाऱ्या तंतूंसारखे असतात (उदा. गहू).
प्रकाशसंश्लेषणासाठी हवा, सूर्यप्रकाश, पाणी व पोषक घटक आवश्यक असतात.
वनस्पतींमधील आयुर्मान म्हणजे त्यांचे जगण्याचा काळ (उदा. पालक काही महिने, वड शेकडो वर्षे).
वनस्पतींमधील विविधता पानांचे आकार, रंग, पोत, कडा, फुलांचे रंग, गंध, आकार यात दिसते.
साधे पानेकडे एकाच पानाला पान असतो (उदा. लिंबू), संयुक्‍त पानेकडे अनेक लहान पर्णिका असतात (उदा. चिंच).
वनस्पतींमधील पदार्थे अन्न (उदा. तांदूळ), वस्त्र (उदा. कापूस), निवारा (उदा. लाकड), सावली, औषधे (उदा. तुळस) तयार करती.
झाडे लावून त्यांची काळजी घेणे पर्यावरण संरक्षणासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहे.

quiz.q: ज्या वनस्पती उंच वाढतात आणि त्यांचे खोड टणक असते, त्यांना काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: उंच वाढणाऱ्या आणि टणक खोड असलेल्या वनस्पतींना वृक्ष म्हणतात.

quiz.q: ज्या वनस्पती दुसर्‍या वनस्पतींवर वाढतात आणि त्यांच्याकडून थोडे अन्न शोषून घेतात, त्यांना काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: दुसऱ्यावर वाढून अन्न घेणाऱ्या वनस्पतींना परपोषी म्हणतात.

quiz.q: फुलांच्या रंगाचा आणि वासाचा वनस्पतीला कोणता उपयोग होतो?
quiz.explain: फुलांचे रंग व वासा कीटकांना आकर्षित करतात जेणेकरून परागण होतो.

quiz.q: कळीचे रूपांतर कशात होते?
quiz.explain: कळी फुलांमध्ये रूपांतरित होतात, त्यानंतर फुलापासून फळ तयार होतात.

quiz.q: वनस्पती कोणत्या प्रक्रियेने अन्न तयार करतात?
quiz.explain: हिरव्या वनस्पती प्रकाशसंश्लेषण प्रक्रियेने स्वतःचे अन्न तयार करतात.

quiz.q: मुळांचे मुख्य कार्य कोणते आहे?
quiz.explain: मुळे मातीतून पाणी व पोषक घटक शोषतात, त्यामुळे त्याचे मुख्य कार्य शोषण आहे.

quiz.q: ज्या मुळाला मुख्य मुळापासून लहान लहान उपमुळे फुटतात ते कोणत्या प्रकारचे मूळ असते?
quiz.explain: मुख्य मुळापासून लहान उपमुळे फुटणाऱ्या मुळांना सोटमूळ म्हणतात.

quiz.q: वनस्पती आपले अन्न तयार करण्यासाठी कोणत्या भागाचा वापर करतात?
quiz.explain: पाने हिरव्या वनस्पतींमध्ये प्रकाशसंश्लेषण करण्यामुळे अन्न तयार करतात.

quiz.q: प्रकाशसंश्लेषणासाठी वनस्पतींना कोणते घटक आवश्यक असतात?
options: हवा, सूर्यप्रकाश, पाणी व पोषक घटक
quiz.explain: प्रकाशसंश्लेषणासाठी हवा, सूर्यप्रकाश, पाणी व पोषक घटक यांचे संयोजन आवश्यक असते.

quiz.q: सोटमूळ व तंतुमूळ हे मुळांचे कोणते प्रकार आहेत?
quiz.explain: सोटमूळ व तंतुमूळ हे मुळांचे दोन मूलभूत प्रकार आहेत.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: पृथ्वींचा अक्ष 23°30' अंशाने कलला आहे.
सूर्याभोवती प्रदक्षिणा व अक्षाच्या कलण्यामुळे ऋतू बदल होतात.
उत्तर गोलार्धात सूर्यासमोर जाणे से तापमान वाढतो व उन्हाळा सुरू होतो.
दक्षिण गोलार्धात तापमान कमी होतो व हिवाळा सुरू होतो.
ज्या गोलार्धात उन्हाळा असतो, त्याच्या विरुद्ध गोलार्धात हिवाळा असतो.
ऋतू बदलामुळे वायुभारात फरक पडतो व वाऱ्यांची निर्मिती होते.
पाऊस पडतो, ज्यामुळे पावसाळा सुरू होतो.
भारतात तीन प्रमुख ऋतू: उन्हाळा, पावसाळा, हिवाळा.
उन्हाळ्यात सैल व सुती कपडे घालतो व थंड पेये पितो.
पावसाळ्यात छत्री, रेनकोट व प्रवासात काळजी घेतो.
हिवाळ्यात उबदार कपडे घालतो व पेरू, बोरे इत्यादी फळे खातो.
ऋतू बदलामुळे प्राण्यांचे वर्तन, पिकांचे उत्पादन व मानवी आरोग्यावर परिणाम होतो.
पक्ष्यांचे स्थलांतर हवामान बदल, अन्नाची उपलब्धता व पिलांचे संगोपन साठी होतो.
पावसाळ्याला सुरुवात झाल्यावर वृक्ष लागवड सप्ताह (१ जुलै ते ७ जुलै) साजरा करतात.
शेतकरी पावसाळ्यात पेरणी सुरू करतो व हिवाळ्यात संरक्षण करतात.

quiz.q: पृथ्वींचा अक्ष किती अंशांनी कलला आहे?
quiz.explain: पृथ्वींचा अक्ष 23°30' अंशाने कलला आहे, ज्यामुळे ऋतू बदल होतात.

quiz.q: उन्हाळ्यात आपण कोणते कपडे घालतो?
quiz.explain: उन्हाळ्यात वातावरणात उष्णता जास्त असल्यामुळे आपण सैल व सुती कपडे घालतो.

quiz.q: पावसाळ्यात आपण कोणती वस्तू वापरतो?
quiz.explain: पावसाळ्यात पाऊस पडल्यामुळे आपण छत्री, रेनकोट इत्यादी वापरतो.

quiz.q: हिवाळ्यात कोणते फळे मिळतात?
quiz.explain: हिवाळ्यात पेरू, बोरे इत्यादी फळे मिळतात, जे आपण खातो.

quiz.q: पृथ्वीच्या सूर्याभोवती फिरण्यामुळे व अक्षाच्या कलण्यामुळे काय होतो?
quiz.explain: सूर्याभोवती फिरण्यामुळे व अक्षाच्या कलण्यामुळे ऋतू बदल होतात.

quiz.q: प्रत्येक मुख्य ऋतूचा कालावधी किती महिन्यांची असते?
quiz.explain: प्रत्येक मुख्य ऋतूचा कालावधी चार महिन्यांची असते.

quiz.q: जून ते सप्टेंबर या कालावधीत आपल्या देशात कोणता ऋतू असतो?
quiz.explain: जून ते सप्टेंबर या कालावधीत आपल्या देशात पावसाळा असतो.

quiz.q: सरबत, ताक ही पेये कोणत्य ऋतूती जास्त प्रमाणात पिळावीत?
quiz.explain: उन्हाळ्यात वातावरणात उष्णता जास्त असल्यामुळे सरबत, ताक ह्यांची गरज जास्त असते.

quiz.q: ऋतू बदलामुळे मानवी आरोग्यावर कोणते परिणाम होतात?
quiz.explain: ऋतू बदलामुळे मानवी आरोग्यावर सर्दी-जुकाम, वाढ, बोनी इत्यादी परिणाम होतात.

quiz.q: पक्ष्यांचे स्थलांतर कोठे अधिक होतो?
quiz.explain: जास्तीत जास्त पक्षी हिवाळ्यात भारतात येतात, त्यामुळे हिवाळ्यात भारतात स्थलांतर अधिक होतो.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: शेती मुख्यतः पावसाच्या पाण्यावर अवलंबून असते.
जास्त पावसात तांदूळ, नाचणी, वरई, नारळ घेतले जातात.
मध्यम पावसात गहू, तूर, सोयाबीन घेतले जातात.
कमी पावसात ज्वारी, बाजरी, मूग, मटकी घेतले जातात.
पिके उत्तम येण्यासाठी सुधारित बीज, सुपीक जमीन, सूर्यप्रकाश आणि पाणी आवश्यक आहेत.
देशात विविध प्रदेशांनुसार अन्नधान्य व भाजीपाळ्यामध्ये विविधता दिसते.
सेंद्रिय शेतेत रासायनिक खते वापरत नाही, शेण, कंपोस्ट इत्यादी वापरले जातात.
सेंद्रिय शेतेत उत्पादन सकस असते आणि मृदेची सुपीकता टिकून राहते.
आधुनिक तंत्रज्ञानाने शेतीची उत्पादकता वाढली आहे.
अन्न साठवण्याआधी धान्ये वाळवतात त्या खराब होण्यापासून वाचतात.
अन्न शिजवण्याने ते पचायला सोपे जाते आणि चवदार व रुचकर होतात.
फळे, काकडी, टोमॅटो इत्यादी कच्चे खात येईल पदार्थ असतात.
अन्न तयार करण्याची पद्धती: भाजणे, शिजवणे, उकडणे, वाफवणे, तळणे इत्यादी.
अन्न साठवण्याची पद्धती: वाळवणे, मुरवणे, खारवणे, कडुनिंबाचा पाला मिसळून धान्य साठवणे.
दूषित अन्न हे खराब झालेले, विषारी किंवा आजार पसरवणारे अन्न असते.

quiz.q: शेती मुख्यतः कशावर अवलंबून असते?
quiz.explain: शेती मुख्यतः पावसाच्या पाण्यावर अवलंबून असते.

quiz.q: जास्त पावसाच्या प्रदेशात कोणती पिक घेतली जाते?
quiz.explain: जास्त पावसाच्या प्रदेशात तांदूळ, नाचणी, वरई, नारळ घेतले जातात.

quiz.q: सेंद्रिय शेतीत कोणते खाते वापरत नाहीत?
quiz.explain: सेंद्रिय शेतीत रासायनिक खते वापरत नाहीत.

quiz.q: अन्न साठवण्याआधी धान्ये कशे वाळवतात?
quiz.explain: धान्ये वाळवतात त्यांना खराब होण्यापासून वाचवते.

quiz.q: अन्न शिजवण्याचे फायदा कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: अन्न शिजवण्याने ते पचायला सोपे जाते आणि चवदार व रुचकर होतात.

quiz.q: कोणती पद्धती अन्न साठवण्यासाठी वापरली जाते?
quiz.explain: अन्न साठवण्याची पद्धती: वाळवणे, मुरवणे, खारवणे, कडुनिंबाचा पाला मिसळून धान्य साठवणे.

quiz.q: दूषित अन्न खाल्याने कोणता परिणाम होतो?
quiz.explain: दूषित अन्न आहारात आल्याने शारीरिक थकवा व जुलाब आणि अशक्तपणा होतो.

quiz.q: पर्यावरणपूरक घरात कोणती ऊर्जा साधने जास्त वापरली जातात?
quiz.explain: पर्यावरणपूरक घरात पवन ऊर्जा, सौर ऊर्जा, बायोगॅस यांसारख्या अपारंपरिक ऊर्जा साधनांचा जास्त वापर केला जातो.

quiz.q: शेतकरी शेतात प्रथम कोणती काम करतो?
quiz.explain: शेतकरी शेतात प्रथम मशागत ची कामे करतो.

quiz.q: शेती उत्पादन वाढवण्यासाठी कोणता तंत्रज्ञान वापर केला जातो?
quiz.explain: शेती उत्पादन वाढवण्यासाठी आधुनिक तंत्रज्ञानाचा वापर केला जातो.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: आपत्ती म्हणजे अचानक उद्भवणारी आणि मोठा नुकसान करणारी घटना.
नैसर्गिक आपत्ती: पाऊस, भूकंप, दरड कोसळणे, चक्रीवादळ, दुष्काळ इत्यादी.
मानवनिर्मित आपत्ती: आग, प्रदूषण, युद्ध, अपघात, शॉर्टसर्किट.
दुष्काळ म्हणजे पाऊस कमी पडल्यामुळे पाण्याची टंचाई.
दुष्काळावर मात करण्यासाठी पाण्याचे नियोजन, बंधारे, तलाव, धरणे बांधणे.
तिबक व तुषार सिंचन वापरण्याने पाण्याची बचत होते.
चक्रीवादळामुळे वेगाने वारे, मुसळधार पाऊस, समुद्री उंच लाटा निर्माण होतो.
चक्रीवादळापासून बचाव: हवामान खात्याने संदेश ऐकणे, सुरक्षित ठिकाणी राहणे, अनावश्यक प्रवास टाळणे.
अतिवृष्टीमुळे नद्या-नाल्यांमध्ये पाणी भरतो, पूर येतो, घरे, पिके, झाडे नष्ट होतात.
घरात सुरक्षित राहण्यासाठी गॅस, विजेची उपकरणे, धोकादायक रसायने, उंची ठिकाणी काळजी घ्यावी.
लिफ्टमध्ये वडीलधार्यांसोबतच जाणे, लहान मुलांना आधार देणे, दृष्टिहीन मदत करणे.
दृष्टिमित्र बनवणे: डोळ्यांवर पट्टी बांधणे, आधार देणे, मार्गदर्शन करणे.
अनोळखी व्यक्‍तीने काही देण्याचा प्रयत्न केल्यास तुरंत 'नाही' म्हणा, बोलणे व थांबणे टाळणे.
बळजबरीने पकडण्याचा प्रयत्न केल्यास शांत राहणे, हातापात करणे, धक्का देणे.
सुरक्षा चिन्हे: जीवनरक्षक पिशवी तयार करणे, आपत्ती व्यवस्थापन क्रमांक जाणून घेणे (पोलीस-100, अग्निशमन-101, अंबुलन्स-108/102, बाल मदत-1098, आपत्ती व्यवस्थापन-1077).

quiz.q: नैसर्गिक आपत्ती कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: भूकंप नैसर्गिक आपत्ती आहे, बाकी मानवनिर्मित.

quiz.q: दुष्काळ का घडतो?
quiz.explain: दुष्काळ म्हणजे पाऊस कमी पडल्यामुळे पाण्याची टंचाई.

quiz.q: चक्रीवादळापासून बचाव करण्यासाठी काय करणे महत्त्वाचे आहे?
quiz.explain: हवामान खात्याने दिलेले संदेश ऐकणे, सुरक्षित ठिकाणी राहणे, अनावश्यक प्रवास टाळणे.

quiz.q: घरात काय घडवू शकतो मानवनिर्मित आपत्ती म्हणून?
quiz.explain: गॅस चालू ठेवणे, शॉर्टसर्किट, कचरा जाळणे यामुळे घरात आग लागू शकते.

quiz.q: लहान मुलांपासून काय दूर ठेवले पाहिजेत?
quiz.explain: औषधे, किटकनाशके आणि रसायने लहान मुलांपासून दूर ठेवले पाहिजेत.

quiz.q: प्लॅस्टिकचा वापर टाळणे का महत्त्वाचे आहे?
options: ते पर्यावरणाला प्रदूषित करते आणि रोगराई पसरवू शकते
quiz.explain: प्लॅस्टिक पर्यावरणाला प्रदूषित करते आणि रोगराई पसरवू शकते.

quiz.q: आपत्कालीन मदतसाठी पोलीसला काय क्रमांक फोन करावे?
quiz.explain: पोलीस मदतसाठी 100 क्रमांक फोन करावे.

quiz.q: दृष्टिमित्र बनवताना काय करणे आवश्यक आहे?

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: परिसर स्वच्छ ठेवणे आपली जबाबदारी आहे.
कचरा कमी न केल्यास दुर्गंधी पसरते, आजार पसरतात, आरोग्यासाठी घातक असते.
ओला कचरा: जो कचरा कुजतो व सडतो (उदा. भाज्यांची देठे, पाने, अंडांची टरफले).
ओला कचरा साठवण्यासाठी हिरव्या रंगाची कचरापेटी वापरते.
सुका कचरा: जो कचरा न कुजतो, न सडतो अनेक दिवस राहतो (उदा. प्लास्टिक, कागद, खिळे).
सुका कचरा साठवण्यासाठी निळ्या रंगाची कचरापेटी वापरते.
ओला कचरा कुजून कंपोस्ट खत तयार केला जातो.
कंपोस्ट खत म्हणजे ओला कचरा कुजून तयार झालेला जैविक खत.
सुका कचरा कारखान्यांत पाठवून नवीन वस्तू तयार केली जातात.
कचरा कमी करण्यासाठी: वापरात नसलेल्या वस्तूंचा वापर, सुस्थितीत असलेल्या वस्तूंचा वापर.
पुनर्वापर: जुनी वस्तू पुन्हा वापरणे (उदा. कोऱ्या पाने चित्रे काढण्यासाठी).
पुनर्चक्रीकरण: सुका कचर्यातील पदार्थे (प्लास्टिक, कागद) वापरून नवीन वस्तू तयार करणे.
कचरा कमी, पुनर्वापर, पुनर्चक्रीकरण हे परिसर स्वच्छ व सुंदर ठेवण्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहेत.
पाणी अपव्यय करणे नका; नळ सुरू राहिल्यास तुरंत बंद करा.
शाळेत स्वच्छता नियम पाळा: कचरा योग्य पेटीत टाका, कागद खोडरबर फेकू नका, भिंतीवर खरडू नका.

quiz.q: ओला कचरा काय आहे?
options: जो कचरा न कुजतो, न सडतो
quiz.explain: ओला कचरा म्हणजे जो कचरा कुजतो व सडतो, जसे भाज्यांची देठे, पाने इत्यादी.

quiz.q: सुका कचरा साठवण्यासाठी कोणती रंगाची कचरापेटी वापरते?
quiz.explain: सुका कचरा साठवण्यासाठी निळ्या रंगाची कचरापेटी वापरते.

quiz.q: कंपोस्ट खत म्हणजे काय?
options: ओला कचरा कुजून तयार झालेला जैविक खत
सुका कचरा जला करून तयार खत
quiz.explain: कंपोस्ट खत म्हणजे ओला कचरा (जसे भाज्यांची देठे, पाने) कुजून तयार झालेला खत.

quiz.q: पुनर्वापराचा अर्थ काय आहे?
quiz.explain: पुनर्वापर म्हणजे जुनी झालेली वस्तू पुन्हा वापरणे, जसे कोऱ्या पाने चित्रे काढण्यासाठी.

quiz.q: प्लास्टिकची बाटली कोणत्या वर्गात येते?
quiz.explain: प्लास्टिकची बाटली न कुजते, न सडते, त्यामुळे सुका कचरा आहे.

quiz.q: घरात पाण्याचा नळ सुरू राहिल्यास काय करावे?
quiz.explain: पाण्याचा अपव्यय टाळण्यासाठी नळ सुरू राहिल्यास तुरंत बंद करावे.

quiz.q: शाळेत कागद व खोडरबरचे तुकडे काय करणे नाहीत?
quiz.explain: शाळेत कागद व खोडरबरचे तुकडे जमिनीवर फेकू नका, त्यामुळे स्वच्छता बाळगते.

quiz.q: कचरा कमी करण्यासाठी स्टीलचा पेला वापरावे का?
options: नाही, स्टीलचा पेला वापरणे कठीण आहे
quiz.explain: प्लास्टिकचे पेला जागविण्यासाठी स्टीलचा पेला वापरून कचरा कमी होतो.

quiz.q: ओला कचरा कुजून तयार होणारा खत काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: ओला कचरा कुजून तयार होणारा खत कंपोस्ट खत म्हणजे.

quiz.q: परिसर स्वच्छ ठेवण्यासाठी आपली जबाबदारी काय आहे?
options: परिसर स्वच्छ ठेवणे आपली जबाबदारी आहे
quiz.explain: परिसर स्वच्छ ठेवणे आपली जबाबदारी आहे, जसे की घर, शाळा, आजूबाजू.

subject: EVS Part 1
notes: प्राण्यांचे विविध प्रकार असतात: पक्षी, कीटक, स्तनधारी, मासे इ.
प्रत्येक प्राण्यांची वैशिष्ट्ये असतात जसे आकार, रंग, अन्न, राहण्याची जागा, उडण्याची पद्धती.
पक्षींचे मुख्य अवयव: चोच, पाय, पंख, पिसं.
पक्षींचे अन्न, राहण्याची जागा, उडण्याची पद्धती वेगवेगळ्या असतात.
कीटक लहान असतात पERO संख्या भरपूर असते व पर्यावरण स्वच्छ ठेवण्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहेत.
कीटक मातीत वाळविसारखे वाळलेल्या भागांचे विघटन करून माती बनवतात.
कीटक फुलांपासून फळ तयार होण्याच्या प्रक्रियेत मदत करतात.
कीटक अनेक पक्ष्यांचे आणि प्राण्यांचे अन्न हवे.
अंडज प्राणी: जे अंड्यातून जन्म देतात (उदा. पक्षी, कीटक, सरपटणारे प्राणी).
जरायुज प्राणी: जे पिल्लांना जन्म देतात (उदा. मानव, कुत्रा, मांजर, गाय).
अंडी-आळी-कोष-पतंग हे जीवनक्रम बऱ्याच कीटकांचा असतो.
अन्नसाखळी: जे जीव अन्नासाठी दुसऱ्या जीवावर अवलंबून असतात.
शाकाहारी प्राणी: वनस्पती खातो (उदा. हरीण, गाय, म्हैस).
मांसाहारी प्राणी: शाकाहारी प्राण्यांना खातो (उदा. अळी, बेडूक, साप, गरुड).
प्राण्यांचे आयुर्मान वेगवेगळे असतात (उदा. फुलपाखरू: १-२ आठवडे, मानव: ८०-१०० वर्षे).
परिसराशी एकरूप झालेले प्राणी: त्यांचे रंग व आकार परिसराशी असेच एकरूप असतो (उदा. काडीकिडा).
समूहात राहणारे प्राणी: अन्न शोधणे, पिल्लांची काळजी, धोका ओळखणे, एकमेकांचे रक्षण करणे यास मदत मिळतो.
निशाचर प्राणी: रात्रीला बाहेर पडते (उदा. कोल्हा, लांडगा, घुबड, बिबट्या, वटवाघूळ, खवले मांजर, रानमांजर, साप).
दिवसचर प्राणी: दिवसाला बाहेर पडते (उदा. कुत्रा, हरीण, गाय, म्हैस).
कीटक, पक्षी, प्राणी यांचे अवलंबून अन्नसाखळी तयार होते.
प्राणी निरीक्षण करताना तेचे शांतपणे अवलंबुन करणे गरजे.
प्राणी, अंडी, घरटी, छोटे कीटक यांना हात लावू नये.

quiz.q: पक्ष्यांचे कोणते अवयव उडण्यास मदत करते?
quiz.explain: पंख उडण्यास मुख्यतः मदत करते.

quiz.q: कीटकांचे कोणते कार्य पर्यावरण स्वच्छ ठेवण्यासाठी महत्त्वाचे आहेत?
options: मातीत वाळविसारखे वाळलेले भागे विघटन करणे
quiz.explain: कीटक मातीत वाळविसारखे वाळलेले भागे विघटन करून माती बनवतात.

quiz.q: जे प्राणी अंड्यातून जन्म देतात, त्यांना काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: अंड्यातून जन्म देणाऱ्या प्राण्यांना अंडज म्हणतात.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणता शाकाहारी प्राणी नाही?
quiz.explain: अळी मांसाहारी प्राणी आहे, त्यामुथे शाकाहारी नाही.

quiz.q: फुलपाखरूचे आयुर्मान किती असते?
quiz.explain: फुलपाखरूचे आयुर्मान १ ते २ आठवडे असते.

quiz.q: प्राण्यांचे आयुर्मान काय म्हणजे?
quiz.explain: आयुर्मान म्हणजे जिवाचे जन्मापासून मृत्यूपर्यंतचा संपूर्ण कालावधी.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणता निशाचर प्राणी नाही?
quiz.explain: हरीण दिवसचर प्राणी आहे, निशाचर नाही.

quiz.q: कीटकांना खाणारे कोणते पक्षी तुम्हांला माहीत आहेत?
quiz.explain: गवतकीडा कीटक खातो.

quiz.q: वनस्पती आणि प्राणी यांची दोघे खाणाऱ्या प्राण्यांना काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: वनस्पती आणि प्राणी यांची दोघे खाणाऱ्या प्राण्यांना सर्वाहारी म्हणतात.

quiz.q: प्राणी निरीक्षण करताना काय करणे गरजे?
quiz.explain: प्राणींचे शांतपणे निरीक्षण करणे गरजे.

subject: EVS Part 2
chapter: Maharashtra before the Times of Shivaji Maharaj
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a brave king who lived in the medieval period.
He fought against the powerful sultans of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and the Mughal emperor.
Shivaji created Swaraj, meaning self‑government, for the people of Maharashtra.
Swaraj was based on justice, fairness and equal treatment for all castes and religions.
He did not distinguish between Hindus and Muslims and honoured saints of all faiths.
Before him, Maharashtra was ruled by the Nizamshah, Adilshah and the Mughals who oppressed the people.
The people were hungry, unhappy and had no freedom under these rulers.
Shivaji’s Swaraj gave the people a sense of safety and dignity.
He used clever tactics and won many battles to establish his rule.
His legacy is celebrated every year on Shivaji Maharaj’s birthday (Shivaji Jayanti).
The people sang powadas and worshipped him with garlands and songs.
Shivaji’s Swaraj was a model of good governance and fairness.
The term Swaraj means ‘our own rule’ or self‑rule.
Shivaji’s Swaraj lasted for about 200 years after his death.
His story inspires people to fight for justice and freedom.

quiz.q: In which period did Shivaji Maharaj live?
quiz.explain: Shivaji Maharaj lived during the medieval period.

quiz.q: What did Shivaji Maharaj establish for Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: He established Swaraj, meaning self‑government.

quiz.q: Which of these rulers did Shivaji fight against?
quiz.explain: He fought against all three.

quiz.q: What is Swaraj?
quiz.explain: Swaraj means self‑government.

quiz.q: Shivaji Maharaj was known for treating all people equally. Which term best describes this?
quiz.explain: He practiced equality among all castes.

quiz.q: Which saint’s shrine did Shivaji honor?
quiz.explain: He honored saints of all religions.

quiz.q: The people sang powadas to celebrate Shivaji. Powadas are:
quiz.explain: Powadas are songs praising Shivaji.

quiz.q: Shivaji Maharaj’s Swaraj lasted for how many years?
quiz.explain: It lasted about 200 years.

quiz.q: Which of the following was NOT a ruler Shivaji fought?
quiz.explain: The British were not yet present.

quiz.q: Shivaji’s Swaraj was based on which of these principles?
quiz.explain: All three principles were central.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji was a brave king who fought many battles.
Panhala fort was captured by Shivaji from the Bijapur army.
Siddi Jauhar was a powerful enemy who tried to stop Shivaji.
Shivaji used a clever trick to escape from the siege by sending a fake palanquin.
Baji Prabhu Deshpande was a loyal soldier who defended the Ghodkhind pass.
The Ghodkhind pass is a steep and narrow path that was hard to cross.
Shivaji and Baji Prabu fought together to protect the fort of Vishalgad.
Baji Prabhu died while protecting the pass but his bravery is remembered.
The battle at Ghodkhind made the pass famous as a symbol of courage.
Shivaji’s escape shows his cleverness and determination to protect his people.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shivaji capture from the Bijapur army?
quiz.explain: Shivaji captured Panhala fort from the Bijapur garrison.

quiz.q: Who sent a fake palanquin to help Shivaji escape?
quiz.explain: Baji Prabhu sent a fake palanquin to deceive the enemy.

quiz.q: What was the main reason Siddi Jauhar was angry?
options: He was sad about his father
quiz.explain: Siddi Jauhar was angry because he wanted to avenge his father’s death.

quiz.q: Which pass did Baji Prabhu defend?
quiz.explain: Baji Prabhu defended the Ghodkhind pass.

quiz.q: What did Shivaji do after escaping the siege?
quiz.explain: After escaping, Shivaji went to Vishalgad.

quiz.q: Who was the brave soldier that died at Ghodkhind?
quiz.explain: Baji Prabhu died while defending the pass.

quiz.q: What made the Ghodkhind pass famous?
quiz.explain: The Ghodkhind pass became famous because of the battle fought there.

quiz.q: Which of these was a clever trick used by Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Shivaji used a fake palanquin to escape.

quiz.q: Why did Siddi Masaud pursue Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Siddi Masaud pursued Shivaji to capture him.

quiz.q: What is the main lesson from Shivaji’s escape?
options: Cleverness and courage are both important
quiz.explain: Shivaji’s escape shows that cleverness and courage are both important.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shaista Khan was a Mughal general sent by Emperor Aurangzeb to attack the Maratha king Shivaji.
He marched from Bijapur and captured the fort of Chakan, but was defeated there.
Shaista Khan then laid siege to the fort of Purandar in 1660, but could not force Shivaji to surrender.
Shivaji fought back and eventually broke the siege, forcing Shaista Khan to retreat.
Later, Aurangzeb sent a larger army of 75,000 men, including elephants and cannon, to Pune.
Shaista Khan tried to escape through the windows of Lal Mahal, the Maratha palace, but was caught by Shivaji’s spies.
Shivaji entered Lal Mahal at night, killed Shaista Khan’s son, and forced the general to flee.
This event was a major blow to Mughal power in Maharashtra.
Shivaji’s use of surprise, spies, and knowledge of the palace’s secret passages was key to his victory.
The incident shows how intelligence and daring tactics can defeat a larger force.
The story is an example of Maratha resistance and the importance of protecting one’s capital.
It also illustrates the consequences of underestimating an opponent’s courage and skill.
The battle at Lal Mahal is remembered as a proud moment in Maratha history.
Key dates: 1660 – siege of Purandar; 1663 – attack on Lal Mahal.
Shivaji’s tactics included disguising his troops as a wedding procession and using the palace’s hidden passages.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shaista Khan capture before being defeated by Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Shaista Khan captured Chakan but was defeated there.

quiz.q: What was the main reason Aurangzeb sent a larger army to Pune?
quiz.explain: Aurangzeb wanted to crush Shivaji after the failed siege.

quiz.q: How many men were in the Mughal army that attacked Pune?
quiz.explain: The army numbered 75,000 men.

quiz.q: What tactic did Shivaji use to enter Lal Mahal?
quiz.explain: Shivaji entered at night disguised as a wedding procession.

quiz.q: What did Shivaji do to Shaista Khan’s son?
quiz.explain: Shivaji killed the son to demoralise the Mughal troops.

quiz.q: Why did Shaista Khan try to escape through the windows of Lal Mahal?
options: He wanted to escape the siege
He was looking for a secret passage
He wanted to spy on Shivaji
He was looking for a new palace
quiz.explain: He tried to escape the siege by using the palace windows.

quiz.q: Which of the following was NOT a tactic used by Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Shivaji did not use a large cannon in this attack.

quiz.q: What was the outcome of the attack on Lal Mahal?
quiz.explain: Shivaji won the battle.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shaista Khan capture on his way to Pune?
quiz.explain: He captured Chakan on the way to Pune.

quiz.q: What was the main consequence of Shivaji’s victory at Lal Mahal?
quiz.explain: It was a major blow to Mughal power.

subject: EVS Part 2
chapter: The Siege and Treaty of Purandar
notes: The Siege of Purandar was fought between the Marathas and the Mughal army led by Dilerkhan.
Shivaji Maharaj was the king of the Marathas and the ruler of Pune.
The fort of Purandar was a stronghold of Shivaji’s forces.
Dilerkhan, a Mughal general, wanted to capture Purandar to weaken the Marathas.
Murarbaji Deshpande was the commander of the fort and defended it bravely.
During the siege, Murarbaji fought hard but was eventually killed by a cannon shot.
After the battle, Shivaji decided to negotiate a treaty with the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665 and gave the Mughals control of 23 forts and a revenue of four lakh rupees.
Shivaji kept his promise to return safely to Pune after the treaty.
The treaty helped Shivaji to plan future attacks on the Mughal empire.
The Marathas used the treaty to regroup and strengthen their forces.
The siege showed the courage and skill of Maratha commanders like Murarbaji.
The Mughal army was large and had powerful cannons and elephants.
Shivaji’s raid on Surat earlier showed his bravery and strategic thinking.
The treaty was a diplomatic solution, not a war victory.
The Marathas still fought after the treaty and continued to challenge the Mughals.
The story teaches that courage, strategy and diplomacy are all important in war.
The Treaty of Purandar was a turning point in the Maratha–Mughal conflict.
The Marathas used forts like Purandar to protect their territory.
The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb was a powerful ruler who wanted to control all of India.
The Marathas were known for their guerrilla tactics and quick attacks.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a brave king who ruled Maharashtra.
He once visited the Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb in Agra.
Shivaji did not like the way the Emperor treated him and his people.
He decided to leave the court secretly and escape from Agra.
Shivaji used a clever plan: he hid in baskets that were allowed to pass without inspection.
The baskets were meant to carry sweets for the Emperor’s guests.
Shivaji and his son Sambhaji were hidden inside two baskets.
When the baskets reached a pre‑arranged spot, they got out and ran away on horses.
The Emperor tried to catch them, but they escaped and never returned to Agra.
After escaping, Shivaji returned to his kingdom and continued to rule bravely.
The story shows how clever thinking can help a leader protect his people.
It also teaches that courage and planning are important for a king.
Shivaji’s escape is remembered as a great act of bravery.
The story is part of the Maharashtra State Board textbook for Standard 4.
It is written in simple English for young students.
The chapter is titled “Shivaji Maharaj Outwits the Badshah”.
Key facts: He hid in baskets, his son was left behind, the Emperor was angry, he escaped to Rajgad.
The story is used to teach history, courage, and problem‑solving.

Because he was angry at the Emperor
Because he wanted to visit his mother

options: He rode a horse into the forest
quiz.explain: He hid in baskets that were allowed to pass.

quiz.explain: To avoid being seen by guards.

subject: EVS Part 2
chapter: The Fort is Won but the Lion is Lost
notes: The fort was captured by Shivaji’s army but the brave warrior Tanaji died in the battle.
Tanaji Malusare was a close comrade of Shivaji and a fearless soldier.
The fort of Kondana was one of the 23 forts that Shivaji had to capture from the Mughals.
Jijamata, Shivaji’s mother, urged him to capture Kondana before attending a wedding.
Shivaji decided to launch a campaign to recapture Kondana and asked Tanaji to lead it.
Tanaji planned to attack the fort by scaling a steep precipice and entering through the Kalyan gate.
The fort had two entrances: a main gate and a side gate guarded by a steep slope.
Udaybhan was a Rajput officer appointed by Jaising to guard Kondana; he had a disciplined garrison of 500 men.
During the attack, Tanaji and his men fought bravely but were outnumbered and eventually killed.
After Tanaji’s death, the Mavlas (soldiers) lost their leader and had to retreat from the fort.
The phrase “The fort is won but the lion is dead” means the fort was captured but the brave warrior died.
Shivaji expressed sorrow over Tanaji’s death and performed a mourning ceremony at Umrathe.
The Kalyan gate was the main entrance that Tanaji’s men tried to open during the battle.
The fort’s walls were heavily guarded and the battle was fought in the dark night with torches.
The Mavlas managed to climb the steep precipice but many were cut off by a rope tied to a tree.
The story teaches that courage and sacrifice are more important than material gains.
It also shows the importance of planning and timing in military campaigns.
The name of Tanaji’s younger brother was Murarbaji.
The fort of Kondana later became known as Sinhagad after its capture.
The battle took place in 1670, the same year Shivaji’s son Rajaram was born.
The story is part of the Maharashtra State Board (Balbharati) textbook for Standard 4, EVS Part 2.

options: The fort was captured but the brave warrior died
The fort was lost and the lion escaped
The fort was captured and the lion was captured
The fort was lost and the lion died
quiz.explain: It refers to the fort being captured but the brave warrior Tanaji dying.

quiz.explain: Udaybhan was the Rajput officer guarding the fort.

quiz.explain: The steep precipice made entry difficult.

quiz.explain: Murarbaji was Tanaji’s younger brother.

quiz.explain: She urged him to capture Kondana first.

quiz.explain: The battle occurred in 1670.

quiz.explain: They lost their leader and had to retreat.

quiz.explain: It became known as Sinhagad.

quiz.explain: Shivaji performed the ceremony.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was crowned king in 1674.
The coronation ceremony was held at Raigad fort.
Shivaji chose Raigad as the capital because it was a strong hill fort and easy to defend.
During the ceremony, a golden throne was made and a canopy (chhatra) was placed over Shivaji’s head.
A special vessel was filled with water from seven rivers: Ganga, Sindhu, Yamuna, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada, Kaveri and the sea.
The water was poured over Shivaji’s head to purify him before he became king.
Shivaji’s mother Jijamata’s eyes filled with tears of joy when he was crowned.
Shivaji struck his own coins after the coronation to show his sovereignty.
The coronation calendar was started by Shivaji to mark the beginning of his rule.
The ceremony was attended by many princes, Brahmins, and foreign envoys.
Shivaji’s coronation was not for personal glory but to give Swaraj a firm footing.
The ceremony included music, singing, and the recitation of coronation mantras.
The golden canopy for the goddess Bhavani was presented by Shivaji after the ceremony.
Shivaji’s fame spread everywhere after the coronation.
The coronation day was considered the most auspicious day for the new king.
Shivaji’s coronation helped establish Swaraj as a recognized kingdom.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji Maharaj started a southern campaign to create a strong base against the Mughals.
He first visited Golconda, the capital of the Golconda Sultanate, where he was warmly welcomed by Sultan Abul Hasan Kutubshah.
The Sultan gave Shivaji a special throne and many gifts, showing respect for him as a king.
After Golconda, Shivaji went to the fort of Jinji on the east coast and captured it after a long siege.
He also tried to capture the fort of Vellore, but could not succeed and had to leave it.
Shivaji’s step‑brother Vyankoji Raje controlled the Tanjavur Jagir in the south and did not give Shivaji his share.
Shivaji wrote to Vyankoji and asked him to change his ways and help him in his campaign.
Shivaji’s southern campaign helped him gain control of many forts and a large territory with an annual revenue of about twenty lakhs.
Shivaji died on 3rd April 1680 at the age of fifty‑five, leaving a legacy of a powerful Maratha kingdom.
The capital of the Golconda Sultanate was the city of Golconda, a fortified town in present‑day Telangana.

subject: EVS Part 2
chapter: Administration of Forts and the Navy
notes: - A fort is a strong building used for defence.
- Shivaji Maharaj built many forts like Raigad, Rajgad, Pratapgad, Sindhudurg, Vijaydurg.
- Forts are of three types: forest forts, hill forts and sea forts.
- A sea fort is also called a coastal fort.
- Important people in fort management: Killedar (fort commander), Sabnis (account officer), Karkhanis (workers).
- Killedar protects the fort and gives orders.
- Sabnis keeps accounts and supplies food.
- Karkhanis build and maintain the fort and handle ammunition.
- Guns were used on forts; they were coated with wax to stop rust.
- Shivaji’s navy had warships made from local boats and used cannons and gunpowder.
- The navy protected the coast and helped Shivaji win battles.
- Shivaji was called the ‘Father of the Indian Navy’.
- He used spies to gather information before launching attacks.
- Guerilla tactics involve quick, unexpected attacks and use of forests and hill forts.
- Shivaji’s army respected women and did not drink alcohol.
- The Maratha navy made enemies like the English, Portuguese, Dutch and Siddis fear them.
- Management skills of Shivaji include planning, organisation, discipline and use of resources.
- Students can learn from Shivaji’s planning to organise their own work.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: • The Welfare State is a state that looks after the needs of its people – food, clothing and shelter.
• Shivaji Maharaj created a welfare state called Swaraj where people could live happily and safely.
• He divided his administration into eight departments and appointed a Minister for each – the Council of Eight Ministers.
• The ministers were responsible for Administration, Revenue, Defence, Religious Matters, Justice, Government Orders, Correspondence and Foreign Relations.
• Shivaji Maharaj protected the environment – he forbade cutting trees unless the owner gave permission and paid for it.
• He built water tanks, dams, bunds and canals so that forts and villages had enough water even in droughts.
• He encouraged trade by building ports, markets and a navy, and he levied taxes on imported goods to promote local trade.
• He was tolerant to all religions – he protected mosques, temples and churches and helped people who changed their faith.
• He gave special treatment to brave women like Mallamma Desai and honoured them with titles and new settlements.
• The welfare state is run by the people for the people, with confidence, self‑respect and patriotism.
• Good governance means justice, fairness, protection of nature and care for the poor and the needy.
• A welfare state provides free grain, water and medicine to those in need.
• The welfare state is a state that is run by the people, for the people and for the welfare of all.
• Shivaji Maharaj’s policies are examples of how a ruler can build a welfare state that protects people, nature and culture.
• The welfare state is a model for future governments to look after the well‑being of all citizens.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a welfare state as described in the chapter?
options: To provide for people's basic needs
quiz.explain: A welfare state ensures food, clothing, shelter and other necessities for its citizens.

quiz.explain: The council of eight ministers handled revenue, defence, religion, etc., but did not directly build schools.

Cut all trees for building forts
quiz.explain: He allowed cutting of teak and other useful trees with permission, but protected mango, jackfruit, etc.

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of water management by Shivaji Maharaj?
options: Building a dam near his village
quiz.explain: He built dams, bunds, canals and reservoirs to manage water.

quiz.q: What was the main reason Shivaji Maharaj levied higher taxes on imported salt?
quiz.explain: Higher taxes on imported salt made local salt cheaper, encouraging local trade.

quiz.q: Shivaji Maharaj’s attitude towards people of different religions was:
quiz.explain: He respected Muslims, Christians, Hindus and did not harm them.

quiz.q: Which of the following was a benefit of the ‘Jalyukt Shivar’ project?
quiz.explain: The project supplied water to drought‑affected peasants, helping them earn a living.

quiz.q: The Council of Eight Ministers was also known as:
quiz.explain: It was called the Council of Eight Ministers, also referred to as the Swaraj of People.

quiz.q: Which tree was explicitly protected from cutting in Shivaji Maharaj’s orders?
quiz.explain: Mango and jackfruit trees were protected because they do not grow quickly.

quiz.q: The main goal of Shivaji Maharaj’s environmental policies was to:
options: Protect the environment for future generations
quiz.explain: He aimed to preserve forests, water and other natural resources for future generations.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Sants are saints who taught equality and love for all people.
They came from different backgrounds – princes, farmers, women, and even people of lower castes.
They preached that no one is superior or inferior; everyone should be treated equally.
They sang devotional songs called keertans and abhangs to spread their messages.
Sant Namdeo was a great devotee of Vitthal and preached compassion, non‑violence and brotherhood.
Sant Dnyaneshwar wrote the Dnyaneshwari in Marathi, making religious knowledge accessible to common people.
Sant Eknath continued the work of Namdeo and Dnyaneshwar, teaching devotion (Bhaktimarg) and equality.
Sant Tukaram sang abhangs, performed keertans, and taught forgiveness, pity and peace of mind.
Samarth Ramdas wrote Dasbodh, a guide to good living and self‑reliance.
The saints’ songs and teachings are still sung and read in Maharashtra today.

quiz.explain: He preached equality and brotherhood.

quiz.explain: Sant Tukaram helped a poor child and died.

quiz.explain: Dasbodh is his guide to good living.

subject: EVS Part 2
chapter: Maratha Sardars – The Famous House of the Bhosales
notes: - Maratha Sardars were brave warriors who fought for their people.
- They had private armies and were often hired by sultans of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar.
- The Bhonsales of Verul were a famous Maratha family known for bravery and loyalty.
- Maloji Raje Bhonsale was a Patil of Verul and later received the Jagir of Pune and Supe from Nizamshah.
- His wife Umabai came from the House of Bijapur and helped him gain respect at the Adilshah court.
- Shahaji Raje was a brave general who served both Nizamshah and later the Adilshah before returning to Nizamshah.
- The temple of Ghrushneshwar near Verul was restored by the Jadhavs of Sindkhed, Nimbalkars of Phaltan, Ghorpades of Mudhol, Moreys of Javali, and Bhonsales of Verul.
- The Jadhavs of Sindkhed were descendants of the Yadavs of Devgiri and were known for repairing the temple.
- Malik Amber was a powerful Vazir (Chief Minister) of Nizamshah and was killed in battle by the Moghul emperor.
- The Maratha Sardars were also known for their devotion to Shiva, often visiting temples and offering flowers and prayers.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji was born in 1630 in Pune and was educated by his mother, Jijabai, and teachers sent by his father, Shahaji Raje.
Jijabai was a strong, wise woman who taught Shivaji values like courage, honesty and love for his people.
Shivaji began learning at age 7, studying Sanskrit, Marathi, Persian, and local languages.
He learned to read and write, and studied the great epics Ramayana, Mahabharata and Bhagavata.
Jijabai also taught him martial skills – riding, wrestling, sword‑fighting and strategy.
Shivaji’s teachers taught him about war tactics, administration, and the importance of good governance.
He learned to manage revenue, build forts, and protect his people from enemies like the Nizamshahi and Adilshah.
Jijabai’s example of bravery inspired Shivaji to fight injustice and protect the Maval people, who were hardworking and loyal.
Shivaji’s education helped him become a great leader who built the Maratha Empire and promoted Swaraj (self‑rule).

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji was a young prince who dreamed of a free India called Hindavi Swaraj.
He promised to fight for freedom and to stop fighting each other for land.
Shivaji gathered his friends at Raireshwar temple and made an oath to fight for Swaraj.
He trained his friends in sword fighting, riding, and learning the hills and forts.
Shivaji surveyed all forts and secret paths so he could protect his people.
He made a Royal Seal that said he would rule for the welfare of the people.
The seal was written in Sanskrit, showing respect for local culture.
Shivaji wanted to end quarrels among the Deshmukhs who fought over their lands.
He promised to give each Deshmukh a ‘Watan’ (land) to stop wasting money and soldiers.
Shivaji’s oath was a promise to give his life for freedom and to stop being a slave of the Sultan.

quiz.q: What was the main goal of Shivaji’s oath?

quiz.explain: He surveyed to know secret paths and protect his people.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji was a brave king who wanted Swaraj (self‑rule).
He lived when four powers ruled Maharashtra: the Mughals, the Bijapur Sultanate, the Portuguese, and the Siddi of Janjira.
Shivaji’s first big win was taking the fort of Torana in 1640. It was a natural hill fort with two strong walls called ‘Machis’.
The fort had a temple of the goddess Bhavani, who gave Shivaji a gift of pots filled with money and ammunition. This helped him start his own army.
After Torana, Shivaji captured many other forts: Rajgad, Pratapgad, Sinhagad, Shivneri, and many in the Maval region.
The first capital of his Swaraj was Rajgad, a fort he finished and used for administration.
Shivaji used clever tactics, good soldiers called Mavlas, and the help of local people from all castes. He treated everyone equally.
He sent a message to the Sultan of Bijapur saying he had taken possession of the fort and would not return it. The Sultan was surprised.
Shivaji’s army was small but brave; they could move fast and capture forts quickly.
The story of Torana shows how a strong fort can protect a king and give him power to rule.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shivaji first capture to start his Swaraj movement?
quiz.explain: Shivaji captured Torana fort first.

quiz.q: Who was the ruler of Bijapur that controlled many forts in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: Adilshah of Bijapur ruled the region.

quiz.q: What is a ‘Machi’ in the context of Shivaji’s forts?
quiz.explain: A ‘Machi’ refers to a group of Shivaji’s soldiers.

quiz.q: Which goddess is associated with blessings that helped Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Goddess Bhavani is credited with blessings.

quiz.q: What was the first capital of Shivaji’s Swaraj?
quiz.explain: Rajgad became the first capital.

quiz.q: Which fort was left unfinished by Adilshah and later completed by Shivaji?
quiz.explain: Adilshah left Rajgad unfinished.

quiz.q: What did Shivaji use the pots of mohurs for?
quiz.explain: The pots were used to buy arms.

quiz.q: Which group of people were called Mavlas?
quiz.explain: Mavlas were soldiers in Shivaji’s army.

quiz.q: Which hill is known as the ‘Zunjar Machi’?
quiz.explain: Zunjar Machi refers to Torana fort.

quiz.q: What was the main reason Shivaji chose Torana fort?
quiz.explain: Torana’s strategic location made it ideal.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Shivaji was a brave king who fought for his land called Swaraj.
The Mavlas were people who lived in forests and helped Shivaji.
Morey was a leader of the Mavlas and fought against Shivaji at first.
Shivaji used force and clever plans to defeat enemies inside his own country.
He captured forts like Raigad and Pratapgad to protect his kingdom.
After winning, he gave titles and tribute to those who helped him.
He punished those who betrayed him, like Morey and Yeshwantrao.
Sambhaji Mohite of Supe tried to attack Shivaji but was arrested and sent away.
Shivaji’s main goal was to keep his people safe and keep the kingdom united.
He was known for being fair and giving rewards to loyal soldiers.
The conquest of Javali was a big victory because it added new forts to Swaraj.
Raigad was a strong fort surrounded by forest and water, making it hard to attack.
Shivaji changed the name of the fort to Raigad after conquering it.
He made sure that people who wanted to be king had to give up their claims.
Shivaji’s leadership showed that duty to the country is more important than family ties.
He taught that a king should listen to his people and protect them from danger.
The story shows how Shivaji used both force and kindness to win battles.
It also shows that enemies inside the kingdom can be defeated by good planning.
Shivaji’s victories helped spread the idea of a free and safe land.
The chapter teaches that courage, loyalty and fairness are important values for a king.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shivaji conquer that became a landmark for Swaraj?

quiz.explain: It added new forts to Swaraj.

quiz.q: What was Shivaji’s main goal in fighting?
quiz.explain: He fought to protect his people.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: Pratapgad is a fort in Maharashtra where Shivaji Maharaj fought Afzal Khan.
Afzal Khan was a powerful commander from Bijapur who wanted Shivaji captured alive or dead.
Shivaji moved his base from Rajgad to Pratapgad to stay away from the plains and make it hard for Afzal Khan to attack.
Afzal Khan sent a friendly message to Shivaji, saying he would give him a Sardar title if he returned the forts.
Shivaji refused to leave Pratapgad and used clever tactics to avoid open battle with Afzal Khan.
He divided his army into small units and kept them hidden in the forest and hills.
During the meeting, Shivaji used a dagger to stab Afzal Khan, killing him while the Khan was trying to attack him.
After Afzal Khan’s death, the Bijapur army was defeated and Shivaji’s fame spread across the hills.
Pratapgad is famous for its strong walls, thick forest, and high hills that protect it from enemy attacks.
Shivaji’s strategy was to use surprise and terrain advantage rather than direct confrontation.
The story shows Shivaji’s bravery, intelligence, and his ability to protect his people.

quiz.explain: Shivaji shifted his base to Pratapgad.

quiz.explain: Shivaji stayed because the plains were dangerous for his forces.

quiz.explain: Afzal Khan sent a friendly message offering friendship.

quiz.q: Which weapon did Shivaji use to stab Afzal Khan?
quiz.explain: Shivaji stabbed the Khan with a dagger.

quiz.q: What was the name of Shivaji's ceremonial sword?
quiz.explain: The sword was called Dandpatta.

quiz.q: What did Afzal Khan do to try to capture Shivaji?
quiz.explain: He attacked the plains to lure Shivaji out.

quiz.q: Which Marathi proverb was associated with Shivaji's cleverness?
quiz.explain: The proverb ‘Kale Gadhi’ reflects Shivaji’s cunning.

quiz.q: What was the main reason Shivaji used strategic moves?
quiz.explain: Shivaji avoided open battle because his army was smaller.

quiz.q: What happened to Afzal Khan after the encounter?
quiz.explain: Afzal Khan was killed by Shivaji.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: पुरंदर हा एक महत्त्वाचा किल्ला होता ज्यावर मुघलांनी वेढा घातला.
शिवरायांनी १६६५ साली पुरंदरचा तह केला ज्यात मुघलांना काही किल्ले आणि मुलूख देण्याचे मान्य केले.
मुरारबाजी हा पुरंदरचा किल्लेदार होता आणि तो अतिशय धैर्यवान व जिद्दी होता.
दिलेरखान हे मुघलांचे सेनापती होते आणि त्यांनी पुरंदरवर वेढा घातला.
मुरारबाजीने दिलेरखानाला आव्हान दिले आणि त्याच्या शौर्याने मुरारबाजीची प्रसिद्धी वाढली.
पुरंदरच्या तहानंतर मुघलांनी माघार घेतली आणि शिवरायांना काही किल्ले मिळाली.
शिवरायांनी जयसिंगाला बादशाहाच्या भेटीसाठी पाठवले.
पुरंदरचा तह १६६५ साली झाला.
मुरारबाजीने दिलेरखानाला सांगितले की तो शिवरायांची माणसे आहेत.
मुरारबाजीने दिलेरखानाला दिलेल्या उत्तरात त्याने शिवरायांची निष्ठा दाखवली.
पुरंदरचा वेढा आणि तह हे मराठ्यांच्या स्वराज्याच्या इतिहासात महत्त्वाचे आहेत.

शिवरायांनी मुघलांना काही किल्ले आणि मुलूख दिले.

मुरारबाजीचे शौर्य आणि दिलेरखानाची लढाई मराठ्यांच्या आत्मविश्वासाला बळकटी दिली.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: गड म्हणजे किल्ला, ज्याला रक्षण आणि आक्रमण दोन्ही करता येते.
गड आला पण सिंह गेला या कथेत तानाजी आणि सूर्याजी यांनी कोंढाणा किल्ला जिंकला.
कोंढाणा किल्ला मुघलांच्या ताब्यात होता, परंतु शिवरायांनी तो परत घेतला.
शिवरायांनी कोंढाणा घेण्यासाठी योजना आखली आणि तानाजीने चढाई केली.
तानाजीने किल्ल्यावर चढताना उभ्या दगडावरून उडी मारली आणि शत्रूला पराभूत केले.
सूर्याजीने तानाजीच्या मदतीने किल्ल्याचा दरवाजा उघडला.
गड जिंकताना शत्रूच्या मावळ्यांना पराभूत केले.
साहस आणि धैर्य हे या कथेत महत्त्वाचे गुण आहेत.
किल्ल्याचे दरवाजे दोन असतात – कल्याण दरवाजा आणि दुसरा दरवाजा.
गडात शत्रूची तलवार आणि ढाल यांची लढाई झाली.
साहसिक कथा वाचताना आपण धैर्य आणि योजना करण्याचे महत्त्व समजतो.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: गडकोट म्हणजे किल्ला, ज्याची उभारणी शिवरायांनी केली.
शिवरायांचे व्यवस्थापन कौशल्य म्हणजे ध्येय साध्य करण्यासाठी शिस्तबद्ध पद्धतीने काम करणे.
किल्ल्यांवर किल्लेदार, सबनीस आणि कारखानीस हे अधिकारी असत.
किल्लेदार गडाचे संरक्षण व कारभार करतो.
सबनीस गडावरील जमाखर्चाचा हिशोब ठेवतो आणि गडातील लोकांना धान्य व वस्तू पुरवतो.
कारखानीस तोफ आणि दारूगोळ्याची व्यवस्था करतो.
गडांमध्ये तोफांना गंजू नये म्हणून मेणाचा लेप लावला जात असे.
शिवरायांनी जलदुर्ग, वनदुर्ग आणि गिरिदुर्ग असे तीन प्रकारचे किल्ले बांधले.
आरमार म्हणजे युद्धनौकांचा समूह, शिवरायांनी स्वतःचा आरमार उभा केला.
आरमारात गुराब, गलबत, पाल, मचवा, नाव, होडी अशी जहाजे होती.
सिंधुदुर्ग किल्ला आणि प्रतापगड हे प्रसिद्ध किल्ले आहेत.

subject: EVS Part 2
notes: संत म्हणजे आध्यात्मिक गुरू ज्यांनी समाजाला समता, दया, अहिंसा शिकवली.
संतांची कामगिरी म्हणजे समाजात समतेचा संदेश पसरवणे आणि भेदभाव नाकारणे.
संत नामदेव हे निस्सीम भक्त होते ज्यांनी दया आणि परोपकाराचे उदाहरण दिले.
संत ज्ञानेश्वर यांनी मराठी भाषेत भजन आणि अभंग रचले आणि सर्वांना समतेचा संदेश दिला.
संत एकनाथ यांनी लहान मुलांना मदत करून समतेची भावना पसरवली.
संत तुकाराम यांनी कर्जमुक्ती, दया, क्षमा आणि शांती शिकवली.
संत रामदास यांनी लोकांना संघटित होऊन अन्यायाविरुद्ध लढण्यास प्रेरित केले.
संतांची कामगिरी म्हणजे लोकांच्या मनात समतेची आणि दयाळूपणाची भावना रुजवणे.
संतांनी सर्व जाती-धर्मांना समान मानले आणि भेदभाव नाकारला.
संतांच्या उपदेशाने समाजात धार्मिक सहिष्णुता आणि एकात्मता वाढली.

quiz.explain: तुकारामांनी इंद्रायू नदीमध्ये कर्जमुक्त करून दया दाखवली.

quiz.q: संत नामदेव यांनी कोणत्या प्रकारची भक्ति रचली?

quiz.q: संत एकनाथ यांनी कोणत्या प्रकारचे कर्ज दिले?
quiz.explain: संत एकनाथ यांनी कर्जमुक्तीची शिकवण दिली.

quiz.q: संत तुकाराम यांनी कोणत्या प्राण्यांना दया दाखवली?
quiz.explain: संत तुकाराम यांनी सर्व प्राण्यांवर दया दाखवली.

quiz.q: संत रामदास यांनी कोणत्या प्रकारचे संदेश दिले?
quiz.explain: संत रामदास यांनी सामाजिक समता आणि प्रतिकाराचा संदेश दिला.

subject: English
notes: - Back to School is a poem about the excitement of the first day of school.
- The poem talks about new clothes, books, friends and the teacher’s smile.
- It mentions learning, singing, playing and having fun.
- The teacher encourages us to read, write and enjoy school activities.
- The poem ends with a question: "How about you?" to share feelings with classmates.
- The chapter also includes activities like listening, repeating, naming pictures and solving riddles.
- Riddles describe common school items: a bookcase, a clock, a chair and a globe.
- Students are encouraged to make lists of things they receive on the first day.
- The teacher’s role is to create a friendly, bright learning environment.
- The poem and activities help students practice listening, speaking, reading and writing skills.

subject: English
notes: - A word family is a group of words that share the same root word.
- The root word is the main part that gives the meaning of the word.
- Adding prefixes or suffixes to the root changes the meaning but keeps the root the same.
- Syllables are parts of a word that are spoken together; you can split a word into syllables by listening to its sounds.
- Example: 'kingdom' has two syllables: king – dom.
- Example: 'competition' has four syllables: com – pe – ti – tion.
- Words in a word family can be nouns, verbs, adjectives, or adverbs.
- Sorting words into boxes helps you see which words are actions, qualities, or objects.
- Writing sentences with words from a word family helps you use the words correctly.
- Remember to use the root word correctly when making new words (e.g., 'freeze' is a verb, 'frozen' is an adjective).

quiz.q: Which of the following words is a verb in the word family?
quiz.explain: Freeze is an action word (verb).

quiz.q: How many syllables are in the word 'competition'?
quiz.explain: Competition is split as com – pe – ti – tion (4 syllables).

quiz.q: Which word is a noun that represents a place?
quiz.explain: Kingdom is a place (noun).

quiz.q: Choose the word that means 'to feel happy'.
quiz.explain: Cheer means to feel happy or to give encouragement.

quiz.q: Which word is an adjective that describes honesty?
quiz.explain: Honest is the adjective form of honesty.

quiz.q: What is the root word in 'freeze'?
quiz.explain: The root is 'free'; 'freeze' is a verb form.

quiz.q: Which word is a noun that refers to a small stone?
quiz.explain: Pebble is a small stone.

quiz.q: Which word means a group of people competing?
quiz.explain: Competition is a group of people competing.

quiz.q: Which word is a verb that means to make someone feel excited?
quiz.explain: Excite is the verb meaning to make excited.

quiz.q: Which word is a noun that represents a type of bird sound?
quiz.explain: Quack is the sound a duck makes.

subject: English
notes: - A rhyme is a short poem that has words that sound the same at the end.
- In this poem the rhyme keeps changing into different things.
- The poem shows how a rhyme can be playful and imaginative.
- Key words: rhyme, caught, floor, bicycle, icicle, hat, cat, tail, whale, boat, goat, tin, paper, skyscraper, kite, sight.
- The poem ends with the rhyme flying away, showing freedom.
- Rhyming pairs in the poem: rhyme/​time, floor/​door, bicycle/​icicle, hat/cat, tail/​whale, boat/goat, tin/paper, skyscraper/kite, sight/out.
- The poem encourages listening, repeating and singing.
- Students should identify rhyming words and think of their own rhymes.
- Opposite words: in – out, tall – short, melt – freeze, little – big.
- Fill‑in‑the‑blanks help practice word order and meaning.

quiz.q: What does the rhyme become after being fed tin and paper?
quiz.explain: It becomes a tall skyscraper.

quiz.q: Which of these pairs is a rhyming pair from the poem?
quiz.explain: Hat and cat rhyme; the others do not.

quiz.q: What is the main activity the poet does with the rhyme?
quiz.explain: The poet catches the rhyme.

quiz.q: Which word best describes the rhyme after it grows?
quiz.explain: It grows into a tall kite.

quiz.q: The rhyme runs to which place?
quiz.explain: It runs out the door.

quiz.q: Which word is NOT an opposite of "in"?
quiz.explain: Inside is not the opposite of in.

subject: English
notes: - Raghu Kaka delivers fresh milk from his farm to houses in the town.
- Milk can be used to make curd, butter, ghee, ice cream and masala buttermilk.
- Cows and buffaloes give milk every day.
- A simple masala buttermilk recipe: 1 cup curd, 1 cup water, salt, cumin powder, grated ginger, chopped coriander leaves, stir well.
- Milk is good for health: keeps you strong and healthy.
- Conversation shows how to ask about daily activities and show gratitude.
- Key words: milk, curd, butter, ghee, ice cream, masala buttermilk, farm, cows, buffaloes, cans, deliver, fresh.
- Remember to say “Good morning” and “Thank you” politely.
- Use polite questions: “How are you?” “Did you bring fresh milk?”

subject: English
notes: Maharashtra Day is celebrated on 1st May every year.
The state of Maharashtra was established on 1st May 1960.
Maharashtra Day is also called Kamgar Din (Labour Day).
On Labour Day we thank all workers like factory workers, drivers, cleaners, etc.
The flag of Maharashtra (Tiranga) is unfurled on Maharashtra Day.
The state song of Maharashtra is called Rajyageet.
Maharashtra is known for its rich culture, heritage, delicious food, and folk songs.
Mumbai is the capital city of Maharashtra and is called the Financial Capital of India.
Neighbouring states of Maharashtra are Gujarat, Karnataka, Telangana, and Goa.
The national flag (Tiranga) is also unfurled in schools on Maharashtra Day.
Maharashtra Day is a day of pride and joy for people of the state.
The day reminds us of the dignity of labour and the importance of workers.
Children’s Day is celebrated on 1st November.
Teachers’ Day is celebrated on 5th September.
Republic Day is celebrated on 26th January.
Independence Day is celebrated on 15th August.
Science Day is celebrated on 28th February.
The flag of India is also unfurled on Republic Day.
Maharashtra Day is a public holiday in the state.
People write slogans and poems to celebrate Maharashtra Day.
Students can write about their favourite food, sportsperson, festival, and science topics.

quiz.q: When is Maharashtra Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: Maharashtra Day is celebrated on 1st May.

quiz.q: What is Maharashtra Day also known as?
quiz.explain: It is also called Kamgar Din or Labour Day.

quiz.q: Who is thanked on Labour Day?
quiz.explain: Labour Day thanks factory workers, drivers, cleaners, etc.

quiz.q: Which city is the capital of Maharashtra?

quiz.q: Which flag is unfurled on Maharashtra Day?
quiz.explain: The Maharashtra flag (Tiranga) is unfurled.

quiz.explain: It celebrates pride in Maharashtra.

quiz.q: What is the main message of Labour Day?
quiz.explain: Labour Day reminds us to respect workers.

quiz.explain: Children’s Day is on 1st November.

subject: English
notes: - Teddy is a soft toy that can be lost and found.
- A little girl and her father waited for a bus at the bus stop.
- The girl forgot her teddy on the bench when she boarded the bus.
- A kind lady saw the teddy and put it on a book so it was visible.
- Three naughty boys played with the teddy and its arm came off.
- The boys sewed the arm back on the teddy.
- A lady with two children came, asked to take the teddy, but the lady said it belonged to someone else.
- The children left a small candy for the teddy.
- Many people saw the teddy waiting all day.
- The next morning the teddy was gone, but a note was left on the bench.
- The note thanked everyone for their kindness and said the teddy’s arm felt better.
- The story teaches kindness, caring for others’ belongings, and the importance of returning lost items.
- Key vocabulary: bus stop, teddy bear, kind, owner, sewed, candy, lost, found, note.
- The sequence of events: waiting → forgetting → lady finds → boys play → arm breaks → boys sew → lady with children → candy → waiting all day → teddy gone → note left.
- The story shows that people can help each other even if they don’t know the owner.
- The note is a way to thank those who helped.
- The teddy’s arm was fixed by sewing, showing how small acts help.
- The story can be used to practice reading, writing, and speaking skills.
- It also helps students learn about empathy and responsibility.

quiz.q: Who was waiting for the bus in the morning?
options: A little girl and her father
quiz.explain: The story starts with a little girl and her father waiting at the bus stop.

quiz.q: What did the girl forget on the bench?
quiz.explain: She forgot her soft teddy bear on the bench.

quiz.q: Who first saw the teddy on the bench?
quiz.explain: The kind lady came to the bus stop and saw the teddy.

quiz.q: What happened to the teddy’s arm?
quiz.explain: The boys played with the teddy and its arm came off.

quiz.q: How did the boys fix the teddy?
quiz.explain: They carefully sewed the arm back on the teddy.

quiz.q: What did the lady with two children leave for the teddy?
quiz.explain: They left a small candy for the teddy.

quiz.q: What did the next morning find?
options: The teddy was on a tree
The teddy was on a bus
quiz.explain: The next morning the teddy was gone.

quiz.q: What was left on the bench after the teddy was gone?
quiz.explain: A short note was left on the bench.

quiz.q: What did the note thank the people for?
quiz.explain: The note thanked them for keeping the teddy safe.

quiz.q: What does the story teach about kindness?
options: It is the same as sharing
quiz.explain: The story shows that being kind helps others.

subject: English
chapter: From the Sugarcane to Sweet Gold
notes: - Sugarcane is a tall plant grown in fields.
- Farmers cut sugarcane when it is ready for harvest.
- The cut cane is taken to a jaggery‑making place called Gurhal.
- In Gurhal a big machine crushes the cane to get sweet juice.
- The juice is poured into a big iron pan and heated over fire.
- While heating, the juice thickens and turns brown, becoming jaggery.
- Workers stir the juice to help it cook evenly.
- The thickened jaggery is poured into small moulds to set.
- After cooling, jaggery blocks are ready for use.
- Jaggery is a natural sweetener used in many Indian dishes.
- The process shows how a plant becomes a sweet food.
- The story of Rajveer shows how children learn by watching.
- Jaggery is famous in Maharashtra and is used in tea and sweets.
- The process involves crushing, heating, stirring, and moulding.
- Understanding the steps helps students see science in everyday life.

quiz.q: What is the first step after sugarcane is ready for harvest?
quiz.explain: Farmers cut the cane when it is ready.

quiz.q: Where is the jaggery‑making place called?
quiz.explain: The place is called Gurhal.

quiz.q: What happens to the juice when it is heated?
quiz.explain: Heating makes the juice thick and brown.

quiz.q: What is poured into moulds after the juice thickens?
quiz.explain: The thickened juice becomes jaggery and is poured into moulds.

quiz.q: Which animal is mentioned as helping to carry sugarcane?
quiz.explain: Bullock-cart is used to carry cane.

quiz.q: What does Rajveer call the jaggery?
quiz.explain: He says it is a magic.

quiz.q: Who uses jaggery in tea?
quiz.explain: His grandmother uses jaggery in tea.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT part of the jaggery process?
quiz.explain: Boiling water is not mentioned.

quiz.q: What is the main ingredient of jaggery?
quiz.explain: Jaggery comes from sugarcane juice.

quiz.q: Why does the teacher suggest visiting a Gurhal?
quiz.explain: To see how jaggery is made.

subject: English
notes: • ‘Thank you’ is said when someone gives or helps you.
• ‘Please’ is used when you want something politely.
• ‘Excuse me’ is said before you interrupt or when you sneeze.
• ‘Sorry’ is said when you hurt someone or make a mistake.
• Saying these words shows good manners and kindness.
• We use ‘Thank you’ after receiving help or a gift.
• We use ‘Please’ before asking for something.
• ‘Excuse me’ can mean ‘Sorry’ or ‘Pardon me’ when we bump into someone.
• ‘Sorry’ is used when we do something wrong.
• Good manners make friends and keep peace.
• When you help a friend tie shoelaces, you show kindness.
• A small help can make someone’s day better.
• Listening kindly and speaking politely keeps relationships strong.
• Polite words are called ‘magic words’ because they make people happy.
• We can pair a word with a picture to remember its meaning.
• We can create short poems or posters to practice polite words.

quiz.q: Which word is used when you want something politely?
quiz.explain: Please is used before asking for something.

quiz.q: What should you say when you sneeze?
quiz.explain: Excuse me is used before or after a sneeze.

quiz.q: If you accidentally bump into someone, what do you say?
quiz.explain: Sorry is used when you hurt someone.

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym for ‘kind’?
quiz.explain: Helpful is a synonym for kind.

quiz.q: What do you do when you see a friend struggling to tie shoelaces?
quiz.explain: Helping shows kindness.

quiz.q: Which word means ‘to give a small gift’?
quiz.explain: Thank you is said after receiving a gift.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of ‘big’?
quiz.explain: Small is the opposite of big.

quiz.q: When you want to borrow a toy, which phrase do you use?
quiz.explain: The phrase asks for borrowing a toy.

quiz.q: Which word means ‘to make someone happy’?
quiz.explain: Happiness is the feeling of being happy.

quiz.q: If you forget to bring a book to class, what should you do?
options: Ask a friend for the book
quiz.explain: Asking a friend for the book is polite.

subject: English
notes: The giant panda is a very rare animal found only in the mountains of Western China and Tibet.
It lives in bamboo forests at high altitudes.
Its favourite food is bamboo – about 99 % of its diet.
A panda can eat 12–38 kilograms of bamboo each day.
Pandas have strong jaws and teeth to crush bamboo stalks.
Adult pandas weigh 70–100 kilograms, sometimes more.
A baby panda is called a cub and weighs about 100 grams at birth.
Pandas are slow‑moving, peaceful and friendly animals.
They are a symbol of peace and friendship in China.
Pandas spend most of their day eating and resting.
Only a few pandas remain in the world, so we must protect forests for them and other animals.

quiz.q: Where do giant pandas live?
quiz.explain: They live in bamboo forests in the mountains.

quiz.q: What makes up 99% of a panda’s diet?
quiz.explain: Bamboo is the main food of pandas.

quiz.q: How much bamboo can a panda eat in one day?
quiz.explain: The range given is 12–38 kilograms.

quiz.q: What is a baby panda called?
quiz.explain: A baby panda is called a cub.

quiz.q: Which of the following best describes pandas?
quiz.explain: Pandas are slow‑moving and peaceful.

quiz.q: Pandas are symbols of what?
quiz.explain: They symbolize peace and friendship.

quiz.q: What is the typical adult weight of a panda?
quiz.explain: Adults usually weigh 70–100 kg.

quiz.q: Pandas spend most of their day doing which two activities?
quiz.explain: They mainly eat and rest.

quiz.q: Which mountain ranges are home to pandas?
quiz.explain: Pandas are found in Western China and Tibet.

quiz.q: Why should we protect forests for pandas?
quiz.explain: Protecting forests helps pandas and other animals survive.

subject: English
notes: True friends are people who help each other without asking for anything in return.
A best friend is someone you trust, share secrets with, and spend time together.
Honesty means telling the truth and being fair to others.
Friendship is shown by sharing, caring, and being honest.
In the story, Gopi and Krishna were good friends and neighbours.
Krishna’s crops were ruined by heavy rains, showing how nature can hurt farmers.
Gopi lent land to Krishna so he could grow crops, showing kindness.
Krishna found a golden statue while tilling the land.
The king listened to the friends and decided to buy the statue.
Tenali Raman suggested using the money to help poor farmers.
A monument can remember a good friendship for everyone.
The moral of the story is that honesty and friendship are very important.
When friends face problems, they should help each other and be honest.
A good friend is always ready to share his land, time, or money if needed.
True friends respect each other’s property and do not keep it for themselves.

quiz.q: What did Gopi and Krishna do for each other in the story?
quiz.explain: The story says Gopi and Krishna were friends as well as neighbours.

quiz.q: Why did Krishna’s crops get ruined?
quiz.explain: The text mentions Krishna’s crops were ruined by heavy rains.

quiz.q: What did Krishna find in the field?
quiz.explain: Krishna found a precious golden statue.

quiz.q: Who suggested buying the statue at a fair price?
quiz.explain: Tenali Raman suggested buying it at a worthy price.

quiz.q: What did the king decide to do with the money from the statue?
options: Send it to the king’s treasury
quiz.explain: The king used the money to help peasants like Krishna.

quiz.q: What is the moral of the story?
quiz.explain: The story teaches about honesty and friendship.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT true about the story?
options: Gopi kept the statue for himself
Krishna wanted to give the statue to Gopi
The king ignored the farmers' problem
Tenali Raman gave a wise suggestion
quiz.explain: Gopi did not keep the statue; he offered it to the king.

quiz.q: What did Tenali Raman propose to do with the statue?
options: Buy it at a fair price
quiz.explain: Tenali Raman suggested buying it at a fair price.

quiz.q: Which word best describes the relationship between Gopi and Krishna?
quiz.explain: They were friends as well as neighbours.

quiz.q: What did the king do with the statue after buying it?
options: He kept it in his palace
He erected a pillar in its honor
He sold it to a foreign king
He buried it in the ground
quiz.explain: The king erected a pillar as a timeless monument for their friendship.

subject: English
notes: - Eating healthy food keeps the body strong and happy.
- Fruits and vegetables are full of vitamins that help you grow and stay fit.
- Milk is good for bones and teeth and gives energy for play.
- Eating too many sweets can upset the stomach and make you feel tired.
- Water is essential; drink enough every day to stay active.
- Resting well helps the body recover and keeps the mind sharp.
- Healthy foods include carrots, tomatoes, apples, bananas, sprouts, lentils, rice, roti, eggs, fish, and milk.
- A balanced meal should have at least two servings of grains and vegetables.

notes: - Conversation starters are simple questions that help people start talking.

subject: English
notes: - A word family is a group of words that share the same root or base word.
- Words in a word family can be nouns, verbs, adjectives, etc.
- Example: the root word "giant" can lead to "giant" (noun), "gigantic" (adj).
- Some words in the list are action words (verbs) like chase, stretch, melt, deliver, hug, pour, sew, crush.
- Some words describe nature: sugarcane, ginger, jaggery, mountain.
- One-syllable words are short and easy to remember: chase, stretch, melt, hug, pour, sew, crush, giant, rare, jaw, peace, symbol, capital, pride, brave, celebrate, vitamin.
- Opposites help you understand meaning: brave ↔ fearful, giant ↔ tiny, rare ↔ common, peace ↔ war, excite ↔ calm.
- Practice by making lists, finding odd ones out, and circling one-syllable words.
- Remember: a word family helps you learn many words from one root.
- Use the word family to improve reading, writing, and speaking skills.
- Keep a notebook of new word families and review them regularly.
- Try to use new words in sentences to remember them better.
- The word "sugarcane" is a plant, "ginger" is a spice, "jaggery" is a sweetener.
- "Mould" and "mold" are the same word spelled differently in UK and US.
- "Specimen" is a sample, "extinct" means no longer existing.
- "Capital" can mean a city or money, but here it means city.
- "Symbol" represents an idea, like a peace sign.
- "Vitamin" is a nutrient that keeps you healthy.
- "Celebrate" means to honor or enjoy a special day.

subject: English
notes: - Birds have three kinds of feathers: down (warmth), body (cover), flight (help flying).
- All birds are warm‑blooded and have two feet.
- Birds have wings; most can fly, but penguins and ostriches cannot.
- A bird’s body is light and shaped like an aeroplane, with strong muscles and light bones.
- Beaks are used to cut, open, tear, and crush food; they have no teeth.
- Birds have three toes forward and one toe backward, used for walking, holding, balancing, climbing, swimming, and wading.
- Birds build nests in trees, walls, or on the ground; the female sits on eggs to keep them warm.
- After hatching, baby birds are blind and featherless; parents feed and care for them.
- Migration is the yearly journey to warmer places to find food and then return to build nests.
- Penguins live in cold places, swim well, and walk/slide on ice.
- Ostriches live in hot places, are the heaviest and largest birds, and run fast on land.
- Claws are used for different purposes: ducks swim, eagles catch prey, cranes walk in water, hens scratch ground, woodpeckers climb trees.
- An Arctic Tern can travel about 35,000 km in a year, almost around the Earth.
