१२ = १+१०+१, म्हणजे एक आणि दहा आणि एक.
१३ = दहा + तीन, किंवा एककात ३ आणि दहाकडे १.
१४ = दहा + चार, एककात ४ आणि दहाकडे १.
१५ = दहा + पाच, एककात ५ आणि दहाकडे १.
१६ = दहा + सहा, एककात ६ आणि दहाकडे १.
१७ = दहा + सात, एककात ७ आणि दहाकडे १.
१८ = दहा + आठ, एककात ८ आणि दहाकडे १.
१९ = दहा + नऊ, एककात ९ आणि दहाकडे १.
२० = दोन दहाकडे, एककात शून्य.
एककातील संख्या १‑९ आणि दहाकडे १ किंवा २ यांचे जोडणे हे ११‑२० चे लेखन पद्धत आहे.
संख्या वाचताना दहाकडे आधी वाचतो, नंतर एकक वाचतो (उदा. १७ – ‘सतर’).
संख्या लिहिताना दहाकडे ‘१’ आणि एककातील अंक लिहितो (उदा. १७ – ‘१७’).
संख्या ओळखताना अंक आणि शब्द दोन्ही स्वरूपात ओळखणे महत्त्वाचे आहे.
संख्या ११‑२० मध्ये ‘दहा’ हा शब्द वारंवार येतो, त्यामुळे त्याची ओळख मजबूत करावी.
संख्या ११‑२० चे क्रमाने सराव केल्याने पुढील दहाकडे (३०, ४० इ.) सोपे होते.

quiz.q: ११ हा अंक काय दर्शवितो?
quiz.explain: ११ = दहाकडे १ + एककात १.

quiz.q: संख्या १५ चे शब्दरूप काय आहे?
quiz.explain: १५ = दहा + पाच, शब्दरूप ‘पंधरा’.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणती संख्या २० पेक्षा मोठी नाही?
quiz.explain: १९ ही २० पेक्षा कमी आहे; इतर संख्या २० पेक्षा जास्त आहेत.

quiz.q: संख्या १७ चा अंक स्वरूप काय आहे?
quiz.explain: १७ हा अंक स्वरूपात १७ असे लिहितात.

quiz.q: संख्या १४ मध्ये किती दहाकडे आहेत?
quiz.explain: १४ मध्ये दहाकडे १ (१०) आहे, उरलेले ४ एककात.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणती संख्या ११‑२० च्या गटात नाही?
quiz.explain: २२ हा २० पेक्षा जास्त आहे, इतर सर्व ११‑२० मध्ये आहेत.

quiz.q: संख्या १९ चे शब्दरूप काय आहे?
quiz.explain: १९ चे शब्दरूप ‘एकोणिस’ आहे.

quiz.q: संख्या १२ मध्ये एककात किती अंक आहे?
quiz.explain: १२ मध्ये एककात २ आहे.

quiz.q: खालीलपैकी कोणती संख्या ११‑२० मध्ये दहाकडे २ असते?
quiz.explain: २० मध्ये दहाकडे २ (२०) आहे; इतरांमध्ये दहाकडे १ आहे.

quiz.q: संख्या १८ चे शब्दरूप काय आहे?
quiz.explain: १८ = दहा + आठ, शब्दरूप ‘अठरा’.

subject: Maths
chapter: लगतची पुढची, लगतची मागची व मधली संख्या
notes: लगतची पुढची संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्येच्या उजवीकडील संख्या.
लगतची मागची संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्येच्या डावीकडील संख्या.
मधली संख्या म्हणजे दोन संख्यांच्या मध्ये येणारी संख्या.
उदाहरण: ५ च्या लगतची पुढची संख्या ६ आहे.
उदाहरण: ५ च्या लगतची मागची संख्या ४ आहे.
उदाहरण: ३ आणि ५ यांच्या मधली संख्या ४ आहे.
१ आणि २ यांच्या मधली संख्या १.५ नाही, कारण १ आणि २ मध्ये फक्त १ संख्या नाही; त्यामुळे मधली संख्या फक्त दोन सलग संख्यांमध्येच असते.
१ ते २० पर्यंतच्या संख्यांसाठी हे नियम लागू होतात.
संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवण्यासाठी तालिका काढणे उपयुक्त ठरते.
संकल्पना समजण्यासाठी लहान खेळ खेळू शकतो.
वर्गात एकमेकांना प्रश्न विचारून सराव करणे चांगले.
संकल्पना समजल्यावर गणिताच्या इतर भागातही मदत होते.
कधी कधी ० किंवा १ सारख्या संख्यांसाठी लगतची संख्या नसते, ते लक्षात ठेवा.
संकल्पना शिकताना चित्रे आणि तक्ते वापरा.
संकल्पना समजल्यावर विद्यार्थ्यांना स्वतःची तक्ता तयार करण्यास प्रोत्साहित करा.
संकल्पना शिकताना शब्दांची स्पष्टता राखा.
संकल्पना समजण्यासाठी दैनंदिन जीवनातील उदाहरणे द्या.
संकल्पना शिकताना प्रश्नांची पुनरावृत्ती करा.
संकल्पना समजल्यावर विद्यार्थ्यांना स्वतःचे प्रश्न तयार करण्यास सांगा.
संकल्पना शिकताना शिक्षकाने स्पष्ट बोलणे आवश्यक आहे.
संकल्पना शिकताना विद्यार्थ्यांना उत्तर लिहिण्यास सांगणे उपयुक्त ठरते.

quiz.q: १ च्या लगतची पुढची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: १ च्या उजवीकडील संख्या २ आहे.

quiz.q: ४ च्या लगतची मागची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: ४ च्या डावीकडील संख्या ३ आहे.

quiz.q: २ आणि ४ यांच्या मधली संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: २ आणि ४ यांच्या मध्ये ३ येते.

quiz.q: ५ च्या लगतची मागची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: ५ च्या डावीकडील संख्या ४ आहे.

quiz.q: ७ च्या लगतची पुढची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: ७ च्या उजवीकडील संख्या ८ आहे.

quiz.q: ९ आणि ११ यांच्या मधली संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: ९ आणि ११ यांच्या मध्ये १० येते.

quiz.q: १० च्या लगतची मागची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: १० च्या डावीकडील संख्या ९ आहे.

quiz.q: १५ च्या लगतची पुढची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: १५ च्या उजवीकडील संख्या १६ आहे.

quiz.q: १ आणि ३ यांच्या मधली संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: १ आणि ३ यांच्या मध्ये २ येते.

quiz.q: १२ च्या लगतची मागची संख्या कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: १२ च्या डावीकडील संख्या ११ आहे.

subject: Maths
notes: संख्या म्हणजे मोजमापाचे चिन्ह

subject: Maths
notes: चढता क्रम म्हणजे लहान ते मोठा असा क्रम
उतरता क्रम म्हणजे मोठा ते लहान असा क्रम
संख्या लिहिताना सर्वांत लहान संख्या आधी, सर्वांत मोठी नंतर लिहायची
उदाहरण: २, ५, ३ या संख्यांचा चढता क्रम २, ३, ५ असा होतो
उदाहरण: ६, ४, १ या संख्यांचा उतरता क्रम ६, ४, १ असा होतो
साधारणपणे चढता क्रम लिहिताना १, २, ३, ४… असे लिहिले जाते
उतरता क्रम लिहिताना ९, ८, ७, ६… असे लिहिले जाते
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी सर्व संख्या तुलना करून सर्वांत लहान शोधा
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी सर्व संख्या तुलना करून सर्वांत मोठी शोधा
चढता क्रमात सर्व संख्या वाढत्या क्रमाने असतात
उतरता क्रमात सर्व संख्या घटत्या क्रमाने असतात
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “पहिले लहान, नंतर मोठे” हे नियम पाळा
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “पहिले मोठे, नंतर लहान” हे नियम पाळा
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “सर्वांत लहान” शोधून ते प्रथम लिहा
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “सर्वांत मोठे” शोधून ते प्रथम लिहा
चढता क्रम आणि उतरता क्रम हे दोन्ही गणितात महत्त्वाचे आहेत
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “क्रमबद्ध” शब्द वापरला जातो
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “उलटा क्रम” शब्द वापरला जातो
चढता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “सर्वात लहान” ते “सर्वात मोठे” असा प्रवास
उतरता क्रम लावण्यासाठी “सर्वात मोठे” ते “सर्वात लहान” असा प्रवास

quiz.explain: सर्वांत मोठी ८, नंतर ७, नंतर ६.

subject: Maths
notes: उतरता क्रम म्हणजे सर्वांत मोठी संख्या आधी, नंतर लहान, शेवटी सर्वांत लहान लिहायची पद्धत.
उदाहरण: ८, १, ५ या संख्यांचा उतरता क्रम ८, ५, १ असा होतो.
सर्वांत मोठी संख्या शोधण्यासाठी सर्व संख्या पाहून सर्वात मोठी ओळखावी.

quiz.explain: आखूड ओंडक्याच्या मागे उभा असलेल्या कोंबड्याला आखूड म्हणतात.

quiz.q: कोंबडा उभा राहण्यासाठी योग्य जागा शोधतो कारण?
quiz.explain: कोंबडा सुरक्षित वाटण्यासाठी योग्य जागा शोधतो.

quiz.q: कोंबडा उभा राहण्यासाठी कोणत्या शब्दांचा वापर करतो?
quiz.explain: कोंबडा उभा राहण्यासाठी उंच, ठेंगणा, लांब, आखूड हे शब्द वापरतो.

quiz.q: कोंबडा उभा राहण्यासाठी कोणत्या वस्तूंचा वापर करतो?
quiz.explain: कोंबडा खांब आणि ओंडके दोन्ही वापरतो.

quiz.q: कोंबडा उभा राहण्यासाठी योग्य जागा शोधतो, त्यामुळे तो?
quiz.explain: कोंबडा सुरक्षित वाटण्यासाठी योग्य जागा शोधतो.

subject: Maths
notes: तीस ते नव्व्यांची ओळख करण्यासाठी दशक व एकक ओळखणे आवश्यक आहे.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके दोन अंकी संख्या आहेत.
तीस ते नव्व्यांची ओळखमध्ये पहिला अंक दशक दर्शवतो, दुसरा अंक एकक दर्शवतो.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके लिहिताना पहिला अंक दशक, दुसरा अंक एकक असतो.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना 'तीस', 'चव्विस', 'पन्नास' इत्यादी शब्द वापरतात.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके लिहिताना दशक व एककचे सही जोडा लावणे आवश्यक आहे.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे नाव लिहिणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे अंकी व नावी रूप ओळखणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांची ओळख करण्यासाठी गिनती करणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे क्रम समजून घेणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे तुलना करणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे जोड-वघाव करणे शिकवले जाते.
तीस ते नव्व्या अंके ओळखताना संख्यांचे ओळख करण्यासाठी चित्रे, कर्डे, खेळ वापरले जातात.

quiz.q: तीस अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: तीस अंक म्हणजे तीन दशक व शून्य एकक.

quiz.q: चव्विस अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: चव्विस म्हणजे दोन दशक व सात एकक.

quiz.q: पन्नास अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: पन्नास अंक म्हणजे पाच दशक व शून्य एकक.

quiz.q: सत्तावीस अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: सत्तावीस म्हणजे सात दशक व चार एकक.

quiz.q: अठ्ठावीस अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: अठ्ठावीस म्हणजे आठ दशक व आठ एकक.

quiz.q: एकेकं अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: एकेकं म्हणजे नऊ दशक व एक एकक.

quiz.q: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत पहिला अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत पहिला अंक दशक दर्शवतो.

quiz.q: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत दुसरा अंक काय दर्शवतो?
quiz.explain: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत दुसरा अंक एकक दर्शवतो.

quiz.q: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत पहिला गट कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत पहिला गट 30-39 आहे.

quiz.q: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत शेवटचा गट कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: तीस ते नव्व्या अंकोत शेवटचा गट 90-99 आहे.

subject: Maths
notes: संख्या म्हणजे कद किती वस्तू आहेत हे दर्शविणारे अंक.
एक ते नऑपर्यंतची एक अंकीय संख्या.
दोन अंकीय संख्या १० ते ९९ पर्यंत असतात.
पुढची संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्यापुढे येवली जाणारी संख्या.
मागची संख्या म्हणजे दिलेल्या संख्यापूर्वी येवली जाणारी संख्या.
पुढची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी १ जोडतो.
मागची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी १ काढतो.
जोडी लावणे म्हणजे दोन संबंधित गोष्टी जोडणे.
जोडी लावण्यात संख्या व त्याची नाव जोडतात.
जोडी लावण्यात संख्या व त्याची पुढची/मागची संख्या जोडतात.
संख्या लिहिते व त्याचे नाव ओळखितात.
संख्या ओळखण्यासाठी चित्रे किंवा वस्तू वापरतात.
संख्या सांकेतिकपणे लिहिती.
संख्या सांगण्यासाठी शब्द वापरतात.
संख्या ओळखण्यासाठी गाणे किंवा कविता वापरतात.

quiz.q: 5 चा पुढचा संख्या कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: 5 चा पुढचा संख्या 6 आहे, कारण 5 + 1 = 6.

quiz.q: 9 चा मागचा संख्या कोणता आहे?
quiz.explain: 9 चा मागचा संख्या 8 आहे, कारण 9 - 1 = 8.

quiz.q: जोडी लावा: 7
quiz.explain: 7 चा नाव मराठीत 'सात' आहे, त्यामुळे जोडी 7 - सात.

quiz.q: कोणती संख्या 10 नो टक्के आहे?
पुढची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी काय करणे पडतो?
quiz.explain: पुढची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी दिलेल्या संख्यामा १ जोडतो.

quiz.q: मागची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी काय करणे पडतो?
quiz.explain: मागची संख्या शोधण्यासाठी दिलेल्या संख्यामधून १ काढतो.

quiz.q: जोडी लावा: 3
quiz.explain: 3 चा नाव मराठीत 'तीन' आहे, त्यामुळे जोडी 3 - तीन.

quiz.q: कोणती संख्या 1 नो टक्के आहे?
quiz.explain: 1 नो टक्के म्हणजे 1, कारण 1 × 1 = 1.

quiz.q: जोडी लावा: पुढची संख्या 5
quiz.explain: पुढची संख्या 5 म्हणजे 5 + 1 = 6, त्यामुळे जोडी 5 - 6.

quiz.q: जोडी लावा: मागची संख्या 8
quiz.explain: मागची संख्या 8 म्हणजे 8 - 1 = 7, त्यामुळे जोडी 8 - 7.

subject: Maths
notes: आकृतिबंध म्हणजे आकृती आणि आकारांची ओळख.
वर्गात आपण वर्तुळ, चौकोन, त्रिकोण, आयत हे आकृतिबंध पाहतो.
वर्तुळाला 'वर्तुळ' म्हणतात, त्यात एकच बाजू असते.
चौकोनाला चार समान बाजू असतात आणि चार समकोन असतात.
त्रिकोणाला तीन बाजू आणि तीन कोन असतात.
आयताला चार बाजू असतात, पण बाजूंची लांबी वेगवेगळी असू शकते.
समकोन म्हणजे ९० अंशाचा कोन.
समकोन असलेल्या आकृतिबंधाला 'समकोनी' म्हणतात.
वर्तुळाचे केंद्र 'केंद्रबिंदू' म्हणतात.
वर्तुळाची परिमिती 'परिघ' म्हणतात.
आयताची लांबी आणि रुंदी 'माप' म्हणतात.
आकृतिबंधांमध्ये समान बाजू असलेल्या आकृतिबंधांना 'समरूप' म्हणतात.
वर्तुळात कोणतीही बाजू नसते, त्यामुळे त्याला 'बाजू' म्हणत नाहीत.
आकृतिबंध ओळखण्यासाठी आपण त्याच्या बाजूंची आणि कोनांची मोजणी करतो.
आकृतिबंधांचे नाव शिकताना आपण त्यांना चित्रासह ओळखतो.
आकृतिबंधांचे गुणधर्म लक्षात ठेवण्यासाठी आपण तक्ती वापरतो.
आकृतिबंध ओळखताना आपण त्याच्या आकारावरून नाव ओळखतो.
आकृतिबंधांचे वर्गीकरण करताना आपण 'आकार' आणि 'बाजू' या आधारावर करतो.
आकृतिबंधांमध्ये सममिती असू शकते, ज्याला 'सममिती रेषा' म्हणतात.
आकृतिबंध ओळखताना आपण त्यांच्या कोनांची मोजणी करतो.

quiz.q: आकृतिबंधात सर्वात लहान आकृती कोणती आहे?
quiz.explain: त्रिकोणात फक्त तीन बाजू असतात, त्यामुळे तो सर्वात लहान आकृती आहे.

quiz.q: वर्तुळाला किती बाजू असतात?
quiz.explain: वर्तुळाला कोणत्याही बाजू नसतात, तो सतत वक्र आहे.

quiz.q: चौरसाला किती कोन असतात?
quiz.explain: चौरसाला चार समकोन असतात.

quiz.q: आयताच्या विरुद्ध बाजू समान असतात. हे विधान बरोबर आहे का?
quiz.explain: आयताच्या विरुद्ध बाजू समान असतात.

quiz.q: त्रिकोणाच्या सर्व बाजूंची बेरीज किती असते?
quiz.explain: त्रिकोणाच्या कोनांची बेरीज नेहमी 180° असते.

quiz.q: वर्तुळाच्या व्यासाला काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: वर्तुळाचा व्यास म्हणजे त्याच्या केंद्रातून जाणारी रेषा.

quiz.q: आकृतिबंधात कोणती आकृती सर्वात जास्त बाजू असते?
quiz.explain: आयताला चार बाजू असतात, इतर आकृत्यांपेक्षा जास्त नाही, पण वर्तुळाला बाजू नसतात.

quiz.q: वर्तुळाच्या परिघाला काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: वर्तुळाच्या परिघाला परिघ म्हणतात.

quiz.q: आकृतिबंधात कोणती आकृती सर्वात जास्त कोन असते?
quiz.explain: चौरसाला चार कोन असतात, त्रिकोणाला तीन, आयताला चार, वर्तुळाला कोन नसतात.

quiz.q: वर्तुळाच्या आत एक बिंदू असतो ज्याला काय म्हणतात?
quiz.explain: वर्तुळाचे केंद्र म्हणजे त्याच्या आतला एक बिंदू.

subject: Maths
notes: - मापन म्हणजे वस्तूंची लांबी, वजन, वेळ इत्यादी मोजणे.
- लांबी मोजण्यासाठी मीटर, सेंटीमीटर, इंच वापरतात.
- वजन मोजण्यासाठी किलोग्राम, ग्रॅम, पाउंड वापरतात.
- वेळ मोजण्यासाठी सेकंद, मिनिट, तास वापरतात.
- मापनाचे एकक म्हणजे लांबीचे एकक, वजनाचे एकक, वेळेचे एकक.
- लांबी मोजताना पट्टी किंवा रूलर वापरतो.
- वजन मोजताना तौल किंवा स्केल वापरतो.
- वेळ मोजण्यासाठी घड्याळ किंवा स्टॉपवॉच वापरतो.
- मापन करताना एककाचे रूपांतर करणे आवश्यक असते.
- १०० सेंटीमीटर = १ मीटर.
- मापन करताना अचूकता महत्त्वाची असते.
- मापनाचे परिणाम नोंदवताना एककासह लिहावे.
- मापनाच्या प्रश्नांमध्ये रिकाम्या जागा भरणे, बरोबर/चूक, जुळवणे अशा प्रकारचे प्रश्न असतात.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना दिलेल्या आकड्यांवरून योग्य एकक निवडावे.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना एकक रूपांतराचे नियम लक्षात ठेवावेत.
- मापनाच्या प्रश्नांमध्ये चित्र किंवा आकृती दिली असेल तर ती नीट पाहून उत्तर द्यावे.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना गणितीय चिन्हे आणि शब्दांची योग्य वापर करावी.
- मापनाच्या प्रश्नांमध्ये दिलेल्या आकड्यांवरून लांबी, वजन किंवा वेळेचे मूल्य शोधावे.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना उत्तरात एककासह लिहावे.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना दिलेल्या आकड्यांवरून योग्य एकक निवडावे.
- मापनाचे प्रश्न सोडवताना एकक रूपांतराचे नियम लक्षात ठेवावेत.

quiz.q: १ मीटरमध्ये किती सेंटीमीटर असतात?
quiz.explain: १ मीटर = १०० सेंटीमीटर.

quiz.q: १००० ग्रॅममध्ये किती किलोग्राम असतात?
६० सेकंदात किती मिनिटे होतात?
quiz.explain: ६० सेकंद = १ मिनिट.

quiz.q: मापन करताना कोणते साधन लांबी मोजण्यासाठी वापरतात?
quiz.explain: रूलर लांबी मोजण्यासाठी वापरतात.

quiz.q: वजन मोजण्यासाठी कोणते साधन वापरतात?
quiz.explain: स्केल वजन मोजण्यासाठी वापरतात.

quiz.q: १ तासात किती मिनिटे असतात?
मापनाच्या प्रश्नांमध्ये उत्तर लिहिताना काय लिहावे?

बेरीज करताना डावीकडून उजवीकडे लिहावे.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Sources of history are evidence that help us understand the past.
There are three main types of sources: material, written and oral.
Material sources include coins, inscriptions, monuments, sculptures, buildings and everyday objects.
Written sources are documents, books, letters, chronicles, travelogues, biographies and legal records written on paper, palm leaf, copper plate etc.
Oral sources are folk songs, legends, powadas, stories, proverbs and oral histories passed down by word of mouth.
Coins give information about rulers, economy, language and religion through their designs and inscriptions.
Inscriptions on stone or copper plates record royal edicts, land grants, religious donations and historical events.
Monuments such as forts, temples, palaces and graves show architectural style, technology and social life of a period.
Written records like chronicles (bakhar), travelogues (tavarikh) and biographies provide narrative accounts of events and people.
Oral traditions such as powadas and folk tales reveal cultural values, social norms and everyday life of ordinary people.
All sources must be evaluated for authenticity, reliability, bias and context before using them in history.
Authentic evidence is evidence that can be verified by cross‑checking with other contemporary sources.
Material sources are usually more reliable for dating events because they are harder to change.
Written sources can be biased if written by a ruler’s court or a religious institution.
Oral sources may contain exaggerations or metaphors, so they need careful interpretation.
The four factors important for history are individuals, society, place and time.
History is a systematic, chronological account of the past based on evidence.
Evaluating sources involves checking authenticity, internal consistency and external corroboration.
A stone inscription is considered an authentic source because it is a physical record that can be dated and verified.
Monuments include forts, temples, palaces, graves, caves, sculptures and other built structures.
Tarikh (or Tavarikh) is a Persian term for a chronicle or historical record written by travelers or historians.
The author’s impartiality, neutrality and integrity are crucial for reliable historical writing.

quiz.explain: Weather is not one of the four factors.

quiz.explain: Inscriptions are written sources.

quiz.explain: Tarikh means a chronicle.

quiz.explain: Oral sources often contain exaggerations.

quiz.explain: A fort is a monument.

quiz.explain: Evaluation checks authenticity and reliability.

quiz.explain: Stone inscriptions are written sources.

subject: History & Civics
notes: 1. The Maratha Empire grew after the death of Aurangzeb in 1707 when the Mughal power weakened.
2. Shahu Maharaj was released from Mughal captivity and became the new Chhatrapati (king) of the Marathas.
3. Shahu’s coronation in 1713 marked the revival of Maratha sovereignty after the war with Maharani Tarabai.
4. Balaji Vishwanath became the first Peshwa (prime minister) and helped organise the Maratha administration.
5. Bajirao I, son of Balaji, was a brilliant general who expanded the Maratha influence northwards.
6. The Marathas fought and defeated the Nizam of Hyderabad at the Battle of Palkhed (1715).
7. Bajirao’s campaigns captured the forts of Thane and Vasai from the Portuguese (1739).
8. The Marathas collected ‘Chauthai’ (one‑fourth of revenue) and ‘Sardeshmukhi’ (one‑tenth) from conquered territories.
9. The Marathas also secured the Subhedari (governorship) of Malwa and Bundelkhand from the Mughal emperor.
10. The Maratha navy, led by Kanhoji Angre, protected the Konkan coast and controlled the Arabian Sea trade routes.
11. The Marathas’ policy of ‘Chauth’ and ‘Sardeshmukhi’ helped them sustain a large army and administrative network.
12. Shahu’s reign saw the Marathas shift from fighting the Mughals to becoming a major power in North India.
13. The Marathas’ expansion was aided by internal Mughal conflicts and the decline of the Mughal court.
14. The Maratha Empire at its peak covered most of present-day Maharashtra, parts of Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
15. The Marathas’ rise set the stage for later conflicts with the British and the eventual establishment of the Maratha Confederacy.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Marathas as Guardians of the Nation
notes: Marathas were a powerful Indian group who ruled large parts of western and central India in the 18th century.
The Peshwa was the chief military and political leader of the Maratha Empire.
Shahu Maharaj was a Maratha king who helped the Marathas gain more power after Bajirao I.
The Marathas fought against the Afghans led by Ahmad Shah Abdali, who invaded India several times.
In 1751 the Marathas entered a treaty with the Mughal emperor to protect Delhi from Abdali’s attacks.
The Marathas captured Delhi in 1752 and later pushed Abdali’s army as far as Attock (now in Pakistan).
The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) was a huge defeat for the Marathas against Abdali’s forces.
After Panipat the Marathas lost much territory but later regained power under Peshwa Madhavrao and Mahadji Shinde.
The Marathas were known for their cavalry, artillery and a strong navy in the Konkan region.
They built many forts, temples and irrigation works, and promoted education and justice.
The Maratha Empire had a complex family tree of Peshwas, with many members sharing the same names.
The Marathas were tolerant of different religions and allowed people of all faiths to serve in their army.
The Marathas fought against the Nizam of Hyderabad, Hyder Ali of Mysore and the British East India Company.
The Marathas’ decline began after the defeat at Panipat and the rise of British power in India.
The Marathas’ legacy includes the city of Pune, the Maratha navy and the concept of a united India.

subject: History & Civics
notes: - The Maratha Empire expanded under leaders like Malhar Rao Holkar, Ahilyabai Holkar, Mahadji Shinde, and the Bhosale of Nagpur.
- Malhar Rao Holkar founded the Holkar rule in Indore and built temples, ghats, and water facilities.
- Ahilyabai Holkar was a great administrator, built lakes, temples, and promoted trade and agriculture.
- Mahadji Shinde (Mahadji Scindia) restored Maratha control over Delhi and the North after the defeat at Panipat.
- The Bhosale of Nagpur, especially Raghuji, expanded Maratha influence into the South and East (Odisha, Bengal).
- The Maratha navy, led by Kanhoji Angre, defeated Portuguese, British, and Siddhi naval forces.
- The Maratha Empire faced internal strife and external pressure from the British, leading to its decline by 1818.
- Key titles: Peshwa (prime minister), Sardar (chief), Vakil (chief agent).
- Maratha administration introduced new laws, agricultural cess, and improved irrigation.
- The Marathas used guerrilla tactics and modernized artillery with French help (e.g., de Boigne).

subject: History & Civics
notes: - Life of people in Maharashtra during the Maratha period (1630‑1810 CE) was largely agrarian and village‑based.
- Villages were self‑sufficient; main crops were jowar, bajra, wheat, ragi, maize and rice.
- Daily diet consisted of bhakari (flatbread), onions, chutney, vegetables, milk and dahi.
- Barter system was used for everyday transactions; money was rarely used.
- Houses were simple mud or brick constructions; wadas (large houses) were built in cities with one or two storeys.
- Men wore dhoti, kurta, angarakha and mundas; women wore nine‑yard sarees and blouses.
- Festivals celebrated included Gudhi Padwa, Nagpanchami, Bail‑Pola, Dasara, Diwali, Makarsankrant, Holi, Eid and Ganeshotsava.
- Maratha administration had Patil (village protector) and Kulkarni (revenue officer).
- Balutedars were village specialists (blacksmith, carpenter, potter, goldsmith etc.) paid in kind.
- Joint family system was common and important for village affairs.
- Women’s life was confined to household chores; transport was by bullocks, boats and camel riders.
- Education was mainly through pathshalas (Hindu) and madarasas (Muslim); literacy was low among women.
- Maratha rulers promoted architecture (wadas, ghats, forts) and painting (wall paintings, temple murals).
- Sports and games like wrestling, kho‑kho, chess, dice, and folk dances (tamasha, mallakhamb) were popular.
- Two major religions were Hinduism and Islam; the state followed a liberal religious policy.
- Maratha rulers built temples, forts, water supply systems and underground pipes in cities like Pune and Nashik.
- The period saw the rise of Maratha power and the spread of Marathi culture and literature.

subject: History & Civics
notes: A Constitution is a written document containing the basic rules for governing a country.
It is the fundamental law that the government must follow.
The Constitution outlines the rights and duties of citizens.
It defines the relationship between citizens and the State.
The Constitution includes provisions on citizenship, elections, and government powers.
It establishes the rule of law and prevents misuse of power.
The Indian Constitution was made by the Constituent Assembly.
The Constituent Assembly had 299 members and was presided over by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and is called the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution'.
The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into force on 26th January 1950.
26th November is celebrated as Constitution Day and 26th January as Republic Day.
The Constitution has 22 parts, 395 articles, and 12 schedules (as per final version).
It reflects India’s diversity, history, and social values.
The Constitution can be amended but only through a special process.
It promotes justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.

quiz.explain: A Constitution is a written document containing the basic rules and principles for governing a country.

quiz.q: Who is known as the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution'?

subject: History & Civics
notes: The Preamble is the introduction to the Indian Constitution and states its objectives.
It begins with 'We, the people of India'.
India is a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
Sovereign means India is free from foreign control and governs itself.
Socialist means reducing the gap between rich and poor; wealth should not be concentrated.
Secular means all religions are equal; the state has no religion.
Democratic means power lies with the people who elect representatives.
Republic means the head of state is elected, not hereditary.
Justice includes social, economic, and political justice.
Liberty means freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship.
Equality means equal status and opportunity without discrimination.
Fraternity promotes a sense of brotherhood and dignity among citizens.
The Preamble reflects the ideals of the freedom struggle.
The Constituent Assembly drafted the Constitution; Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was its chairman.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.

quiz.explain: Sovereign means India is independent and not under any foreign power's subject.

quiz.explain: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the 'Architect of the Indian Constitution' and chaired the Drafting Committee.

quiz.explain: In a secular state, all religions are equal before the law and the state does not favor any religion.

quiz.q: Why do we celebrate 26th January as Republic Day?
quiz.explain: The Indian Constitution came into effect on 26th January 1950, making India a republic.

quiz.q: Which value in the Preamble promotes a sense of brotherhood and empathy among citizens?
quiz.explain: Fraternity promotes a 'we-feeling' and dignity among all citizens.

quiz.q: What does 'Democratic' mean in the Preamble?
options: Power lies with the people who elect representatives
quiz.explain: In a democracy, the people hold sovereign power and elect their representatives to govern.

quiz.q: What does 'Socialist State' aim to achieve according to the Preamble?
options: Ensure wealth is concentrated in few hands
Reduce gap between rich and poor; ensure fair distribution of wealth
quiz.explain: A Socialist State aims to minimize inequality and ensure wealth is not concentrated in a few hands.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a feature of a Republic?
options: Head of state is elected by the people
quiz.explain: In a Republic, public offices are held by elected individuals, not by birthright.

quiz.q: What does 'Liberty' in the Preamble guarantee to citizens?
options: Freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship
quiz.explain: Liberty means freedom of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship, exercised responsibly.

subject: History & Civics
notes: The Constitution of India has three lists: Union List (97 subjects), State List (66 subjects), and Concurrent List (47 subjects).
Union Government makes laws on subjects in the Union List, e.g., defence, foreign affairs, currency.
State Government makes laws on subjects in the State List, e.g., agriculture, law and order, health.
Both Union and State Governments can make laws on subjects in the Concurrent List, e.g., education, employment.
Subjects not in any list are residuary subjects; Union Government has power to make laws on them.
Federalism means division of powers between central and state governments for cooperative governance.
India has a parliamentary system where the Legislature (Parliament) holds supreme power.
Parliament consists of President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha; Council of Ministers is responsible to Lok Sabha.
Judiciary is independent; judges are appointed by President and not easily removable.
India provides single citizenship to all citizens, known as Indian Citizenship.
Amending the Constitution is a careful process; not too easy nor too difficult, ensuring stability and flexibility.
Election Commission is an independent body responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.
Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Constitution to ensure equality and justice for all citizens.
Union Territories are directly governed by the Union Government; there are 9 Union Territories in India.
India has 28 States and 9 Union Territories under one Union Government.

quiz.q: Which list contains subjects like defence, foreign relations, and currency?
quiz.explain: Defence, foreign relations, and currency are part of the Union List, which only the Union Government can legislate on.

quiz.q: How many subjects are in the State List according to the Indian Constitution?
quiz.explain: The State List contains 66 subjects on which State Governments can make laws, such as agriculture and health.

quiz.q: What is the term used for powers not mentioned in any of the three lists of the Constitution?
quiz.explain: Subjects not included in Union, State, or Concurrent Lists are residuary subjects; the Union Government has power over them.

quiz.q: Who appoints the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts in India?
quiz.explain: Judges are appointed by the President of India, ensuring independence of the judiciary from the executive.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a feature of the Indian parliamentary system?
options: Council of Ministers is responsible to Lok Sabha
States have veto over central laws
quiz.explain: In India's parliamentary system, the Council of Ministers stays in office only as long as it has the support of the Lok Sabha.

quiz.q: Which list includes subjects like education, employment, and environment?
quiz.explain: Education, employment, and environment are in the Concurrent List, allowing both Union and State Governments to make laws.

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to vote in Indian elections?
quiz.explain: The Constitution grants voting rights to all citizens aged 18 years and above.

quiz.q: Which body is responsible for conducting elections in India?
quiz.explain: The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting free and fair elections.

quiz.q: What does 'single citizenship' mean in the Indian context?
options: All Indians have only Indian citizenship
quiz.explain: India provides single citizenship—every citizen is an Indian citizen, regardless of the state they reside in.

quiz.q: Why is the amendment procedure of the Indian Constitution designed to be neither too easy nor too difficult?
options: To prevent instability while allowing necessary changes
To give power to states only
quiz.explain: The procedure ensures stability by avoiding frequent changes, yet allows amendments for progress with careful consideration.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Fundamental rights are basic rights given by the Constitution to all citizens.
They have the status of law and must be followed by everyone.
Right to Equality ensures no discrimination based on religion, caste, sex, race, or place of birth.
Untouchability in any form is abolished and is a cognizable offence.
Titles like Raja, Maharaja, Raobahadur that create artificial hierarchy are abolished.
Right to Liberty includes freedom of speech, expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
No person can be arrested or detained without reason; allegations must be proved before punishment.
Right to Life includes the Right to Education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
Right against Exploitation bans bonded labour, forced labour, and employment of children under 14 in hazardous places.
Cultural and Educational Rights allow communities to preserve their language, script, and establish institutions for their development.
Right to Freedom of Religion allows individuals to practise any religion and establish religious institutions.
The State cannot impose religious taxes or make religious education compulsory in aided institutions.
Right to Constitutional Remedies allows citizens to approach courts if their fundamental rights are violated.
Awards like Padmashree, Padmabhushan, Padmavibhushan, and Bharat Ratna are given for distinguished service but do not confer special rights.
Fundamental rights promote equality, liberty, and dignity for all individuals in society.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Right to Liberty as per the Constitution?
options: Freedom to move freely throughout India
quiz.explain: Right to Liberty does not include the right to own private property; it covers speech, assembly, movement, etc.

quiz.q: What is the status of untouchability in India according to the Constitution?
options: It is allowed in rural areas
It is abolished and a cognizable offence
It is only applicable to certain castes
quiz.explain: Untouchability in any form is abolished by law and is a cognizable offence under the Constitution.

quiz.q: Which award is the highest civilian honour in India?
quiz.explain: Bharat Ratna is the highest civilian award in India for exceptional service in any field.

quiz.q: What does the Right against Exploitation prohibit?
options: Children under 14 from working in factories
Children under 14 from working in hazardous places
All children from working after school
Only girls from working in homes
quiz.explain: The Constitution prohibits employment of children under 14 years of age in hazardous places like factories and mines.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a feature of the Right to Equality?
quiz.explain: Right to Equality means equal protection of laws and no discrimination based on religion, caste, sex, etc.

quiz.q: Which freedom is NOT included in the Right to Liberty?
options: Freedom to reside in any part of India
quiz.explain: Right to Liberty includes profession, residence, and association, but not the right to strike, which is subject to legal restrictions.

quiz.q: What does the Right to Constitutional Remedies allow citizens to do?
options: Approach courts if fundamental rights are violated
quiz.explain: This right allows citizens to move the court for enforcement of fundamental rights when they are infringed.

quiz.q: Which of the following titles has been abolished by the Constitution?
quiz.explain: Titles like Raobahadur that create artificial social hierarchy have been abolished by the Constitution.

quiz.q: What is the age group for which the Right to Education is a Fundamental Right?
quiz.explain: The Constitution provides free and compulsory education as a Fundamental Right to children between 6 and 14 years of age.

quiz.q: Which statement is true about awards like Padmashree?
options: They are only for military personnel
They are recognition of distinguished service without special rights
quiz.explain: Awards like Padmashree are given for distinguished contribution but do not confer any special rights or privileges.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Fundamental Rights are basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution to all citizens.
They include rights like equality, freedom, and protection against exploitation.
The judiciary protects Fundamental Rights through writs.
Writs are formal written orders issued by courts to enforce rights.
Habeas Corpus protects against unlawful arrest and detention.
Mandamus commands a public official to perform their legal duty.
Prohibition stops a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
Quo Warranto prevents a person from holding an office they are not entitled to.
Certiorari transfers a case from a lower court to a higher court for review.
Directive Principles of State Policy guide the government in making laws for social and economic welfare.
They are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental in governance.
Examples include securing livelihood, equal pay for equal work, and promoting education.
Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of citizens to promote patriotism and unity.
They include respecting the Constitution, National Flag, and National Anthem.
Citizens must strive for excellence, protect public property, and promote harmony.

quiz.q: Which writ is used to protect a person from unlawful arrest?
quiz.explain: Habeas Corpus means 'produce the body' and is used to release a person illegally detained.

quiz.q: What does the writ of Mandamus do?
options: Orders a public official to perform duty
Stops a lower court from overreach
quiz.explain: Mandamus is a command to a public authority to perform a legal duty they have failed to do.

quiz.q: Which writ prevents a subordinate court from exceeding its jurisdiction?
quiz.explain: Prohibition is issued by a higher court to stop a lower court from acting beyond its legal authority.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of the writ of Quo Warranto?
options: To release an unlawfully detained person
To challenge someone's right to hold a public office
To transfer a case to a higher court
To order government to perform a duty
quiz.explain: Quo Warranto means 'by what authority' and is used to question a person's legal right to hold a public office.

quiz.q: Which writ is used to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court?
quiz.explain: Certiorari means 'to be certified' and is used to quash an order of a lower court or transfer a case.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a Directive Principle of State Policy?
quiz.explain: Equal pay for equal work is a Directive Principle under Article 39(d), guiding the state to ensure fair wages.

quiz.q: Are Directive Principles of State Policy enforceable by courts?
quiz.explain: Directive Principles are guidelines for the state and are not justiciable, meaning courts cannot enforce them directly.

quiz.q: Which Fundamental Duty involves respecting national symbols?
options: To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and Anthem
quiz.explain: The first Fundamental Duty is to abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem.

quiz.q: What is the age group for which parents must provide education opportunities as a Fundamental Duty?
quiz.explain: Under Article 51A(k), parents or guardians must provide education opportunities to children between the age of six and fourteen years.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
options: To renounce practices derogatory to women’s dignity
quiz.explain: Imposing religious taxes is prohibited by Fundamental Rights, not a Fundamental Duty. Fundamental Duties are moral obligations, not powers to tax.

subject: History & Civics
chapter: Civics: Guiding Principles and Fundamental Duties
notes: Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of citizens to promote patriotism and unity.
Directive Principles guide the state to establish social and economic democracy.
Fundamental Rights are justiciable; Directive Principles are non-justiciable.
Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
Article 51A lists 11 Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
Directive Principles aim to create a welfare state.
Uniform Civil Code is a Directive Principle aiming for common personal laws.
Education is a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
Citizens must respect the National Flag and National Anthem.
Protecting public property and natural resources is a Fundamental Duty.
Promoting harmony and brotherhood among all people is a Fundamental Duty.
Safeguarding cultural heritage and historical monuments is a duty of citizens.
Striving for excellence in individual and collective activity is a Fundamental Duty.
The State shall protect monuments of historic interest and national importance.
Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles complement each other in governance.

quiz.q: Which part of the Indian Constitution contains the Fundamental Duties?
quiz.explain: Fundamental Duties are listed in Part IVA of the Constitution under Article 51A.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty of Indian citizens?
quiz.explain: Protecting public property and avoiding violence is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A.

quiz.q: What is the status of Directive Principles of State Policy in courts?
quiz.explain: Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning courts cannot enforce them directly.

quiz.q: Which article deals with the Uniform Civil Code in the Directive Principles?
quiz.explain: Article 44 of the Directive Principles states that the State shall endeavor to secure a Uniform Civil Code.

quiz.q: Which age group has the right to free and compulsory education?
quiz.explain: Under Article 21A, free and compulsory education is a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?
quiz.explain: Receiving education is a right, not a duty. Developing scientific temper is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(h).

quiz.q: What does the Directive Principle regarding monuments aim to protect?
options: Monuments of historic interest and national importance
quiz.explain: The Directive Principle under Article 49 directs the State to protect monuments of historic interest and national importance.

quiz.q: Why are Directive Principles and Fundamental Rights considered two sides of the same coin?
options: Both aim to establish social and economic democracy
quiz.explain: While Fundamental Rights protect individual liberty, Directive Principles aim for social justice—together they ensure a balanced democracy.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a Directive Principle related to workers' welfare?
quiz.explain: Directive Principles include securing just and humane conditions of work and ensuring that men and women receive equal pay for equal work.

quiz.q: Which activity reflects the Fundamental Duty of promoting harmony?
options: Participating in festivals of different religions
quiz.explain: Participating in festivals of different religions promotes unity and brotherhood, which is a Fundamental Duty.

subject: History & Civics
notes: - The last powerful dynasty before Shivaji Maharaj was the Yadava dynasty, whose capital was Deogiri near Aurangabad.
- The Yadavas ruled from the 9th to the 13th century and spread their influence from the Krishna River to the east and west.
- The Gurjara-Pratihara and Rashtrakuta empires were earlier North Indian powers that spread from Kanauj to the south.
- The Chola dynasty (8th–13th century) ruled Tamil Nadu and had naval power in the Indian Ocean, conquering parts of Karnataka and Sri Lanka.
- The Delhi Sultanate began with Qutubuddin Aibak (1206–1210) and later rulers like Alauddin Khalji, Muhammad bin Tughluq, and Ibrahim Lodi.
- The Bahamani Sultanate (1336–1527) was founded by Hasan Gangu and later ruled by the Adilshahi, Nizamshahi, Qutubshahi, and Baridshahi.
- The Vijayanagara Empire (1336–1646) was founded by Harihara and Bukka and reached its peak under Krishnadevaraya.
- The Mughal Empire (1526–1707) was founded by Babur, expanded under Akbar, and ended with Aurangzeb.
- The Marathas rose under Shivaji Maharaj after the decline of the Bahamani and Mughal powers.
- Key terms: Yadava, Gurjara-Pratihara, Rashtrakuta, Chola, Delhi Sultanate, Bahamani, Vijayanagara, Mughal, Maratha.

quiz.q: Which dynasty ruled the Deccan region before the rise of the Bahamani Sultanate?
quiz.explain: The Yadava dynasty was the dominant power in the Deccan before the Bahamani Sultanate.

quiz.q: Who was the first ruler of the Bahamani Sultanate?
quiz.explain: Bukka, brother of Harihar, founded the Bahamani Sultanate in 1347 CE.

quiz.q: Which battle marked the beginning of Mughal rule in India?
quiz.explain: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 CE brought Babur to power.

quiz.q: Who was the last Sultan of Delhi before the Mughal Empire?
quiz.explain: Ibrahim Lodi was the final Sultan of Delhi before Babur established the Mughal Empire.

quiz.q: Which empire extended its rule from Kashmir to Bengal?
quiz.explain: The Mughal Empire expanded from Kashmir in the north to Bengal in the east.

quiz.q: Who founded the Vijayanagar Empire?
quiz.explain: Krishnadevaraya is credited with founding the Vijayanagar Empire.

quiz.q: Which dynasty was known for its naval strength in the eighth century?
quiz.explain: The Chola dynasty had a powerful navy in the eighth century.

quiz.q: Who introduced the concept of Din‑i‑Ilahi?
quiz.explain: Akbar introduced the religious concept of Din‑i‑Ilahi.

quiz.q: Which region did the Bahamani Sultanate NOT control?
quiz.explain: Delhi was not part of the Bahamani Sultanate; it was under the Delhi Sultanate.

quiz.q: Which ruler was known for his liberal religious policies?
quiz.explain: Akbar was famous for his tolerant and liberal religious policies.

subject: History & Civics
notes: - The Bhakti movement was a religious reform movement that started in India around the 7th century and spread across the country.
- It emphasised devotion (bhakti) to a personal god and rejected rigid rituals and caste barriers.
- Famous saints of the movement include Ramanuja, Ramananda, Kabir, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, and Basaveshwara.
- Ramanuja taught that God is loving and accessible to all, not just the elite.
- Ramananda preached that all human beings are equal and that devotion is the path to God.
- Kabir’s verses were simple and used everyday language to reach common people.
- Chaitanya Mahaprabhu promoted devotion to Krishna using songs and dance.
- Basaveshwara in Karnataka introduced the Lingayat faith, rejecting caste distinctions and encouraging simple living.
- The movement also influenced the rise of Sikhism and Sufi traditions, promoting harmony between Hindus and Muslims.
- Key features: use of local languages, emphasis on love and service, rejection of idol worship, and acceptance of all social groups.

quiz.q: Which saint is known for teaching that God is loving and accessible to everyone?
quiz.explain: Ramanuja emphasised a compassionate God for all.

quiz.q: What does the word 'bhakti' mean?
quiz.explain: Bhakti literally means devotion to God.

quiz.q: Which saint’s verses were written in simple everyday language?
quiz.explain: Kabir used plain language to reach common people.

quiz.q: The Lingayat faith was founded by which saint?
quiz.explain: Basaveshwara established the Lingayat movement.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Bhakti movement?
quiz.explain: Bhakti rejected strict idol worship.

quiz.q: Sufi saints believed that the way to reach God is through what?
quiz.explain: Sufi teachings emphasise love and devotion.

quiz.q: Guru Nanak was the first guru of which religion?
quiz.explain: Guru Nanak founded Sikhism.

quiz.q: Which saint is known for the saying 'Work is worship'?
quiz.explain: Basaveshwara’s famous saying is 'Work is worship'.

quiz.q: The Bhakti movement helped spread which of these?
quiz.explain: It promoted equality and devotion.

quiz.q: Which saint composed the 'Sursagar' in Marathi?
quiz.explain: Surdas wrote the Marathi poem 'Sursagar'.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Maharashtra before Shivaji was ruled by various Muslim sultanates like Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and the Mughals.
The local village head was called a Patil; he collected revenue and maintained order.
A Kulkarni was a village accountant who kept records of land and revenue.
The village was called a Mauja; a larger settlement was a Kasba and the district was a Pargana.
A Pargana consisted of many villages; its headquarters was usually a Kasba.
The people of a village were called villagers or “Mauja” people; they worked mainly in agriculture.
Artisans such as carpenters, blacksmiths and weavers lived in Kasbas and made a living by trading their goods.
The Portuguese, Dutch, French and British established trading posts (peths) near Kasbas to control trade.
A peth was a market area adjacent to a Kasba where merchants and craftsmen sold their wares.
The term “Budruk” meant a larger or older village; “Khurd” meant a smaller or newer village.
During the 1630s a great famine struck Maharashtra, causing crop failure, famine and loss of livestock.
The Deshmukh was the chief of a Pargana, the Deshpande was the chief of all Kulkarnis, and the Patil was the chief of a village.
The Varkari movement, led by saints like Dnyaneshwar, Namdeo, Eknath and Tukaram, promoted equality, devotion and social reform.
The saints used simple Marathi language (abhanga, keertans) to reach common people and to criticize social inequality.
Sant Ramdas Swami, a 17th‑century saint, wrote Dasbodh, a practical guide for self‑development and governance.
The Samarth Sampradaya was a devotional tradition founded by Sant Chokhamela and later followed by Sant Tukaram and others.
The term “Vatan” (Arabic) meant hereditary land granted to a saint, exempt from revenue.
The term “Baluta” was a share of produce paid by peasants to artisans for their services.
The term “Topkar” was a custom headgear worn by Shete and Mahajan, the local merchants and money‑lenders.
The term “Peth” was also called “Topkar” because of the merchants’ headgear.
The Varkari pilgrimage (Vari) to Pandharpur is celebrated every year in the month of Bhadrapada.
The Varkari movement encouraged people to live in harmony, equality and devotion to God.
The saints’ teachings helped people cope with foreign invasions, droughts and famines.
The saints’ compositions are still sung in Maharashtra’s temples and homes.
The saints’ teachings influenced later leaders like Shahaji Maharaj and the Maratha warriors.

quiz.q: Which title was given to the village head who collected revenue and maintained order?
quiz.explain: The Patil was the local village head responsible for revenue collection.

quiz.q: What does the term "Budruk" mean?
quiz.explain: Budruk indicates a larger or older village, while Khurd indicates a smaller one.

quiz.q: Which saint wrote the work "Darbodh"?
quiz.explain: Sant Ramdas Swami authored Dasbodh, a practical guide for self‑development.

quiz.q: During which decade did a great famine occur in Maharashtra?
quiz.explain: The famine of the 1630s devastated crops and livestock.

quiz.q: What was the main occupation of people in a Kasba?
quiz.explain: Kasbas were hubs for artisans and traders, not primarily agricultural.

quiz.q: Which term refers to the share of produce paid by peasants to artisans?
quiz.explain: Baluta was the share of produce given to artisans for their services.

quiz.q: What was the headquarters of a Pargana usually called?
quiz.explain: The Pargana headquarters was usually a Kasba.

quiz.q: Which saint is known for the composition "Amrutanubhav"?
quiz.explain: Sant Namdeo authored the work "Amrutanubhav".

quiz.q: Which movement promoted equality and devotion among common people?
quiz.explain: The Varkari movement, led by saints, promoted equality and devotion.

quiz.q: In which month do Varkaris go on the Pandharpur Vari?
quiz.explain: The Varkari pilgrimage to Pandharpur is celebrated in Bhadrapada.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was born on 19 February 1630 at Shivneri fort.
His father Shahajiraje was a prominent Sardar in the Deccan who resisted Mughal and Adilshahi powers.
Shahajiraje received the jagir of Pune, Supe, Indapur, and Chakan from the Adilshah of Bijapur.
Veermata Jijabai, Shivaji's mother, provided military training and education to him and inspired values like courage and truthfulness.
Shivaji began establishing Swaraj in the Maval region, using its hilly terrain for strategic advantage.
He captured forts like Torana, Rajgad (formerly Murumbdev), Kondhana, and Purandar to challenge Adilshahi control.
Shivaji's royal seal (Rajmudra) symbolizes the growth of Swaraj like the new moon and expresses his vision for people's welfare.
He defeated Afzalkhan in 1659 at Pratapgad through courage and strategy, boosting his reputation.
Shivaji built a strong navy to counter foreign powers like the Siddi, Portuguese, and British on the western coast.
He escaped from Panhala fort during a siege by Siddi Jauhar with the brave sacrifice of Baji Prabhu Deshpande at Ghod pass.
Shivaji formed alliances and treaties when necessary, such as with the Adilshah after Vishalgad, to consolidate power.
His companions like Tanaji Malusare, Bajiprabhu Deshpande, and others played key roles in military campaigns and fort captures.
Shivaji's administration emphasized justice, welfare of subjects, and independent rule, forming the foundation of Swaraj.
He conquered regions like Javali, Kalyan, and Bhiwandi, gaining wealth and expanding influence in Konkan and beyond.
Shivaji is remembered as a visionary leader who founded the Maratha Swaraj through courage, strategy, and people's welfare.

quiz.q: Where was Shivaji Maharaj born?
quiz.explain: Shivaji Maharaj was born at Shivneri fort near Junnar in Pune district on 19 February 1630.

quiz.q: What does 'jagir' mean in the context of Shivaji's father Shahajiraje?
options: Right to collect revenue from a region
quiz.explain: Jagir means the right to enjoy the revenue of a region instead of receiving a salary.

quiz.q: Which region did Shivaji Maharaj choose to start founding Swaraj due to its geographical features?
quiz.explain: Shivaji started founding Swaraj in the Maval region, which is full of hills and valleys and not easily accessible.

quiz.q: What was the original name of the fort that Shivaji renamed as Rajgad?
quiz.explain: Shivaji repaired and renamed the fort Murumbdev as Rajgad, which became the first capital of Swaraj.

quiz.q: Who sacrificed his life to help Shivaji Maharaj escape from Panhala fort?
quiz.explain: Baji Prabhu Deshpande held the Ghod pass against Siddi's army, allowing Shivaji to reach Vishalgad safely.

quiz.q: Why did Shivaji Maharaj focus on building a navy?
options: To fight Siddi, Portuguese, and British powers on the western coast
quiz.explain: Shivaji realized a strong naval force was necessary to counter the Siddi, Portuguese, and British powers on the western coast.

quiz.q: What does the inscription on Shivaji's royal seal (Rajmudra) symbolize?
quiz.explain: The seal means 'This seal will grow in splendour like the new moon', symbolizing the growing glory of Swaraj.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shivaji capture and rename as Vishalgad?
quiz.explain: Shivaji captured the Adilshahi fort of Khelna and renamed it Vishalgad.

quiz.q: Who was sent by the Adilshah to curb Shivaji Maharaj's rising power?
quiz.explain: The Adilshah sent Afzalkhan, a powerful and experienced general, to curb Shivaji Maharaj.

quiz.q: What quality of Veermata Jijabai is highlighted in shaping Shivaji's character?
quiz.explain: Jijabai gave Shivaji military training, education, and instilled values like courage, truthfulness, and fearlessness.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a brave king who fought against the Mughals and the Adilshahi to protect his Swaraj (self‑rule).
He captured many forts such as Chakan, Purandar, Rajgad, Sinhgad, and later Jinji in Tamil Nadu.
The Mughals, led by Aurangzeb, tried to stop him by sending armies and even putting him under house arrest in Agra.
Shivaji escaped from Agra with the help of his friend Moropant Pingale and returned to Maharashtra.
He fought the Mughals in several battles: the raid on Lal Mahal, the campaign to Surat, and the battle at Vani‑Dindori.
In 1665 he signed the Treaty of Purandar with the Mughals, giving them 23 forts but keeping most of his own.  He later broke the treaty to regain the forts.
Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati (king) on 6 June 1674 at Raigad, a ceremony that symbolised his sovereignty.  He had a second coronation on 24 September 1674.
The coronation used both Vedic and Tantric rituals and a special throne made of gold and precious jewels.
After the coronation, Shivaji launched a southern campaign, capturing forts like Jinji and Vellore, which helped him control parts of Tamil Nadu.
He died on 3 April 1680 at Raigad.  His younger brother Rajaram later became king and had to flee to southern forts for safety.
Shivaji’s courage and strategies inspired many Maratha leaders such as Tanaji Malusare, Moropant Pingale, and Prataprao Gujar.

quiz.q: Which Mughal emperor was defeated by Shivaji Maharaj in the Battle of Purandar?
quiz.explain: Aurangzeb was the Mughal emperor during the Battle of Purandar.

quiz.q: What was the main objective of Shaistakhan’s invasion in 1660?
quiz.explain: Shaistakhan’s invasion aimed at raiding Surat and its trade routes.

quiz.q: Which fort did Shivaji Maharaj capture after escaping from Agra?
quiz.explain: After escaping from Agra, Shivaji captured Rajgad.

quiz.q: The Treaty of Purandar was signed in which year?
quiz.explain: The Treaty of Purandar was signed in 1665.

quiz.q: Which of the following was NOT a part of Shivaji’s coronation ceremony?
quiz.explain: Singing of hymns was not mentioned as part of the coronation.

quiz.q: Who assisted Shivaji Maharaj in escaping from Agra?
quiz.explain: Dilerkhan helped Shivaji escape from Agra.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj founded Swaraj and crowned himself king to establish independent rule.
He formed a Council of Eight Ministers (Ashtapradhan Mandal) to manage different departments like finance, agriculture, army, foreign affairs, justice, religion, etc.

Each minister had a specific title: Pradhan (chief), Amatya (finance), Sachiv (secretary), Waknis (correspondence), Senapati (army commander), Dabir (foreign affairs), Nyayadhish (justice), Panditrao (religion).
The Ashtapradhan Mandal was responsible for collecting revenue, maintaining order, and administering conquered territories.
Shivaji’s administration emphasized agriculture as the main occupation and paid farmers for land cultivation and provided bullocks, ploughs, and seeds.
He introduced a feudal system where land was given as jagirs to nobles and soldiers in return for service, but he also kept a strong central control over revenue and land use.
The army was divided into infantry and cavalry; the cavalry had Shiledars (horsemen) and Bargirs (village soldiers).
He built many forts on hilltops and sea forts like Sindhudurg to protect the kingdom and control trade routes.
A dedicated intelligence department, headed by Bahirji Naik, gathered information about enemy movements, especially regarding salt trade from Portuguese territories.
Shivaji’s navy had around 400 ships, including warships like Gurab, Galbat, and Pal. He built sea forts and maintained naval bases to secure the western coast.
He protected the salt industry in Konkan by monitoring Portuguese salt imports and encouraging local salt production.
Shivaji’s policies aimed at welfare: he paid farmers, protected merchants, and ensured justice and religious affairs were managed by appointed officials.
The administration was efficient, with a system of revenue collection, land management, and military organization that kept the Swaraj stable.

Key terms: Swaraj (self-rule), Ashtapradhan Mandal (Council of Eight Ministers), Jagir (land grant), Shiledar (horseman), Bargir (village soldier), Sarnobat (chief officer), Bahirji Naik (intelligence chief).
Shivaji’s governance model combined strong central authority with local administration, ensuring both military strength and economic prosperity.
The forts and navy were crucial for defense and trade control, making Swaraj a formidable power in the region.
Shivaji’s administration is studied as an example of early modern statecraft in India.

subject: History & Civics
notes: Shivaji Maharaj was a 17th‑century ruler who founded the Maratha Empire, also called Swaraj (self‑rule).
He fought against the Mughals, Adilshahi, Siddis and Portuguese, winning many fort battles such as Panhala, Sinhagad and Sinhagad.
Shivaji’s administration was based on the principles of justice, equality and welfare of the people (ryots).
He paid soldiers on time and maintained strict discipline in the army. Soldiers were forbidden from looting or harming civilians.
Shivaji followed a tolerant religious policy – he respected mosques, temples and churches and allowed people of all faiths to practice freely.
He introduced the jagir system to reward soldiers and officers with land, but ensured that the revenue went to the state.
Shivaji’s leadership qualities included courage, intelligence, foresight, organisational skill and a strong sense of duty.
He encouraged his associates to be loyal, brave and to sacrifice for the welfare of the state.
Shivaji’s navy was built to protect the coast and to counter foreign invasions; he built forts like Sindhudurg.
He inspired other leaders such as Chhatrasal and later freedom fighters like Mahatma Gandhi and Jotirao Phule.

subject: History & Civics
notes: The Maratha War of Independence lasted 27 years against the Mughals.
It began after Shivaji Maharaj's death under Sambhaji Maharaj's leadership.
Sambhaji Maharaj was born on 14 May 1657 at Purandar Fort.
He received education in administration and military from age 14.
Sambhaji Maharaj fought bravely against Mughals, Portuguese, and Siddi of Janjira.
He attacked Revdanda fort in 1683 CE to counter Portuguese alliance with Mughals.
Aurangzeb laid siege to Ramsej fort near Nashik but failed to capture it.
Sambhaji Maharaj was captured and executed on 11 March 1689 by Aurangzeb.
After Sambhaji's death, Rajaram Maharaj became Chhatrapati and fled to Jinji.
Rajaram Maharaj escaped Raigad in April 1689 and later recaptured Jinji fort.
Maratha generals Santaji and Dhanaji used guerrilla tactics effectively against Mughals.
They once cut the golden pinnacle of Aurangzeb's tent in a surprise attack.
Rajaram Maharaj died on 2 March 1700 at Sinhgad after a short illness.
After Rajaram's death, Maharani Tarabai led the Maratha resistance for seven years.
Tarabai used the 'Safe deposit locker system' to recapture forts from Mughals.
Aurangzeb died in 1707 CE at Ahmednagar, ending the Maratha War of Independence.
Marathas emerged victorious and later controlled Delhi and much of Hindusthan.
The 18th century is known as the 'Century of the Marathas'.
Maharani Yesubai protected the royal family and supported Rajaram's escape to Jinji.
Sambhaji Maharaj knew Sanskrit and wrote 'Budhbhushanam' on polity and kingly virtues.

quiz.explain: Sambhaji Maharaj attacked Revdanda fort in 1683 CE to counter the Portuguese-Mughal alliance.

quiz.explain: Rajaram Maharaj escaped to the fort of Jinji in the south after the Mughals captured Raigad.

quiz.explain: Yesaji Kank showed great valour in the battle where the Portuguese Governor was wounded.

quiz.explain: Tarabai used the 'Safe deposit locker system' where bribed fort commanders returned wealth to Maratha treasury.

quiz.explain: Santaji Ghorpade and Vithoji Chavan cut the golden pinnacle of Aurangzeb's tent in a surprise attack.

notes: भौतिक साधने म्हणजे इमारती, स्मारके, किल्ले, नाणी, शिलालेख व इतर अवशेष ज्याद्वारे भूतकाळातील घटना समजतात.
लिखित साधने म्हणजे ग्रंथ, पत्रे, ताम्रपट, भूर्जपत्रे, प्रवासवर्णने व इतर लेखी दस्तऐवज.
मौखिक साधने म्हणजे लोकगीते, पोवाडे, दंतकथा, तवारिखा आणि प्रवासी वर्णने.
शिलालेख हे दगडावर कोरलेले लेख असून इतिहासलेखनाचे विश्वसनीय पुरावे मानले जातात.

quiz.q: चौथाई म्हणजे काय?
quiz.explain: चौथाई म्हणजे महसुली उत्पन्नाचा एक चतुर्थांश.

quiz.q: सर्वात मोठा पोर्तुगीज किल्ला कोणता?
quiz.explain: वसईचा किल्ला सर्वात मोठा पोर्तुगीज किल्ला होता.

quiz.q: बाजीरावाने कोणत्या वर्षी दिल्लीवर स्वारी केली?
quiz.explain: बाजीरावाने १७३७ मध्ये दिल्लीवर स्वारी केली.

quiz.q: महाराणी ताराबाईने कोणत्या युद्धात शाहू महाराजांना मदत केली?
quiz.explain: महाराणी ताराबाईने पन्हाळगडावर शाहू महाराजांना मदत केली.

quiz.q: बुंदेलखंड आजच्या कोणत्या राज्यात आहे?
quiz.explain: बुंदेलखंड आजच्या मध्यप्रदेशात आहे.

quiz.q: सिरदार बाजीरावाने कोणत्या सुभेदाराला पराभूत केले?
quiz.explain: सिरदार बाजीरावाने निजामाला पराभूत केले.

quiz.q: महाराजांच्या साहाय्याने दिल्ली दरबाराला कोणाची गरज होती?
quiz.explain: शाहू महाराजांना दिल्ली दरबाराला साहाय्याची गरज होती.

subject: History & Civics
notes: राष्ट्ररक्षक मराठे म्हणजे मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख शौर्यवान सरदार ज्यांनी भारताच्या उत्तर भागात मुघल व अफगाणांच्या आक्रमणांना तोंड दिले.
बाळाजी बाजीराव (पहिला) आणि नानासाहेब (दुसरा) हे प्रमुख पेशवे होते ज्यांनी मराठा वर्चस्व वाढवले.
नानासाहेबने १७५१ मध्ये पंजाबवर आक्रमण केले आणि १७५२ मध्ये अब्दालीशी करार केला.
अब्दाली (अहमद शाह अब्दाली) हा मुघल साम्राज्याचा बादशाह होता ज्याने मराठ्यांना पराभूत करण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.
पानिपतची लढाई १७६१ मध्ये झाली ज्यात मराठ्यांना पराभव झाला आणि पानिपतचा ताबा गमावला.
माधवराव पेशवा (१७५८-१७६०) यांनी मराठा वर्चस्व पुनर्स्थापित करण्याचा प्रयत्न केला.
सदाशिवरावभाऊने दिल्ली जिंकली परंतु नंतर पराभव झाला.
हैदरअली (इ.स.१७८२) आणि टिपू सुलतान (इ.स.१७९९) हे मराठा वर्चस्वावर प्रभाव टाकणारे प्रमुख शासक होते.
मराठा सैन्याने अफगाण व मुघल सैन्याशी लढाईत शौर्य दाखवले परंतु अनेकदा पराभव झाला.
पानिपतच्या लढाईनंतर मराठा वर्चस्व उत्तर भारतात कमी झाले परंतु पुणे दरबारात पुनः उभे राहिले.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख सरदार: शिंदे, होळकर, रामचंद्र कानडे, बिसाजीपंत, बिनिबाले इत्यादी.
मराठा साम्राज्याने १७५८ मध्ये ४००-६०० किमी विस्तार केला.
अफगाण व मुघल सैन्याने मराठा वर्चस्वाला आव्हान दिले.
मराठा वर्चस्वाचे संरक्षण करण्यासाठी मराठा सरदारांनी विविध मोहिमा केल्या.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख युद्ध: पानिपतची लढाई, बुराडी घाटची लढाई, राक्षसभुवनची लढाई इत्यादी.
मराठा साम्राज्याच्या इतिहासात पानिपतची लढाई एक महत्त्वपूर्ण वळण ठरली.
मराठा वर्चस्वाचे पुनर्स्थापन करण्यासाठी विविध सरदारांनी प्रयत्न केले.
मराठा साम्राज्याच्या इतिहासात पानिपतची लढाई व इतर लढाया महत्त्वपूर्ण आहेत.
मराठा साम्राज्याचे प्रमुख सरदार आणि त्यांच्या योगदानाची माहिती वाचकांना उपयुक्त ठरेल.

quiz.q: मराठ्यांचे पहिले प्रमुख पंतप्रधान कोण होते?
quiz.explain: नानासाहेब पेशवा हे मराठ्यांचे पहिले पंतप्रधान होते.

quiz.q: इ.स. १७५१ मध्ये कोणत्या प्रदेशावर अब्दालीने आक्रमण केले?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीने इ.स. १७५१ मध्ये पंजाबवर आक्रमण केले.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या तिसऱ्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव कोणत्या सैन्याने केला?
quiz.explain: पानिपतच्या तिसऱ्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव अब्दालीच्या सैन्याने केला.

quiz.q: सर्वात मोठा मराठा सरदार कोण होता?
quiz.explain: सदाशिवरावभाऊ हे सर्वात मोठे मराठा सरदार होते.

quiz.q: अब्दालीने मराठ्यांना कोणत्या प्रदेशात मदत करण्यास नकार दिला?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीने मराठ्यांना उत्तर भारतात मदत करण्यास नकार दिला.

quiz.q: इ.स. १७५८ मध्ये कोणत्या युद्धात दत्ताजीने शौर्य दाखवले?
quiz.explain: दत्ताजीने पानिपतच्या युद्धात शौर्य दाखवले.

quiz.q: माधवराव पेशव्यांनी कोणत्या सुधारणा केल्या?
quiz.explain: माधवराव पेशव्यांनी दारूगोळा कारखाने सुरू केले.

quiz.q: अब्दालीच्या मृत्यूची तारीख कोणती?
quiz.explain: अब्दालीचा मृत्यू इ.स. १७८२ मध्ये झाला.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव झाल्यानंतर कोणत्या शहरावर नियंत्रण मिळाले?
quiz.explain: पानिपतच्या लढाईत मराठ्यांचा पराभव झाल्यानंतर पानिपतवर नियंत्रण मिळाले.

quiz.q: इंग्रजी सैन्याने मराठ्यांशी कोणत्या वर्षी युद्ध केले?
quiz.explain: इंग्रजी सैन्याने मराठ्यांशी इ.स. १७९९ मध्ये युद्ध केले.

subject: History & Civics
notes: साम्राज्याची वाटचाल म्हणजे मराठा साम्राज्याचा इतिहास आणि त्याची वाढ-घट.
मराठा साम्राज्याची सुरुवात शिवाजी महाराजांनी केली आणि नंतर पानिपतच्या युद्धानंतर त्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.
इंदौरचे होळकर, नाना फडणवीस, ग्वालियरचे शिंदे, गायकवाड हे प्रमुख सरदार होते.
इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी मराठा सत्तेची पुनःस्थापना केली आणि दिल्लीच्या बादशाहाला गादीवर परत आणले.
नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिण भारतात मराठा सत्तेचा विस्तार केला.
ग्वालियरचे शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.
गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने मराठा-इंग्रज संघर्ष तीव्र झाला.
शिवाजी महाराजांनी आरमार उभारला ज्याने मराठा सत्तेला मदत केली.
इंग्रजांनी १८१७ मध्ये पुणे ताब्यात घेतल्यावर मराठा सत्तेचा अंत झाला.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनाचे मुख्य कारण म्हणजे आंतरिक वाद आणि इंग्रजांचा दबाव.
माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी उत्तर भारतात मराठा प्रतिष्ठा पुनःस्थापित केली.
पानिपतच्या युद्धात मराठा सैन्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.
साम्राज्याच्या विस्तारात शेतकरी, कर, व्यापार आणि तलाव-आढावा महत्त्वाचे होते.
माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी शेतकऱ्यांना विहिरी खोदून मदत केली.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतात ब्रिटिश राजवट स्थापन झाली.
मराठा सरदारांनी विविध प्रदेशात प्रशासन व लष्करी कार्य केले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या काळात गनिमी काव्याची पद्धत वापरली.
शिवाजी महाराजांनी आरमाराने समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले.
इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी धर्मस्थळांची सेवा केली.
नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिणेतील राजकारणाची सूत्रे सांभाळली.
ग्वालियरचे शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.
गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने संघर्ष तीव्र झाला.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर ब्रिटिशांनी भारतावर नियंत्रण घेतले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या इतिहासात विविध सरदारांनी योगदान दिले.
मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतीय समाजव्यवस्थेत बदल झाले.

quiz.q: इंदौरचे होळकर यांनी मराठा सत्तेची पुनःस्थापना कशात केली?
quiz.explain: होळकरांनी दिल्लीच्या बादशाहाला गादीवर परत आणले.

quiz.q: पानिपतच्या युद्धानंतर मराठा साम्राज्याची शक्ती कशी बदलली?
quiz.explain: युद्धानंतर मराठा सैन्याची शक्ती कमी झाली.

quiz.q: ग्वालियरचे शिंदे कोणत्या प्रदेशात मराठा प्रभाव वाढवले?
quiz.explain: शिंदे यांनी ओडिशा व बंगालमध्ये मराठा प्रभाव वाढवला.

quiz.q: मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनाचे मुख्य कारण काय होते?
quiz.explain: आंतरिक वाद आणि इंग्रजांचा दबाव.

quiz.q: शिवाजी महाराजांनी कोणती पद्धत वापरून समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले?
quiz.explain: आरमारने समुद्रावर नियंत्रण ठेवले.

quiz.q: नाना फडणवीस यांनी दक्षिण भारतात काय केले?
quiz.explain: दक्षिण भारतात मराठा सत्तेचा विस्तार केला.

quiz.q: गायकवाड यांनी इंग्रजांना काय न दिल्याने संघर्ष तीव्र झाला?
quiz.explain: धान्यसामग्री न दिल्याने संघर्ष वाढला.

quiz.q: इंग्रजांनी १८१७ मध्ये कोणते शहर ताब्यात घेतले?
quiz.explain: पुणे ताब्यात घेतले.

quiz.q: मराठा सत्तेच्या पतनानंतर भारतात कोणती राजवट स्थापन झाली?
quiz.explain: ब्रिटिश राजवट स्थापन झाली.

quiz.q: माल्हारराव होळकर यांनी शेतकऱ्यांना काय मदत केली?
quiz.explain: विहिरी खोदून मदत केली.

subject: History & Civics
notes: 1. महाराष्ट्रातील समाजजीवन हे प्रामुख्याने ग्रामीण व शहरी भागात विभागलेले आहे.
2. गावात बहुतेक लोक स्वयंपूर्ण असत – शेती, पशुपालन व हस्तकला.
3. प्रमुख धान्ये: ज्वारी, बाजरी, गहू, तांदूळ, मका.
4. शेतकरी व गावकरी यांच्याकडे पाट, पाटलाकडे, पाटिलकी यांसारखी साधने होती.
5. गावातील घरांची रचना: एकमजली व दुमजली वाडे, साधी माती-गोट्यांची भिंती.
6. पोशाख: पुरुष लुगडी व चोळी, स्त्रिया अंगरखा व मुंडासे.
7. सण-उत्सव: गुढीपाडवा, नागपंचमी, बैलपोळा, दिवाळी, होळी, ईद, गणेशोत्सव.
8. बालविवाह व बहुपत्नित्व या काळात प्रचलित अनिष्ट चालीरिती होत्या.
9. शिक्षण: पाठशाळा व मदरसा, लेखन व वाचन शिकवले जात.
10. दानधर्म व धार्मिक अनुष्ठाने समाजात महत्त्वाची भूमिका बजावतात.
11. दळणवळण: घाटमार्ग, सडक व नद्यांवरील पूल, होड्या.
12. खेळ: कुस्ती, लाठी, दंडपट्टा, बुद्धिबळ, खोखो, आट्यापाट्या.
13. महिलांचे जीवन: पाठीवरून वाहून नेणे, होड्यांवर प्रवास, शिक्षणाची कमी.
14. महाराष्ट्रातील धार्मिक विविधता: हिंदू व मुस्लिम दोन्ही प्रमुख धर्म.
15. शिल्पकला व वास्तुकला: पाटलाकडे, गंगाराम, नाशिकचे मंदिर, पाटलाकडे वाडे.
16. समाजातील समता व लोकशाहीचे महत्त्व २०व्या शतकात वाढले.
17. संविधानाची ओळख व मूलभूत हक्कांची माहिती महत्त्वाची.
18. समाजात समतेची गरज व लिंगभेदावर चर्चा आवश्यक.
19. स्थानिक शासन व राज्यशासन यांतील फरक समजणे आवश्यक.
20. संविधानातील मार्गदर्शक तत्त्वे व मूलभूत कर्तव्ये यांचा अभ्यास करणे.

quiz.q: महाराष्ट्रातील प्रमुख धान्ये कोणती आहेत?
quiz.explain: गावात ज्वारी, बाजरी, गहू व तांदूळ हे प्रमुख धान्ये आहेत.

subject: History & Civics
notes: संविधान म्हणजे राज्यकारभाराचे नियम स्पष्ट करणारा महत्त्वाचा दस्तऐवज.
भारतीय संविधानाची उद्देशिका 'आम्ही, भारताचे लोक...' पासून सुरू होते.
उद्देशिकेत सार्वभौम, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकशाही गणराज्य гэती मूल्ये ओळखली जातात.
सार्वभौमत्वाचा अर्थ: देशातील सर्व निर्णय घेण्याची शक्ती भारतीय लोकांना असते.
समाजवादी राज्य: संपत्तीचा वितरण समान करणे, गरीब-श्रीमंत यांच्यात मोठी दरी नसावी.
धर्मनिरपेक्ष राज्य: सर्व धर्मांना समान मानणे, राज्याचा कोणती धर्म नाही.
लोकशाही राज्य: सत्ता लोकांच्या हातांमध्ये, निवडणुका द्रष्ट्या सरकार निर्माण होते.
गणराज्य: राज्याचा प्रमुख निवडलेलाpresidente, वंशपरंपरा नाही.
न्याय: सामाजिक, आर्थिक, राजकीय तीन प्रकारचे, सर्वांना समान अवसर.
स्वातंत्र्य: विचार, अभिव्यक्ती, धर्म, सण-उत्सव साजरे करण्याचे हक्क.
समता: जात, धर्म, लिंग, जन्मस्थान आधारित भेदभाव न करणे, सर्वांचा दर्जा समान.
बंधुभाव: परस्पर सहानुभूती, आत्मीयता, एकता व शांतीचे भाव.
संविधान सभा: डॉ. राजेंद्रप्रसाद यांची अध्यक्षता, डॉ. बाबासाहेब आंबेडकर यांची समिती प्रमुखता.
संविधान दिन: 26 जानेवारी, 1950 रोजी भारतीय संविधान लागू झाला.
प्रौढ मतदान पद्धती: 18 वर्षे पूर्ण झालेल्या सर्व नागरिकांना मताधिकार.

quiz.explain: भारतीय संविधानाची उद्देशिका इंग्रजी मध्ये लिहिली आहे, पण त्याचा मराठी अनुवादही उपलब्ध आहे.

quiz.explain: उद्देशिकेत सार्वभौम, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकशाही गणराज्य гэती मूल्ये ओळखली जातात, राज्यवादी नाही.

subject: History & Civics
notes: संविधान हे भारताचे सर्वोच्च कायदा आहे.
संविधानात तीन सूची आहेत – संघसूची, राज्यसूची आणि समवर्ती सूची.
संघसूचीतील विषय – संरक्षण, परराष्ट्र व्यवहार, चलन, राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा इत्यादी.
राज्यसूचीतील विषय – शेती, शिक्षण, आरोग्य, पाणीपुरवठा इत्यादी.
समवर्ती सूचीतील विषय – कर, दंड, वैवाहिक कायदा इत्यादी, दोन्ही सरकारे कायदे करू शकतात.
संघराज्य व्यवस्था म्हणजे दोन स्तरांवरील सरकार – केंद्र आणि राज्य.
शेषाधिकार म्हणजे केंद्र सरकारकडे असलेले अधिकार जे राज्य सरकारकडे नाहीत.
संविधानात स्वतंत्र न्यायव्यवस्था आहे – न्यायालयांना राजकीय दबावापासून मुक्त ठेवले आहे.
निवडणूक आयोग हे स्वतंत्र संस्था आहे, ज्याने सर्व महत्त्वाच्या निवडणुका घेतल्या जातात.
संविधान बदलण्यासाठी संसद आणि राज्यसभेची मंजुरी व राष्ट्रपतींची स्वाक्षरी आवश्यक आहे.
संविधानात नागरिकांना समान हक्क व स्वातंत्र्य दिले आहे – धर्मनिरपेक्षता, समाजवाद, लोकशाही, गणराज्य.
संविधानात विविध अधिकारांचे वाटप करून संघराज्य व्यवस्था साकारली आहे.
संविधानात नागरिकांना मतदानाचा अधिकार व निवडणुकीत भाग घेण्याचे अधिकार दिले आहेत.
